The Blu-Ray release of the film furthers this by adding more polish to the movie's more sloppy or stiff scenes that have no interference with the story, and thus make the visuals come across as more realistic, pleasant, and dynamic.

tropes.name: Epic Fail
tropes.html:
Simba's attempts to pin Nala during their argument as cubs. He pounces on her with a roar expecting to easily pin her and win their argument, only to end up being flipped, slammed down, and pinned himself, all with a shocked look on his face and Nala teasing him. When she turns away from him and is distracted he pounces on her again to get revenge, only to accidentally send them both tumbling down a hill. Nala laughs the whole way down, enjoying herself, while Simba is seen shocked by this accident and struggles to stay on top of Nala, only to end up getting flipped and pinned again for his efforts, and Nala smugly rubbing her victory in his face.
Nala: Pinned ya again.

tropes.name: Epic Movie
tropes.html: Disney's most well-known example from their traditionally animated films. It blends a Coming of Age Story with a rich assortment of literary inspirations (such as The Epic of Sundiata and Shakespeare's works, most noticeably Hamlet) presenting what is regarded as the peak of Disney Renaissance (which is already considered the peak of Disney's animation history itself). Combine its vast scale to an all-star cast, majestic scenes like the opening sequence and the stampede, gorgeous animation and a monumental soundtrack: that's an epic movie.

tropes.name: Equal-Opportunity Evil
tropes.html: Downplayed. Scar looks down upon the hyenas, but will work with them if it suits his goals.

tropes.name: Establishing Character Moment
tropes.html: Mufasa is introduced standing stoically atop Pride Rock on the day of his son's presentation, bearing a grim scowl on his face, but as soon as Zazu presents himself, Mufasa gives him a smile, and then he greets Rafiki with a warm hug. He's an imposing and strong king, but he's also a benevolent and personable figure, as well.

tropes.name: Et Tu, Brute?
tropes.html: As Mufasa hangs on for his life above the stampeding wildebeests, he begs his brother for help only to painfully discover that Scar is relishing the opportunity to ensure his brother's death.

tropes.name: Euphemism Buster
tropes.html:
Scar has to backtrack and Euphemism Bust himself thanks to dumb hyenas:
Banzai: Yeah, be prepared! We'll be prepared! For what?
Scar: For the death of the king!
Banzai: What, is he sick?
Scar: No, you fool, we're going to kill him. And Simba, too.

tropes.name: Evil Is Burning Hot
tropes.html:
• Fires set the stage for Simba's final battle with Scar.
  • Also, for some reason there's unexplained volcanic activity right during "Be Prepared".

tropes.name: Evil Laugh
tropes.html:
• Ed often bursts into laughter, though that's because he's The Hyena (literally and figuratively).
  • Scar lets one out, followed by all the hyenas, at the end of "Be Prepared".

tropes.name: Evil Will Fail
tropes.html: Even if Simba hadn't shown up and pulled a Rightful King Returns, Scar's rule over the lion pride would have collapsed anyway since he'd driven The Pridelands to the point of ecological ruin.

tropes.name: Excrement Statement
tropes.html: Visually referenced during a scene from the song "I Just Can't Wait to Be King" when a herd of zebras turn their butts toward Zazu and raise their tails up, causing him to flinch and lift up his wings protectively.

tropes.name: Exact Words
tropes.html:
Exploited by Scar during the climax. After he guilt-trips Simba into admitting that he was "responsible for Mufasa's death" — which the latter still believes was a tragic accident — Scar twists this confession to brand Simba as a murderer. Through the ensuing "trial", Scar then continues to bait Simba with intentionally vague questions to further incriminate him, preventing Simba from explaining what (he believes) really happened.
Scar: If it weren't for you, Mufasa would still be alive, it's your fault he's dead. Do you deny it?
Simba: No.
Scar: Then, you're guilty!

tropes.name: Exit, Pursued by a Bear
tropes.html: Scar finds his end by the hyenas. Particularly chilling, since most other examples of this trope treats the animal as the vessel for karma, or just a force of nature. But the hyenas that eat Scar were goofy, well-characterized villains like all the other characters earlier in the film, making his death more of a murder than an animal-related fatality. Also, rather than him simply being chased off screen by the hyenas, we instead get to explicitly witness the pack brutally mauling him to death by the shadows cast by the fire on the wall of Pride Rock.

tropes.name: Face Death with Despair
tropes.html: In his last moments, Scar calls the hyenas his "friends" as he hadn't tossed all the blame on them shortly before and they didn't hear him. The hyenas, of course, won't buy that and jump over Scar as he cowers, begs, and tries to make excuses for his betrayal. However, the shadows show that he does at least go down fighting.

tropes.name: Facepalm
tropes.html: Scar massages his forehead softly as he utters, "I'm Surrounded by Idiots."

tropes.name: Failed a Spot Check
tropes.html: Simba and Nala don't realize that they have literally wrestled right into the Elephant Graveyard until a steam geyser goes off right next to them.

tropes.name: Fall Guy
tropes.html: Simba is this to Scar. Scar and the hyenas were the ones responsible for starting the stampede and Scar himself is the one who kills Mufasa, but Simba didn't see any of that, and since he thinks his roaring startled the wildebeests into stampeding, Scar decides to use his ignorance, blames him for killing Mufasa, and orders him to run away and never return. This causes Simba to believe he killed his own father and this lasts until Scar accidentally tells him the truth during the final battle.

tropes.name: Falling-in-Love Montage
tropes.html: The song "Can You Feel the Love Tonight?" shows Simba and Nala falling in love as they spend time together for the first time since growing up. Worth mentioning is that at one point this was going to be somewhat of a deconstruction, as the song was going to be sung sarcastically by Timon and Pumbaa, who were just disgusted at all this "mushy stuff" going on. The only bit of that which survived the final revisions is the ending of the song.

tropes.name: Family of Choice
tropes.html: Timon and Pumbaa follow Nala when Simba returns to Pride Rock. They say that even if it's dangerous, they'll face hyenas and Scar for Simba who acknowledges their dedication and makes them part of the pride.

tropes.name: Family-Unfriendly Death
tropes.html:
• Mufasa's death while his son watches, and Simba's repeated pleas for him to "wake up, Dad" while desperately nudging his corpse.
  • The fight between Simba and Scar ends with Scar being eaten alive (or at the very least being mauled to death) by his hyena henchmen (cast in shadow, but still!). The sequel makes it even worse by implying that he might have been burned to death as well.

tropes.name: Family-Unfriendly Violence
tropes.html: Not only is there the Family-Unfriendly Death of Mufasa early on in the movie, but the scene where Scar smacks Sarabi so hard she goes flying, and the fight scene towards the end, with the hyenas presumably killing and ripping apart Scar offscreen.

tropes.name: Fartillery
tropes.html: Pumbaa's backstory establishes that he... well, smells... and is why he was cast out of warthog society. Demonstrated during "Hakuna Matata," where he clears the waterhole quicker than you could say "safari."

tropes.name: Fascinating Eyebrow
tropes.html: Nala's response to Simba pulling her into the oasis, after overcoming her initial shock from it, is to raise an eyebrow and smirk at Simba in amusement at both his prank on her and his ridiculous appearance with his wet mane covering his face and giving her a goofy smile. This is immediately followed by her playfully pushing him back into the water as revenge and running off for him to chase her.

tropes.name: Fear-Induced Idiocy
tropes.html: When cornered by Simba on the summit of Pride Rock, a terrified Scar begs for mercy and lies that his own hyena allies were responsible for him causing Mufasa's death. However, said hyenas had come to help him against Simba just to overhear him betraying them, and they become extremely enraged.

tropes.name: Fictional Traditions
tropes.html: When Simba is born, he has fruit pulp rubbed on his head and is held up and presented to the denizens of the Pride Lands. They do it again when when his daughter Kiara is born, thus showing it is traditional to do this every time the current Lion King has a cub.

tropes.name: Fighting Fingerprint
tropes.html: Nala's Signature Move of pinning her opponents to the ground, which she most commonly used against Simba, is what allows Simba to realize that the lioness he's fighting as an adult is actually Nala herself, after she pulls the maneuver on him again and he recognizes it from when the times she did it to him as cubs.

tropes.name: Fighting Your Friend
tropes.html: An accidental version happens between Simba and Nala. When Nala tries to hunt Timon and Pumbaa, Simba ends up fighting her to protect them, but neither of them realises that they are fighting their old friend at first because it has been years since they last saw each other. As soon as Simba realises he is fighting Nala when she beats him using the same move to flip and pin him when they were cubs, they immediately stop and happily reunite.

tropes.name: Final Battle
tropes.html: The rightful king Simba and his allies, against Scar and his army of hyenas, warring amongst the flames of a burning Pride Rock, to decide the fate of their kingdom and lands.

tropes.name: Fire/Water Juxtaposition
tropes.html: The climactic fight scene has a lightning strike starting a brush fire in the Pridelands as Simba returns to Pride Rock and challenges Scar for leadership of the pride. After Scar's defeat, a rainstorm quenches the fire and symbolically washes away the traces of Scar's destructive regime.

tropes.name: Firmament
tropes.html: Timon apparently believes that the sky — "that big bluish-black thing" — is a physical structure, and the stars are fireflies that became stuck in it.

tropes.name: Fisher King
tropes.html: When Mufasa is in charge, his wise leadership makes the land around Pride Rock a beautiful place of peace and plenty. When Scar is the king, the same land turns into a dark and dying graveyard due to his poor leadership and the hyenas eating and taking almost everything there is, reflecting his own dark personality. Once Simba assumes the throne, everything goes pretty again.

tropes.name: Fixing the Resource Scarcity
tropes.html: Defied by Scar. After the Time Skip following the Big Bad's usurpation of the throne in Pride Rock, it is shown that there are barely any preys left for the lionesses to hunt and thus feed themselves and the hyenas with, and Pride Lands as a whole became a dry, precarious wasteland. At first, only the leading hyena trio files this complaint in front of Scar, who simply says it's up to the lionesses to find food. But shortly before the movie's climax, Sarabi files the same complaint to him on behalf of the entire kingdom, and suggests to him the idea of moving elsewhere. Scar stubbornly refuses, even accusing her and the lionesses of not trying hard enough to find food. The situation only improves after Scar gets killed and Simba is sworn king as always intended.

tropes.name: Flat Joy
tropes.html:
Scar does the sarcastic version.
Simba: Hey, Uncle Scar, guess what.
Scar: I despise guessing games.
Simba: I'm gonna be king of Pride Rock.
Scar: (deadpan) Oh, goody.

tropes.name: Floating Head Syndrome
tropes.html: The cineplex posters mostly consist of Mufasa's face floating over Pride Rock. This is a unique case of it pertaining to the events of the story.

tropes.name: Foe-Tossing Charge
tropes.html:
• Pumbaa vs. the hyenas in the Battle of Pride Rock.
  • Pumbaa's charge into the flock of vultures when he and Timon first meet Simba.

tropes.name: Forbidden Fruit
tropes.html: The elephant graveyard and anything beyond the borders of the Pride Lands, despite not being an ideal place.

tropes.name: Forced Starvation
tropes.html: After Scar becomes the king of the Pride Lands, he allows the hyenas to eat as much as they want, which results in there being no food left. Scar blames the lionesses by claiming they're not looking hard enough to find food, and when Sarabi suggests that they move somewhere else to survive, Scar insists on staying to avoid having to admit his incompetence as a king, even after Sarabi points out that this will doom everyone to starvation, insisting that as king, he can do whatever he wants. Thankfully, Simba shows up and overthrows Scar before anyone ends up starving.

tropes.name: Foreboding Fleeing Flock
tropes.html: Invoked when Scar has the hyenas cause a wildebeest stampede as a trap for both Simba and Mufasa.

tropes.name: Foreshadowing
tropes.html:
• A subtle one but, at the beginning, Zazu tells Scar "Didn't your mother ever tell you not to play with your food?", something an adult would tell a child rather than a fellow adult. This implies Zazu knows how childish Scar can really be underneath his charming facade, which is shown once he takes power.
    • Moreover, "playing with his food" ends up being what leads to Scar's downfall, first in letting Simba live with the torment of thinking he caused his own father's death, then admitting that it was himself who killed Mufasa when it seems he has Simba pinned, leading to Simba getting a Heroic Second Wind, pinning him instead, and forcing him to confess to everyone else.
  • Mufasa in general seems to have a gift of providing these.
    • "There's more to being King than getting your way all the time." Considering the disaster that arose under Scar's rule when he took the helm, from the lack of food to the ire of his own subjects, Mufasa was onto something there.
    • "A king's time as ruler rises and falls like the sun. One day, Simba, the sun will set on my time here and will rise with you as the new king." Mufasa's reign ends at sundown following his death, and the sun rises as Simba ascends as the new king. As a bonus, every time we see the Pride Lands following Mufasa's death, the sun is obscured by dark gray or brown clouds even in daylight, meaning it quite literally doesn't visibly ascend until Simba takes the helm.
  • In "Be Prepared", the hyenas dance around when chanting "No king, no king..." when Scar has to remind them that he will be the new king and as long as he's in charge, the hyenas won't be hungry. Sure enough, the hyenas don't hesitate brutally "removing" him from power once he sells them out, by eating him instead.

tropes.name: Forgiveness
tropes.html: Despite initially chewing out Simba for his reckless decision to go to the graveyard — neither lion knows of Scar's involvement — Mufasa forgives him on seeing that Simba really is sorry and was doing it out of a misguided attempt to prove to his father that he was brave.

tropes.name: Fourth-Date Marriage
tropes.html: This is played with between Simba and Nala. They were both childhood best friends, and Zazu revealed to them that they are betrothed to be married. They are both disgusted by this idea though, since they find the idea of marrying their best friend too weird. Years later, they reunite as adults after Nala previously believed Simba was dead, and they instantly fall in love with each other. Simba takes Nala on a tour of the jungle, with it essentially being their "first date" together, where they have a Falling-in-Love Montage of playing around and flirting together and ends with it being heavily implied they have G-Rated Sex together. By the time Simba defeats Scar and becomes king, he and Nala are now properly married, which was originally planned for them.

tropes.name: Frame-Up
tropes.html: After Scar kills Mufasa, he gets Simba to believe he's responsible, leading to Simba's running away. Simba believes this until the Just Between You and Me moment in the final act, even to the point of confessing himself to his mother and the rest of the pride.

tropes.name: Freeze-Frame Bonus
tropes.html:
• When Simba first pounces on Nala and she uses her famous flip and pin trick on him, it is blocked from view slightly due to some plants in the foreground obscuring its view, making it difficult for viewers to fully understand what just happened the first time. It also briefly blocks Simba's face from view, where pausing shows his face change from confidence to confusion and shock as Nala flips him over and slams him down.
  • When Timon reaches his arm into a log during the Hakuna Matata number, a red beetle with a hidden Mickey Mouse symbol on its back can briefly be seen escaping along with the dozens of other bugs.
  • At the end of the Hakuna Matata number, when Simba shakes his mane dry, as it unfurls to fluff out, a single frame shows his mane completely spiked out and standing on end.
  • As Simba slumps at the edge of the cliff, the dust clouds spell out “SFX”. Most people thought it read “SEX”, however, so this bonus was removed from the Platinum edition DVD, Diamond Edition Blu-ray, and assumedly all subsequent releases of the film.

tropes.name: Full-Boar Action
tropes.html: Zigzagged by Pumbaa the warthog. Except when you hit his Berserk Button (calling him a "pig"), he's really only dangerous after dinner (Pumbaa with his Berserk Button pressed is an example of this trope, as Shenzi and Banzai found out the hard way).

tropes.name: Full Moon Silhouette
tropes.html: During the Age Cut, Simba and his two new-found friends walk across a tree trunk with a Gigantic Moon in the background.

tropes.name: Funny Afro
tropes.html: At the end of the song Hakuna Matata, Simba’s mane briefly poofs into a giant sphere almost as big as his entire body (as a result of shaking it dry) before falling back to normal.

tropes.name: Funny Background Event
tropes.html:
• Timon and Pumbaa swing on a vine in the background when Simba first starts singing in "Hakuna Matata". Pumbaa does this at the beginning of the theme song in the TV series.
  • During "Be Prepared", Scar scares Shenzi and Banzi onto geysers, which blast them up off the top of the screen. As Scar keeps singing, the two hyenas plummet down half a verse later in the background. In the sing-a-long version, some of the text is also blasted off-screen with the hyenas and comes plummeting back down with them as well.

tropes.name: Furry Reminder
tropes.html: While the lions mainly talk and treat their problems like a person would, there are several times they start growling or roaring especially when they fight or threaten someonenote Or, in Simba's case, when he's marking Pride Rock as his territory and the other lions join in. Plus, like real animals, they eat the other animals in The Pridelands and constantly talk about doing sonote Not to mention the lions live in prides like real lions do. Also, when Nala is hunting Pumbaa, she is portrayed completely as a wild animal chasing after her prey while Pumbaa's reactions are more anthropomorphized.

tropes.name: Gag Echo
tropes.html:
Simba: When I'm king, what does that make you?
Scar: A monkey's uncle.
...
Nala: No, no, no, it's his uncle.
Timon: The monkey's his uncle?

tropes.name: Game Face
tropes.html: The lions in the cast look significantly scarier when in combat. Nala in particular is almost unrecognizable when Simba first meets her, and they all show More Teeth than the Osmond Family when their fangs are bared.

tropes.name: Gaslighting
tropes.html: Scar manages to manipulate Simba into believing that he is responsible for Mufasa's death when in truth, he did it.

tropes.name: Generational Saga
tropes.html: Mufasa tells Simba that even when he's gone he'll always be there in the sky with the great kings to look down on his son. Once he is gone, Simba abandons the Pride Lands to his uncle Scar, but after talking to his father in the sky he realizes that he needs to come home and be king.

tropes.name: The Genie Knows Jack Nicholson
tropes.html: Not a time variant, but location; the characters are all animals of the African savanna who have no known interactions with humans. Yet, the hyenas make puns based on human entrées, and Timon, Pumbaa, and Zazu all sing our songs.

tropes.name: Get Out!
tropes.html:
• Scar tells Simba to "Run away and never return", convincing Simba that he's responsible for Mufasa's death. When a grown-up Simba eventually comes back to Pride Rock and learns that Scar himself is the real murderer, Simba utters these words back at Scar.
  • Scar does it to the hyenas during the complaint that there’s no food.
    Scar: Good. Now get out.
    Banzai: Yeah, but we’re still hungry
    Scar: OUT!

tropes.name: Getting Crap Past the Radar
tropes.html:
Pumbaa very nearly gets away with singing a "naughty" word for his flatulence that wouldn't fly for a 1994 Disney movie, which Timon stops and lampshades (although the MPAA were lenient enough to let Disney imply it, keeping the film "G" instead of raising it to a "PG" for crude humor):
Puumba: And I got downhearted...
Timon: How'd you feel?
Pumbaa: Every time that I --
Timon: Pumbaa! Not in front of the kid!
Pumbaa: Oh... Sorry.

tropes.name: Ghost Reunion Ending
tropes.html: Shortly after saving the Pride Lands and taking his place on Pride Rock, Simba hears Mufasa's ghost saying "Remember" to him, just before he performs his victory roar.

tropes.name: Gilligan Cut
tropes.html: When Timon is offered as live bait, he sarcastically asks if they want him to dress in drag and do the hula. In the next scene, he does exactly that.

tropes.name: Glad I Thought of It
tropes.html:
• Simba calls himself a genius after he and Nala escape Zazu, and Nala points out it was her idea they used. Simba simply says he's the one who pulled it off, but Nala once again claims he did it with her.
  • Pumbaa suggests that they should adopt Simba since "When he grows up, maybe he'll be on our side." Timon first dismisses the idea as stupid but then presents it as his own.

tropes.name: Go Back to the Source
tropes.html: Simba returns to his home of Pride Rock in order to dethrone Scar and claim his place as king.

tropes.name: Good Animals, Evil Animals
tropes.html: The lions and hyenas. With the exception of Scar, the lions are always portrayed as noble and honourable while the hyenas are portrayed as scummy and subservient to Scar. However, Timon & Pumbaa implies that Shenzi, Banzai, and Ed settle for neutrality following the movie, and The Lion Guard introduces Jasiri's clan, who claim that Shenzi's clan is the exception rather than the rule when it comes to hyenas.

tropes.name: Gory Discretion Shot
tropes.html: The camera pans upward just in time for the audience to miss seeing the villain, Scar, get ripped apart by hyenas, only seeing part of it in shadow.

tropes.name: Graceful Loser
tropes.html: Downplayed. During "Can You Feel The Love Tonight" Simba finally manages to pin Nala when they tumble down a hill and he lands on top of her. She rewards him for "beating her" with a lick on the cheek and a seductive look.

tropes.name: G-Rated Sex
tropes.html: At the end of "Can You Feel The Love Tonight", Nala gives a suggestive look toward Simba and it's implied that they do it offscreen (which would explain why they have a cub of their own at the very end of the film). It's all the more obvious in the original, pre-production version, where there's very little room for doubt about what happens. The intent was confirmed by Disney itself; from the DVD audio commentary narrated by directors Roger Allers and Rob Minkoff and producer Don Hahn,

tropes.name: Gratuitous Latin
tropes.html: Scar uses the phrase "quid pro quo" during his big Villain Song.

tropes.name: Greater-Scope Paragon
tropes.html: The Kings of the Past are said to have been the spirits of lions who have once ruled the Pridelands long ago, and have been turned into stars in the night sky, as well as the Sun during the day, upon death. After Mufasa is killed by Scar, he too becomes a spirit who persuades Simba to return to Pride Rock to challenge Scar and reclaim his rightful place as king.

tropes.name: Green Gators
tropes.html: The crocodiles in "I Just Can't Wait to Be King" in the 2002 special edition of the movie are green. Averted in the theatrical version and in ‘’The Lion King II: Simba's Pride’’, however, with the crocodiles being depicted as gray.

tropes.name: Grin of Audacity
tropes.html: There's a scene where Simba boasts "I walk on the wild side... I laugh in the face of danger ha ha ha ha!" upon arriving the Elephant Graveyard. Nala repeats the phrase right before the big battle at the end.

tropes.name: Gut Punch
tropes.html: Starts off as a fairly lighthearted Disney film about a young African lion cub and his life in the Serengeti, albeit with a truly sinister villain. However, things get incredibly dark and depressing when King Mufasa is killed by his evil brother Scar, who convinces Simba to blame himself for it, tries to have him killed, and then takes over Pride Rock and turns it into a tyrannical nightmare that Simba has to end.

tropes.name: Hair Flip
tropes.html:
• Scar's mane flips rather seductively during "Be Prepared".
  • At the end of "Hakuna Matata", after his mane bursts into a frizzy halo, Simba swoops his head down and back up as the mane falls back away from his muzzle.

tropes.name: Hair Reboot
tropes.html: An amusing double subversion at the end of "Hakuna Matata". After Simba splashes into a swimming hole, he climbs out with his mane sopping wet and disheveled with his bangs flattened over his eyes. He shakes it dry in robust fashion… which results in it briefly fluffing up into a giant mass of red frizz… before it cascades back to its normal, finely coiffed style.

tropes.name: Hakuna Matata
tropes.html: This trope is referred to by name when Timon and Pumbaa tell Simba, who has just run away from his responsibilities and his life, that he doesn't need to worry about the past, because a carefree existence is much less trouble. Deconstructed: This mentality ends up becoming an obstacle Simba must throw off before he can start serving the kingdom and rescue it from Scar, who never outgrows this attitude and tries to take the benefits of being king without taking any of the responsibility that goes along with the job. When both Simba and Scar shun this responsibility, the kingdom suffers greatly from Scar's neglectful approach. It's only when Simba grows and learns to take responsibility that prosperity returns. In fact, the song shows him being apathetically cynical. "Bad things happen and there's nothing you can do about it. So why worry?"

tropes.name: Hammy Villain, Serious Hero
tropes.html: Mufasa and his evil brother Scar. Mufasa is a stern and dignified (although not humorless) ruler, whereas Scar is hammy and snarky. This is less pronounced at first with the hero Simba, who initially is a carefree child, but then gets put through tragedy that he spends much of the film guilt-ridden and depressed over, and is dead serious when he finally confronts Scar about it.

tropes.name: A Handful for an Eye
tropes.html: Right before their fight, Scar blinds Simba by kicking hot coals into his face.

tropes.name: Hand Stomp
tropes.html:
• Scar claws Mufasa's paws while the latter is hanging from a cliff.
  • He also does it to Simba during the Final Battle, but Simba gets the strength to lunge back after the "I killed Mufasa" revelation.

tropes.name: Hanging by the Fingers
tropes.html:
• Scar sets a trap for Simba and Mufasa, luring Simba into a gorge and having the hyenas drive a large herd of wildebeest into a stampede to trample him. Mufasa saves Simba but winds up hanging perilously from the gorge's edge; he begs for Scar's help, but Scar throws Mufasa back into the stampede to his death.
  • Simba spares Scar's life but, quoting what Scar told him long ago, orders Scar to leave The Pridelands forever. Scar refuses and attacks his nephew, but after a brief battle, Simba throws him off the ledge to the ground below: with Scar clinging briefly to the ledge before falling.

tropes.name: Happily Married
tropes.html:
• Mufasa and Sarabi are clearly this.
  • After having gotten the Pride Lands back from Scar, Simba and Nala marry and become the rightful rulers. The movie ends with Rafiki presenting their newborn daughter to the rest of the kingdom.

tropes.name: Happy Rain
tropes.html: At the end of the movie, after Simba defeats Scar, the rains return and put out the fire engulfing Pride Rock. The final scene depicts Simba warmly reuniting with his family and friends, and taking the throne at last.

tropes.name: Harmful to Minors
tropes.html: Simba watches his father die right in front of him by falling off a cliff and trampled by wildebeests while convinced it was his fault that he died right up until the end.

tropes.name: Hates Baths
tropes.html: Simba doesn't like when his mom gives him one.

tropes.name: Headbutt of Love
tropes.html:
• Sarabi and Mufasa (lion king and queen) bump their heads at the beginning of the film when their cub Simba is being presented.
  • Simba and Nala headbutt lovingly during their reunion.
  • Simba and his mother Sarabi greet each other with this gesture when they meet after being separated.

tropes.name: Held Gaze
tropes.html: Simba and Nala gaze deeply into each other's eyes at the end of their Falling-in-Love Montage of "Can You Feel the Love Tonight?" before nuzzling each other in a manner that resembles a kiss.

tropes.name: "Hell, Yes!" Moment
tropes.html: Rafiki cheers and excitedly yells to the sky when Simba makes the decision to return to the Pride Lands.

tropes.name: Heroes' Frontier Step
tropes.html:
Being inspired by Hamlet, Simba lost his father to his evil uncle. But unlike Hamlet, Simba doesn't have a dilemma. He makes his choice right away, despite the anger he feels.
Scar: What are you going to do? You wouldn't kill your own uncle...?
Simba: No, Scar. I'm not like you.

tropes.name: Heroic Rematch
tropes.html:
Played with between Simba and Nala.
  • Despite both of them being best friends, the two of them also seemed to have a slight rivalry with each other as cubs due to their Bratty Half-Pint nature. When one of their arguments escalates into the two of them playfully fighting over it, Nala easily flips and pins Simba with little effort twice while laughing at him.
  • The two of them end up fighting again much more seriously years later as adults, and though Simba does much better against her, holding his own despite her having more experience, it being his first real fight of his life, and managing to briefly startle her and hold her down for a moment, it ends up subverted when Simba still ultimately loses to Nala again against the same flip and pin move she used to beat him as cubs.
  • This is later played straight but downplayed between them. During their Falling-in-Love Montage while teasing each other, Simba chases Nala into the jungle and the two begin to playfully wrestle with each other again, resulting in them accidentally tumbling down a hill together. Simba ends up landing on top of Nala, finally pinning her. Despite this being a complete accident, it is still Simba's only win against Nala, and Nala herself seems to acknowledge it as a win for him, acting as a Graceful Loser and giving him an affectionate lick on the cheek as a reward for finally "beating" her.

tropes.name: Heroic Second Wind
tropes.html: When Scar has Simba right where he wants him (desperately trying to keep his grip on the ledge of Pride Rock but about to fall off), and he admits that he killed Mufasa (in what he thinks will be a Just Between You and Me moment, before throwing Simba to his death) ... Simba (who relives watching his father being thrown to his death in what could well be his final moments) instead lunges up the rest of the cliff, pinning his evil uncle and forcing him to reveal the truth to the others.

tropes.name: He's a Friend
tropes.html:
Timon and Pumbaa are being chased by a lioness when Simba shows up to rescue them. But when Simba recognizes her as his best friend Nala, he introduces them to each other and dinner is cancelled.
Timon: Let me get this straight. You know her, she knows you, but she wants to eat him. And... everybody's okay with this? DID I MISS SOMETHING?!

tropes.name: Hidden Depths
tropes.html: One of the darkest examples in a children's movie happens when Ed, the dumb non-verbal hyena, instantly understands that Scar has lost all his power and moves on to eat him.

tropes.name: High-Altitude Homicide
tropes.html: Scar drops Mufasa off a cliff before convincing Mufasa's heir Simba of the latter's own guilt. Scar later attempts to murder a now-adult Simba by suspending him over a cliff. He then confesses that he was the one who threw Mufasa to his death, but this gives Simba the motivation to jump back up and beat the ever-loving crap out of him.

tropes.name: History Repeats
tropes.html:
• Simba being pinned by the exact same flip move by Nala. After she did it to him twice as cubs, he recognizes her as an adult when she uses this move to beat him again, with the flipping and slamming motions being the same.
  • When they were cubs, Simba and Nala accidentally roll down a steep hill together while playfighting, resulting in Nala pinning Simba. Years later, the two playfight again as adults in the jungle, and once again accidentally roll down a hill together. This time though, Simba ends up pinning Nala, and the two fall in love.
  • This is lampshaded by Scar, as he prepares to throw Simba off of Pride Rock into the fire below, he realizes this is the same position his father was in right before he died and sinks his claws into Simba's paws the same way he did to Mufasa as he prepares to kill him the same way. Subverted though as Simba gains the Heroic Second Wind to stop this when Scar whispers what he did to him.

tropes.name: Hoist by His Own Petard
tropes.html: Scar spends his relationship with the hyenas lying and constantly breaking promises about bringing food to them, and their impatience and irritation boil over when Scar tries to pin the blame for Mufasa's death on them. He ends up getting eaten by his own hyenas in a well-deserved Family-Unfriendly Death.

tropes.name: Hollywood Healing
tropes.html:
• During the Elephant Graveyard chase, Simba uses his claws to scratch Shenzi on the cheek when she almost catches Nala. Despite receiving a fresh wound, the cuts on Shenzi’s cheek are instantly gone once she, Banzai, and Ed corner the lion cubs.
  • After encountering Mufasa, Banzai’s butt is left with several cuts from the lion’s claws. Banzai even complains that he won’t be able to sit for a week. His scars disappear after he fights Ed.

tropes.name: Hope Spot
tropes.html:
• The stampede scene is a sequence of multiple Hope Spots. The stampede catches up to Simba.. but then Mufasa arrives, grabs Simba and drops him off on a safe ledge. Then he's dragged away by the stampede, vanishing out of Simba's sight. He jumps back and grabs a ledge.. which is a cue for Scar to show himself to Mufasa. Mufasa thinks that Scar's there to help him, only for Scar to commit his supreme act of evil by sinking his claws into Mufasa's paws and throwing him back in. After the stampede, as Simba is looking for Mufasa, you hear movement. Simba looks up saying "Dad?" and for half a second, you the viewer think that maybe it's not that bad. Then a wildebeest runs by. Then you see what it just jumped over.
  • In a villainous example, Evil Uncle Scar survives dramatically falling off a cliff after the Final Battle with the hero with relatively no injury, and then relaxes in relief at seeing his usually comedic henchmen approach him ("Ahh, my friends..."), only to be begging for his life moments later as they proceed to rip him apart for denouncing them in a cowardly episode that he thought that no one had heard or witnessed.

tropes.name: Human Ladder
tropes.html: Zazu at the end of "I Just Can't Wait to be King" ends up at the bottom of an animal version, with a group of animals standing on top of each other to raise up Simba as he sings.

tropes.name: Humanlike Hand Anatomy
tropes.html: Rafiki the baboon has hands, understandably given that he's a primate. Zazu the bird has Feather Fingers and Timon the meerkat has Humanlike Hand Anatomy, for some reason. And the lions have rather large thumbs on their front paws, with which they can sometimes make humanlike gestures.

tropes.name: Hurricane of Puns
tropes.html:
• Zazu's morning report. The Special Edition's new song has even more of them.
    "Well, the buzz from the bees is that leopards are in a bit of a spot. The baboons are going ape... I told the elephants to forget it, but they can't... Cheetahs never prosper".
  • To cap that off, after Zazu finishes his report and gets pounced by Simba, a groundhog pops up to deliver "news from the underground".
  • Also, with the hyenas.
    Banzai: We could have whatever's... lion around!
    Shenzi: Wait wait wait. I got one. Make mine a cub sandwich. (Ed tries to get their attention) WHAT, ED?!
    Banzai: Hey, did we order this dinner to go?
    Shenzi: No. Why?
    Banzai: 'Cause there it goes! (points to Simba, Nala, and Zazu running like crazy)

tropes.name: Hyperfixation-Induced Error
tropes.html: Pumbaa is so busy chasing after a beetle that he doesn't notice a lioness hunting him until it's almost too late.

tropes.name: Hypocrite
tropes.html:
Scar tries to tell Simba not to kill him because they're family, even though Scar himself already killed one of his own family members and tried to kill another.
Simba: You don't deserve to live.
Scar: But Simba... I am family.

tropes.name: I Am Your Opponent
tropes.html: Done with a roar when the hyenas chase Simba and Nala into a corner. Simba tries to challenge them with an ineffective roar, to which they laugh. The second roar is much more startling... because it came from Mufasa, Simba’s father, and the rightful king of the Pridelands.

tropes.name: I Can Explain
tropes.html: When Scar faces his demise by the claws of the hyenas, he tries the "Let me explain" line to no avail.

tropes.name: Identical Son
tropes.html: As an adult, Simba looks exactly like his father did (a little darker, but that's besides the point). "In your reflection, he lives in you."

tropes.name: I Didn't Mean to Kill Him
tropes.html:
• Simba says this when Scar framed him for killing his father.
    Simba: The wildebeests, and... he tried to save me... It was an accident! I-I-I didn't mean for it to happen!
    Scar: Of course, of course you didn't. No-one ever means for these things to happen.
  • Later, Scar tries to invoke this when he gets cornered by Simba, saying that the hyenas made him kill Mufasa. It backfires greatly, as not only does Simba refuse to take any more of his lies, but the hyenas overhear and become furious, resulting in them attacking and killing Scar once Simba defeats him.

tropes.name: Idiotic Partner Confession
tropes.html:
• Simba when he questions why Zazu is acting so afraid of the hyenas when he said earlier that they were "slobbery, mangy, stupid poachers". Said hyenas are, of course, right in front of them. Downplayed, since Simba isn't so much an idiot as an innocent and silly child. Also, Simba is puffed up with his royal importance. Though this is technically right since, as a crown prince, he would be worth A LOT as a hostage; he forgets that those savage hyenas have zero diplomatic relations with his country.
  • A second example later on, when Mufasa corners the three Hyenas after they tried to kill Simba. Shenzi and Banzai immediately insist that they had no idea Simba is Mufasa's son; then Ed, interrogated in unison, spills the beans.

tropes.name: If You Kill Him, You Will Be Just Like Him!
tropes.html:
Simba immediately follows this by giving Scar a particularly ironic form of Cruel Mercy, which, although to note, does lead to his death:
Scar: What are you going to do? You wouldn't kill your own uncle, would you?
Simba: No, Scar. I'm not like you.

tropes.name: I Kiss Your Foot
tropes.html:
Pumbaa, after learning Simba is the king.
Pumbaa: King? Your Majesty! I gravel at your feet. (begins kissing Simba's paw)
Simba: (pulling it away) Stop that!
Timon: It's not gravel, it's grovel.

tropes.name: I'll Kill You!
tropes.html:
The hyenas' threats to a pursued Simba.
Shenzi: He's as good as dead out there anyway. And IF he comes back, we'll kill him.
Banzai: Yeah! D'you hear that? If you ever come back, we'll kill ya!

tropes.name: I'm Taking Her Home with Me!
tropes.html: When Timon and Pumbaa first run across Simba in the desert, Timon's first reaction is to panic because of, well, the food chain. Pumbaa meanwhile thinks Simba's such a cute little guy that he asks, "Can we keep him?"

tropes.name: I'm Standing Right Here
tropes.html: After Simba and Nala successfully escape from Zazu, the two briefly celebrate their success, until Simba arrogantly calls himself a genius, trying to take sole credit, causing Nala to stop in her tracks and glare at him in annoyance before she starts arguing with him, pointing out it was her idea.

tropes.name: Incest Subtext
tropes.html: The subtext in Simba and Nala's relationship isn't whether it's romantic, but whether they're related. Mufasa is the only adult male in the pride (as is typical in real lion prides), so one would be forgiven for assuming that he's Nala's father as well. In real life, male lions usually leave their prides in search of mates after reaching adulthood.

tropes.name: Inelegant Blubbering
tropes.html: Timon and Pumbaa bawl over "losing" Simba to his romance with Nala in the first film, and at emotional moments throughout the rest of the franchise.

tropes.name: I Never Told You My Name
tropes.html: Simba and Nala reunite as adults with neither recognizing each other, especially since the latter thinks the former is dead. After a brief fight between them in the jungle, with the two of them just growling at each other through the whole thing, Nala eventually wins by flipping Simba over and pinning him down. Simba recognizes this move from when Nala used it on him as cubs, and as she is holding him down, glaring at him menacingly practically nose to nose with him, all he can do is stare up at her helplessly until he says her name. This "mysterious lion" knowing her name shocks Nala into getting off of him and cautiously asks who he is, with him revealing he's Simba.

tropes.name: I Never Said It Was Poison
tropes.html: At the end of his conversation with Simba before the wildebeest stampede, Scar tells Simba "you might want to work on that little roar of yours." He's referring to the earlier incident where Simba let out a rather wimpy roar to try to scare off the hyenas, yet as far as Simba knows, Scar wasn't there at the time and wouldn't have any real reason to know about it. However, Simba fails to notice the discrepancy. Scar has spent a chunk of the conversation dropping very obvious hints about what his plan and motives are ("Simba, it's to die for!"), so it seems he's doing this to lord over how much he's deceived Simba—he effectively just confessed to his crime, and Simba didn't even notice.

tropes.name: Informed Species
tropes.html:
• Although Pumbaa is a warthog, he looks more like a tanned domesticated pig with a mane and tusks. To be fair, he did look like an actual warthog in early concept art.
  • Timon looks almost nothing like an actual meerkat. Timon is peach-yellow when meerkats are sand-coloured, has upturned ears when they have downturned ears, and a head full of red hair like a human would have. Plus, real meerkats walk on all fours and have black eyes.

tropes.name: In Harm's Way
tropes.html:
Simba, as a cub, has the primary goal in life at that point of going on dangerous adventures with his girlfriend Nala.
Simba: Danger? Ha! I walk on the wild side. I laugh in the face of danger. Ha ha ha ha!

tropes.name: Innocence Lost
tropes.html: Simba crosses the Despair Event Horizon while still a cub when he watches his father Mufasa fall to his death while trying to escape a stampede. It traumatized him to the point where he became an overprotective father towards his own daughter Kiara in The Lion King II: Simba's Pride, not wanting history to repeat.

tropes.name: Insult Backfire
tropes.html:
Simba: Hey, why don't you pick on someone your own size?!
Shenzi: Like you?
Simba: Oops.

tropes.name: Insult Misfire
tropes.html:
Zig-zagged:
Simba: Zazu, you told me they were nothing but slobbering mangy stupid poachers.
Zazu: Ixnay on the upidstey.
Banzai: Who you calling 'upidstey'?!

tropes.name: Internal Reveal
tropes.html: Scar, engaging in one last bit of Evil Gloating as he thinks he's finally about to kill Simba for good, leans in and finally tells him the truth: "I killed Mufasa!" This turns out to have been a mistake, as it gives Simba a Heroic Second Wind and he immediately pins Scar and forces him to repeat it to the rest of the pride.

tropes.name: Intimidation Failure
tropes.html: As the hyena trio have Simba and Nala cornered at the elephant graveyard, Simba tries to scare them off by roaring. But since he's just a cub, it's not very intimidating. Shenzi dares him to do it again, and he does, only now it's a booming roar... courtesy of Mufasa, seconds before he strikes the hyenas down.

tropes.name: Ironic Echo
tropes.html:
• After killing Mufasa, Scar tells Simba to "Run. Run away and never return." Then at the end of the film, when Scar seemingly pleads for mercy, Simba accepts but tells him, "Run. Run away, Scar, and never return."
  • Also in the same scene, after making Simba think killing Mufasa was all his fault, Scar says, "What will your mother think?" Later when Nala reunites with Simba and discovers he's alive, she says, "And your mother. What will she think?" not realizing the impact this line has on him.

tropes.name: Irony
tropes.html:
• The whole song "I Just Can't Wait to Be King", sung by an impatient, immature and naive Simba who wants to be a king already. Turns out Simba could wait. He had to. And when the time came he even resisted the call.
  • Simba constantly failed to beat Nala in any fight, to the point it almost seemed like a Running Gag. He was easily beaten by her twice in a row as cubs, even when he tried to cheat against her to gain an advantage. As an adult, he manages to do much better but still ultimately loses to her against the same move she used to flip and pin him as cubs. However, during their Falling-in-Love Montage when the two begin to playfully wrestle again, they end up accidentally tumbling down a hill together with Simba coming out the winner when he happens to land on top of Nala by complete accident. Thus, the only time he was ever able to "beat" her was when he wasn't even trying to. Simba and Nala both seem to realize this, and briefly laugh in amusement together over it.
  • From a certain perspective, Scar and Simba's fates could count as this. Scar basically exiled Simba, which should've been a miserable existence at best and a death sentence at worst. Meanwhile, Scar inherited the throne and therefore should've been living easy in the paradisiacal Pride Lands. But in the span of Simba's banishment, it's the opposite outcome. Simba grows up in Timon and Pumba's oasis, which unto itself is paradise, all the while he gets to live it up with his best friends. Scar on the other hand might as well have exiled himself, as his reign reduces his kingdom to a hyena-infested wasteland while surrounded by his starving subjects and their steadily dropping patience.

tropes.name: Is That a Threat?
tropes.html: A variation, with Mufasa saying "Is that a challenge?" In the original film, Scar reassures his brother, "I wouldn't dream of challenging you."

tropes.name: I Take Offense to That Last One
tropes.html: Banzai only seems to have a problem with being called "stupid" after hearing a bunch of insults. Even then, he doesn't pick up on it until Zazu explains this in Pig Latin.

tropes.name: It's All About Me
tropes.html: It's pretty obvious early on that Scar cares for no one except himself. He wants the throne for himself, is perfectly willing to kill his brother and try to kill his nephew to get it, and drives the Pridelands to ruin because of how he only wants the power of the throne and not the responsibilities that come with it.

tropes.name: It's All My Fault
tropes.html: Simba spends most of the movie believing that he killed his father mostly due to his Uncle's manipulations and tries to hide from the rest of the pride in shame.

tropes.name: I Was Beaten by a Girl
tropes.html: Simba is visibly frustrated at being handily pinned by Nala in their scraps, glaring at her in annoyance and immediately trying to get revenge on her by cheating. He uses this fighting tactic to recognise her as an adult and later uses it against Scar. Though he does eventually pin her himself, it is actually the least like a "fight" out of them all, being while they were romantically rolling down a hill together, and she still leads him 3-1.

tropes.name: It Was with You All Along
tropes.html: Rafiki tells Simba that his father is still alive. When Simba tells Rafiki that his father is dead, Rafiki shows him that his father still lives on inside him.

tropes.name: Jaw Drop
tropes.html: When Simba realizes the lioness he's fighting is childhood friend Nala, they stop fighting and start laughing, prompting a jaw drop from Timon.

tropes.name: Jitter Cam
tropes.html: Done subtly during the stampede scene, where the scene vibrates vertically slightly when at ground level.

tropes.name: Job Title
tropes.html: The title The Lion King describes the job at the heart of the story, the one the hero learns how to undertake.

tropes.name: Joke and Receive
tropes.html:
When Simba tells Timon and Pumba to create a diversion to distract the Hyenas, Timon sarcastically asks if he should "dress in drag and do the hula." Smash Cut to...
[The Hyenas turn their heads to the sound of Hawaiian drums]
Timon: LUAU!

tropes.name: Just Between You and Me
tropes.html: When Scar has Simba trapped on the ledge of a gorge ... instead of simply throwing him to his death, he gloats at the moment and, thinking he's finished him off and about to celebrate victory, whispers to him that he really masterminded his (Simba's) father's death. Huge mistake and huge aversion, as Simba gains a huge Heroic Second Wind and eventually defeats Scar in a fight.

tropes.name: Just Desserts
tropes.html: The ending has a chilling case. When Simba corners Scar, Scar shamefully tries to get Simba's sympathy by by saying it was the hyenas' idea. Unbeknown to him, the hyenas had overheard his attempt to throw them under the bus. After Simba throws him off a cliff, the betrayed hyenas decide to devour him out of spite.

tropes.name: Just Giving Orders
tropes.html: After Simba gets his Heroic Second Wind and has the villain cornered, Scar tries to weasel out of his comeuppance by placing all blame for the coup on Mufasa and the subsequent overrun of The Pridelands on the hyenas. "It was the hyenas; they're the enemy." While this excuse does avert being killed outright by Simba, this defense also proves to be quotable last words.

tropes.name: Just in Time
tropes.html: At the beginning, Scar traps Zazu in his mouth and is about to eat him, when Mufasa enters at just the right moment and orders Scar to drop him. Zazu lampshades it, poking his beak out of Scar's mouth to do so: "Impeccable timing, your majesty!"

tropes.name: "Just Joking" Justification
tropes.html: The movie's Greek dub has Scar try to justify saying the hyenas were the enemy with this.

tropes.name: "Just So" Story
tropes.html: There's an In-Universe example with Timon's theory about how stars form, which involves them really being fireflies, and is true in The Princess and the Frog. This movie, however, rolls with the explanation of them being spirits of lion kings of the past.

tropes.name: Karmic Death
tropes.html: Scar spent his life betraying family and allies, and this finally bites him big time as the Hyenas descend upon him for trying to blame them for Mufasa's death. Doubly so that he is only swarmed after being thrown off a cliff, the same way he killed Mufasa.

tropes.name: Karmic Jackpot
tropes.html: Timon and Pumbaa come to help in the climax, despite being outcasts who spend their time chasing buzzards. They say it's worth facing danger for Simba's sake. Simba smiles and, in the end, makes them part of the Pride.

tropes.name: King of Beasts
tropes.html: It is about a lion’s monarchy, after all, and so lions are portrayed as the rulers who oversee all of the other animals. Note also the subversion of the usual phrasing "king of the jungle" - it's during his time in the jungle where he doesn't normally belong that Simba is trying to avoid facing responsibility and going back to become king.

tropes.name: Kinslaying Is a Special Kind of Evil
tropes.html: Scar is always seen as a dark part of the community but his point of no return is when he sends his brother, Mufasa, hurtling to his death and instructs the hyenas to murder his nephew in order to allow Scar to ascend to the throne. When the truth is eventually revealed, the pack turns on Scar and he is exiled under threat of death. Scar tries to use the hyenas as scapegoats, however, and after he fights back but loses, they eat him.

tropes.name: Lame Comeback
tropes.html: When Simba and Nala are arguing over who deserves credit for the their plan on ditching Zazu, Nala counters every argument Simba makes, first when she says that it was her idea, and then when Simba says he pulled it off she remarks he did so with her. After this, Simba just smirks at her deviously and says "Oh yeah?" in a sly tone instead of trying to make another counterpoint, and resorts to pouncing on her to have the last word and force her to admit he deserves all the credit. This backfires spectacularly when she easily beats him by flipping him and pinning him down, then teases him for his loss to his embarrassment.

tropes.name: Last-Second Word Swap
tropes.html:
• In the scene where the hyenas complain to Scar about not having any food:
    Banzai: (muttering under his breath) I thought things were bad under Mufasa.
    Scar: What did you say?!
    Banzai: I said Muf-(Shenzi elbows him) I said, uh... "'Qué pasa?'"
    Scar: Good. Now, get out!
  • When Pumbaa gets stuck under a tree branch running away from Nala:
    Timon, pushing Pumbaa's ass to get him unstuck: "Why do i always have to save your..." (sees Nala jumping towards them both) "...AAAAAHH!!!"

tropes.name: Last Villain Stand
tropes.html: Scar is outed as the one who killed Mufasa at the end of the film, and begs Simba for mercy; when Simba opts to banish him, Scar makes as if to leave... but then kicks burning embers into Simba's face and attacks him.

tropes.name: Laughing at Your Own Jokes
tropes.html: When Timon and Pumbaa meet Simba, Pumbaa asks "What's eatin' ya?" Before Simba can answer, Timon chimes in with "Nothing, he's at the top of the food chain!" He laughs pretty hard at his own joke until he realizes no one's laughing with him.

tropes.name: Laziness Callout
tropes.html: There's a negative variant; after Scar takes over the Pride Lands, it becomes a wasteland because he allowed the hyenas to run amok eating as they pleased rather than try to rein them in. When Scar accuses Sarabi and her hunting party of not doing their jobs (finding food), Sarabi explains that the herds have moved on. Scar's response is to accuse Sarabi and her hunting party of not looking hard enough.

tropes.name: Leave the Two Lovebirds Alone
tropes.html: When Simba and Nala reunite, she asks for the two of them to be left alone. When Simba repeats that request, Timon realizes what is about to happen and laments the two will fall in love.

tropes.name: Left Hanging
tropes.html: Although 'Hakuna Matata' vaguely explains why Pumbaa became an outcast, why Timon did does not get addressed. Made up by the fact that there's an entire midquel dedicated to it.

tropes.name: Leitmotif upon Death
tropes.html: When Simba finds his father Mufasa dead, "This Land" plays in a very somber tone. While this piece is mainly used for The Pridelands, Mufasa is in most of the scenes where the score was played. It is also used when Simba is visited by Mufasa's spirit.

tropes.name: Lethal Negligence
tropes.html: When Scar takes over the Pride Lands, he ends up turning it from a lush wilderness teeming with life to a barren wasteland with barely any food, because while Scar desired the power and perks that came with being king, he was too lazy to perform the actual responsibilities that came with it.

tropes.name: Let Me Get This Straight...
tropes.html: Timon when Nala shows up: "Let me get this straight. You know her. She knows you. But she wants to eat him. And everybody is okay with this? Did I miss something?!"

tropes.name: Life Isn't Fair
tropes.html: Said by Scar in a creepy tone. It is the first spoken (not sung) sentence in the movie.

tropes.name: Light/Darkness Juxtaposition
tropes.html:
The film contrasts the brightly-lit, beautiful Pride Lands with the Elephant Graveyard, a shadowy, miserable wasteland. Simba and Mufasa's rule is generally associated with light (eg. the Natural Spotlight when a new heir is born, the warm light that surrounds Simba when he arrives to reclaim the throne, their own red-and-gold color scheme); meanwhile, when the dark-colored Scar usurps the throne, the Pride Lands are cast in shadow.
Simba: Everything the light touches... What about that shadowy place?

tropes.name: Lightning Reveal
tropes.html:
Happens during the climax of the movie when Simba reveals himself to Scar before the final confrontation. In the brief glimpse he gets, Scar mistakes Simba for his father at first.
Scar: Mufasa? No! You're dead!

tropes.name: "Lion King" Lift
tropes.html: The Trope Namer and Ur-Example happens in “Circle of Life”, wherein Rafiki grandly lifts the newborn Simba up so everyone can see the new prince on Pride Rock.

tropes.name: Literally Going Bananas
tropes.html: Shortly after meeting with an adult Simba, Rafiki makes an African Chant — "Asante sana, squash banana, we we nugu mi mi hapana" — at which Simba dismisses him as some crazy monkey. Subverted, however, as Rafiki proves to be very wise and this was done merely as a playful taunt (in Swahili, it translates to, "Thank you very much, [mister] squashed banana! You are a baboon, and I am not!")

tropes.name: Literal Metaphor
tropes.html: As Mufasa is continuing the "pouncing lesson", a gopher pops out of the ground to deliver "news from the underground!"

tropes.name: Literal-Minded
tropes.html:
Pumbaa, sometimes.
Timon: Gee, he looks blue.
Pumbaa: I'd say brownish-gold.

tropes.name: Literally Falling in Love
tropes.html: During "Can You Feel The Love Tonight", Simba and Nala accidentally end up tumbling down a hill together while playfully wrestling. Simba ends up pinning Nala, and she gives him a surprise lick on the cheek before they both share a romantic seductive gaze.

tropes.name: Lotus Position
tropes.html: Rafiki has been known to meditate in this position. In this movie, he shows this pose before the appearance of Mufasa's ghost.

tropes.name: Love Redeems
tropes.html: Simba may have seemingly killed his father and happily let the pride become a desert while he sings "Hakuna Matata", but he meets Nala again and returns.

tropes.name: Love Theme
tropes.html: "Can You Feel the Love Tonight" is about the budding relationship between Simba and Nala, from simple friends to something more than that. It ends with the two sharing G-Rated Sex.

tropes.name: Lust
tropes.html: Scar murders his brother and attempts to kill his nephew in order to rule Pride Rock.

tropes.name: Lying on a Hillside
tropes.html: Simba, Timon, and Pumbaa when stargazing, although it isn't actually a hillside they're on.

tropes.name: Make an Example of Them
tropes.html:
Scar's Villain Song is punctuated at one point by him backing one of his hyenas into an open fissure in order to assert his dominance over them in his master plan which makes his later death at their hands as a result of his exploitation of them all the more ironic.
Scar: The future is littered with prizes,
And though I'm the main addressee,
The point that I must emphasize is:
YOU WON'T GET A SNIFF WITHOUT ME!

tropes.name: Make It Look Like an Accident
tropes.html: This is part of Scar's bastardry, when he murders his brother Mufasa and convinces Simba that his father died in an accident for which Simba was to blame, then tells the rest of the pride that Simba also died in the same accident after driving him away.

tropes.name: Malaproper
tropes.html: Pumbaa, occasionally, for example saying "I gravel at your feet" instead of "grovel" and messing up Timon's saying "You've gotta put your past behind you" as "You gotta put your behind in your past". Timon corrects him both times.

tropes.name: Mama Bear
tropes.html: When Simba forces Scar to confess that he killed Mufasa, Sarabi roars and follows Nala into battle. She suddenly understood that Scar framed Simba for Mufasa's death and launched a coup.

tropes.name: Manchild
tropes.html: Timon & Pumbaa (and occasionally the hyenas) can act very immature at times.

tropes.name: Man Hug
tropes.html: Rafiki and Mufasa at the beginning before Simba is revealed (both to the audience and then to the Pridelands) and then Rafiki and Simba at the end before Simba ascends Pride Rock.

tropes.name: Masculine Lines, Feminine Curves
tropes.html: Female lions (lionesses) such as Nala appear smooth, whereas male lions such as Simba appear rugged. The character designers, such as Aaron Blaise, made a conscious effort to integrate the principle of "rough males, smooth females" into designing the characters, even though it may not make a whole lot of sense considering these animals have the same build and are covered in rough fur anyway.

tropes.name: Maybe Magic, Maybe Mundane
tropes.html:
• It's left ambiguous whether or not animals can speak human In-Universe.
  • It's left ambiguous whether or not the "I Just Can't Wait to Be King" sequence is really happening or is just Simba's imagination (at the very least, the animals' more cartoony appearance and bright, unnatural colors are surely an indication of him letting his fantasy of kingship and its perks run away with him, and other things such as Zazu surviving being run over are clearly not meant to be actually happening).
  • It's not exactly clear if Mufasa appearing in the clouds happens for real or if it's just a representation of Simba's conscience. Mufasa notably doesn't tell Simba anything he doesn't already know and Rafiki doesn't directly acknowledge the former, only making a vague comment about the "weather".

tropes.name: Mean Character, Nice Actor
tropes.html: In-Universe example: In the Outtakes short in the 3D release, Scar, Shenzi and Ed get in on the fun. The hyena trio are also frequent guests in House of Mouse.

tropes.name: Meaningful Echo
tropes.html:
• "Run... Run away... and NEVER return." Scar to Simba as a cub, and later an older Simba to Scar once he catches on to the deception.
  • "Danger? Ha!... I laugh in the face of danger! Ha ha ha ha!" by Simba when he and Nala are cubs, later quoted by Nala when they’re adults.
  • "What will your mother/she think?" Scar to Simba, then Nala to Simba when they’re adults.
  • The hyena trio rhetorically questions each other about the cubs' presence in the graveyard scene, Ed concluding with a hysterical laugh. They echo themselves at the end when discussing the fate of Scar, but with a much darker overtone:
    "Ed?" ( Evil laughter)

tropes.name: Meaningful Name
tropes.html:
Several names can be translated from Swahili (except Ed, Timon, Scar, and Mufasa), but it is more or less meaningful for each character:
  • Simba means lion in Swahili and, indeed, Simba is a lion.
  • Scar, who has a very obvious one across the left eye. There may be a heavy background behind this, but it is never detailed in the film. According to The Lion King: Six New Adventures, his Swahili name is Taka, meaning both "garbage" and "want". He certainly wants his brother's kingdom, and being named garbage his whole life might explain his envy of his brother, see below.
  • The origin of Mufasa's name is not certain, either meaning king in Manazoto or being a tribute to an ancient Kenyan king, but with no proofs for either.
  • Pumbaa means foolish. It's right that he's not especially smart and gets often fooled by Timon, although he has also moments of perspicacity.
  • Rafiki means friend. He looks like he is a precious adviser to the king, and his advice is indeed decisive in resolving Simba's inner conflict.
  • Zazu means movement. Of course, since he is a bird, he moves a lot and fast by flying.
  • Shenzi means barbarous. She is part of a species excluded from the "civilized" Pride Lands because they don't respect its rules.
  • There is no certainty about the three lionesses:
    • Nala means gift. It can be speculated that's because she is a foreign princess given to the Pride during some diplomatic exchange, but there are no canon indications (although her father is now clearly established to not be Scar or Mufasa).
    • Sarabi means mirage and Sarafina means bright star. Hard to tell without more backstory.

tropes.name: Melancholy Musical Number
tropes.html: Zazu begins singing "Nobody Knows The Trouble I've Seen" while moping in a ribcage in Scar's lair. Scar objects that the song is too maudlin and commands Zazu to shift to one with "more bounce to it." Mockingly, Zazu shifts to "It's A Small World After All", which Scar finds even worse.

tropes.name: Men of Sherwood
tropes.html: The lionesses of Pride Rock who fight the hyenas while Simba is fighting Scar.

tropes.name: Metaphorically True
tropes.html:
Almost nothing Scar says to Simba before or after the stampede is untrue, which has the dual effect of covering his tracks and appealing to his twisted sense of humor.
"Simba, it's to die for."
If it weren't for you, he'd still be alive.
If it weren't for you, Mufasa would still be alive! Do you deny it?

tropes.name: Mighty Roar
tropes.html: Used a lot by the lions whenever they are about to do something awesome, though Simba as a cub can only give an anticlimatic meow (Truth in Television: lion cubs can't roar, only mewl adorably).

tropes.name: Million Mook March
tropes.html: The goosestepping hyenas in Scar's Villain Song "Be Prepared", which references Nazi party rallies.

tropes.name: Misophonia Gag
tropes.html: After Mufasa berates Scar for missing Simba's ceremony, Scar expresses mock regret while sharpening his claws on the wall of the cave. The scraping sound makes Zazu cringe and wince.

tropes.name: Misplaced Wildlife
tropes.html:
• Giant anteaters and leafcutter ants — both species endemic to Latin America — appear briefly in "I Just Can't Wait To Be King" and "The Circle of Life", respectively.
  • All the other fauna is from Africa, but not all are from East Africa where the movie appears to take place (e.g., meerkats like Timon are from South Africa, Botswana, and Namibia, and mandrills like Rafiki are from the jungles of West and Central Africa).
  • Gorillas are also briefly seen amongst the savannah animals at the end of "The Circle of Life" as well as once in "I Just Can't Wait To Be King", even though gorillas are forest-dwelling primates.
  • The rodent who warns Zazu of the hyenas' invasion also counts. He's referred to as a Gopher in related media (which doesn't make sense in itself, since gophers are endemic to the Americas), but he's actually most likely a big-headed mole-rat; said species is only found in the Ethiopian Highlands, VERY far-removed from the Serengeti.

tropes.name: Mistaken for Romance
tropes.html: When Simba and Nala begin whispering to each other about how to get rid of Zazu and sneak away to the elephant graveyard, Zazu sees the two of them whispering to each other and mistakenly assumes the two of them are flirting together before happily telling them how their "blossoming romance" works perfectly due to their Arranged Marriage.

tropes.name: Mistreatment-Induced Betrayal
tropes.html: At the end of the movie, Scar's plea for mercy from Simba wasn't very convincing or effective, but his Karmic Death could have been averted if he hadn't slagged off the hyenas at the same time.

tropes.name: Mood Whiplash
tropes.html:
• Perhaps most notably when we go from Mufasa and Simba's funeral and Rafiki crossing out Simba's outline to... bowling for buzzards! (the comic relief was badly needed for some after the past few minutes).
  • Just before that, there's Shenzi calling Banzai "cactus butt" right after Mufasa's death.
  • Simba's reunion with Nala in the forest is also noticeable. It starts with a fierce battle between the two with Simba trying to protect Timon and Pumbaa, then the two joyfully recognizing each other and them falling in love by hanging out around the forest in what can be considered a date. Then the two get into an argument immediately afterwards about Simba coming back to become king and Simba storming off in anger, resembling a temporary breakup between the two of them.
  • After Simba receives a pep talk from his dead father, he and Rafiki talk about change. Simba admits he's afraid of facing his past. Rafiki then whacks him with a stick; he then uses it as an analogy about how the past can hurt, but you can learn from it. As a result, Simba playfully tosses Rafiki's stick and starts running back to Pride Rock, causing Rafiki to howl in joy.

tropes.name: Mooning
tropes.html: In one moment during the song "I Just Can't Wait to Be King" shows Simba and Nala walking past a herd of zebras who stand at attention as they pass, but when Zazu tries to follow them, the zebras turn about face and lift their tails to present their butts to him. When Zazu sees this, he promptly flinches and covers himself with his wings, just in case.

tropes.name: Moral Luck
tropes.html:
Scar uses this trope to trick Simba and later the lionesses into thinking he's morally responsible for his father's death. While the audience knows Scar masterminded the whole thing, Simba is tricked into thinking that his "little roar" in the gorge frightened a nearby herd of wildebeest (which he didn't even know were there) into stampeding, which ended up trampling Mufasa. Scar then leads him to believe that accidentally doing something that unintentionally causes someone else's death is morally the same as intentionally killing them.
Scar: Murderer!
Simba: No! It was an accident!
Scar: If it weren't for you, Mufasa would still be alive! It's your fault he's dead. Do you deny it?
Simba: No.
Scar: Then you're guilty.

tropes.name: Mordor
tropes.html:
• The Elephant Graveyard is an eerie, decrepit wasteland full of bones and skeletal corpses that is located far away from Pride Lands, and therefore lacks Mufasa's regal jurisdiction. Mufasa advises Simba against heading there due to its danger, but the latter goes there anyway and exposes his, as well as Nala's and Zazu's, lives to danger.
  • The Pride Lands themselves become a Mordor of sorts after Scar and the hyenas take over. The sky turns grey, all the plants die and all the animals are gone. As expected, when Simba defeats Scar and takes his rightful place as king, the land recovers perfectly (and apparently fast enough that the Pride doesn't starve in the meantime).note  Simba's mother did advise Scar to temporarily leave the Pridelands during this period, and follow the herds in an attempt to solve the scarcity of resources. Scar refused out of pride, not wanting to leave the kingdom he'd spent years coveting.

tropes.name: More Deadly Than the Male
tropes.html: Simba has never been able to beat his best friend Nala in a fight. He lost to her twice in a row as cubs, and the second time he pounced on her when she was distracted. They fight a third time years later as adults and although they are more evenly matched, she still pins him the exact same way, flipping him and pinning him down. She snarls down at him and could have possibly killed him before he says her name. Although Simba does eventually get a "win" against her, pinning her after tumbling down a hill together, it is more of a romantic moment between the two than a "fight".

tropes.name: Moving Beyond Bereavement
tropes.html: Mufasa is killed by Scar shortly after he saves Simba from a wildebeest stampede. With a little persuasion from Scar, Simba believes that he was responsible for the death and flees the Pride Lands in shame; teaming up with Timon and Pumbaa, he accepts their philosophy of Hakuna Matata as a means of distancing himself from his grief — without actually moving on. Years later, he's reunited with Nala, who tries to convince him to return to the Pride Lands and dethrone Scar, but Simba is reluctant to confront his misplaced guilt. Simba soon meets up with Rafiki, who teaches him that the past can hurt, but it's also important to learn from it so he can prepare for the future; Mufasa's spirit also appears and tells Simba that he needs to remember that he's his son and needs to take his place as the one true king, finally giving him the confidence to stand up to Scar.

tropes.name: Multilingual Song
tropes.html: "The Circle of Life", which has lyrics in both English and Zulu.

tropes.name: Mum Looks Like a Sister
tropes.html: When Simba returns to Pride Rock bearing a Strong Family Resemblance to his deceased father, his mother Sarabi doesn't look any different from when he was a cub. (In fact, she shares a similar body model and facial structure to his own childhood sweetheart, Nala.)

tropes.name: Murder by Inaction
tropes.html: It seems like this is how Mufasa is going to die: after luring Simba into a ravine that the hyenas are going to drive a herd of stampeding wildebeest through, it looks as though all that Scar will need to do is sit there and gloat after Mufasa gets Simba to safety but can't save himself without Scar's assistance - but Scar, prideful, treacherous and sadistic to the end, can't resist the opportunity to Kick the Dog and throw Mufasa off the cliff and into the stampede anyway.

tropes.name: Musicalis Interruptus
tropes.html:
Pumbaa's last verse in "Hakuna Matata", a case of Curse Cut Short:
Pumbaa: And I got downhearted, every time that I...
Timon: Pumbaa, not in front of the kids!
Pumbaa: Oh, sorry.

tropes.name: Nails on a Blackboard
tropes.html: Early on, Scar scrapes his nails on a rock face in order to annoy Zazu.

tropes.name: Named After the Injury
tropes.html: Mufasa's evil brother has a scar going down the side of his face, and is named Scar. note  According to The Lion Guard, Scar was originally named "Askari" after his ancestor, while an earlier book based on the film named him "Taka".

tropes.name: Natural Spotlight
tropes.html: • The future king being held to the sky is highlighted by focused sunbeams, when there aren't any clouds to justify the light slits. During the "Hakuna Matata" song, this happens several times.

tropes.name: A Nazi by Any Other Name
tropes.html: Not so much in ideology, but in imagery: the song "Be Prepared", in which Scar rallies the Hyenas into setting up a new age in Pride Rock, ruled by Scar and the Hyenas. The Nazi symbolism is quite clear during a sequence when the Hyenas goose step (the most evilest march ever) by Scar. The scene is directly inspired by Triumph of the Will. This makes the song especially chilling if you watch it in either Hebrew or German.

tropes.name: Never My Fault
tropes.html: Scar attempts to blame Mufasa's death of his hyena army, unaware that Banzai, Ed and Shenzi were overhearing him the whole time. Not only does Simba not buy it, but it sets the stage for the hyenas turning on Scar.

tropes.name: New Era Speech
tropes.html:
• After Mufasa's death, Scar stands before Pride Rock, proclaiming: "A new era, in which lion and hyena come together in a great and glorious future!"
  • His entire Villain Song, "Be Prepared", is about the new era he wants to bring about. In a deleted scene, there's a reprise of the song instead of his normal speech at Pride Rock, which was also a New Era Speech.

tropes.name: Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!
tropes.html: When Mufasa's Ghost speaks to the Adult Simba later in the film, he chastises his son for abandoning Pride Rock and his responsibitlies as King. Mufasa does not, however, share with Simba the revelation of his final moments alive: That Scar, not the Stampede, killed the King. So Simba returns to the Pride Lands still believing he is responsible for Mufasa's death and it nearly derails his entire bid to dethrone Scar (see below) before Simba finally learns the truth.

tropes.name: Nice Job Fixing It, Villain!
tropes.html:
• As a child, Simba had a massive ego and believed that being King allows one to do anything they want. It is scary to imagine just how easily he could have become a tyrant. By destroying his life, Scar sets in motion the events that proceed to turn Simba into a better person. Some may object that Mufasa would have curbed this trait by teaching him how to rule the kingdom; but it is debatable. One can find the admonition he gives to his son a little too short and light-hearted for the case of a child who nearly died with his friend by going into a place he was explicitly told not to by two people on the very day. In parallel, Sarabi seems careless enough to let the crown prince couple take a stroll under the lone supervision of a small powerless hornbill.
  • The hyena trio abandoning their pursuit of Simba after he flees the Pride Lands and letting Scar think Simba was dead when he actually wasn't, so Scar ended up leaving him alone, setting off the chain of events that will ultimately end both Scar's rule and the Hyenas running amok in the Pride Lands. In the Hyenas' defense, a lone wandering cub like Simba should have died in the wastelands under normal circumstances (be it by dehydration, starvation, or local predators). It was just dumb luck for them that Timon and Pumbaa went 'Bowling for Buzzards' when and where they did and ultimately rescued Simba.
  • Scar is being challenged by Simba's return, but he makes the pride turn against Simba by making him still believe he caused Mufasa's death. As he drives Simba towards the cliff, he decides to give a Just Between You and Me speech in which he tells him what really happened. This helps Simba shake off his guilt, and he gets his Heroic Second Wind against Scar, forcing him to confess his crimes in full view of everyone.
  • Scar does it again in the finale when he hastily tries to save his own skin by shifting all the blame onto the hyenas... within their hearing. This makes the hyenas back off to make him fight Simba alone... and they maul him to death later.

tropes.name: "No. Just… No" Reaction
tropes.html:
Scar wants Zazu to sing him something happy sounding instead of the downtrodden depressing songs he's been singing him.
Scar: Come now, Zazu, do lighten up. Sing something with a little… bounce in it!
Zazu: [sarcastically] It's a small world after all…
Scar: No, NO! Anything but that!

tropes.name: Non-Standard Kiss
