tropes.html: Simba and Nala nuzzle their faces together as a means of showing affection soon after they run into each other for the first time in years.

tropes.name: No One Could Survive That!
tropes.html: The hyenas break off the chase after Simba manages to lose them in the briar patch. Shenzi had a point that Simba probably wouldn't survive in the desert. Needless to say, Scar pays for their lack of responsibility years later when Simba returns fully grown.

tropes.name: No Ontological Inertia
tropes.html: Scar is killed and within what must be roughly a lion's gestation period note 110 days, if you care the Pridelands have gone from barren and burned back to Ghibli Hills.

tropes.name: Not in Front of the Kid!
tropes.html:
Timon interrupts Pumbaa’s lyric while also Breaking the Fourth Wall.
Pumbaa: And I felt downhearted / Ev'ry time that I...
Timon: Pumbaa! Not in front of the kids.

tropes.name: No, You
tropes.html:
When Mufasa is confronting Scar for not coming to Simba's presentation and he starts to turn away.
Mufasa: Don't turn your back on me, Scar!
Scar: Oh, no, Mufasa. Perhaps YOU shouldn't turn YOUR back on me.

tropes.name: Ocular Gushers
tropes.html: Timon and Pumbaa cry profusely when they realize they are losing Simba to Nala.

tropes.name: Oddball in the Series
tropes.html: In 2017, The Lion King's everlasting fame and success earned it a spot in the Walt Disney Signature Collection, the third line Walt Disney Home Video created for the Animated Canon's most lucrative hand-drawn movies (and the first to release any of those movies, including TLK, on Ultra HD and Disney+). However, it remains the only entry neither supervised by Walt Disney, nor based on a story he made aborted plans to adapt. The press release states that the collection includes films either made or inspired by Walt, subtly turning Bambi's influence on TLK into grounds to include both movies.note Bambi even joined the Signature Collection the same year that TLK did, as it marked Bambi's 75th anniversary.

tropes.name: Odd Name Out
tropes.html:
• On a grand scale. All members of the main cast have African names (except Scar). (Scar's real name is Askari). The only one to have a more European sounding name is Ed. He also seems to be, er, mentally challenged.
  • Also Timon, whose name is Greek in origin.

tropes.name: Offhand Backhand
tropes.html:
• Rafiki pulls off this stunt on one of the hyenas.
  • Pumbaa does this too. Except with his back legs.

tropes.name: Offscreen Moment of Awesome
tropes.html: We do see the events leading up to it, but Pumbaa managing to scare away Shenzi and Banzai takes place entirely offscreen, with only Ed's reaction being shown. It still manages to be pretty epic.

tropes.name: Offscreen Teleportation
tropes.html: Following the stampede, we see Simba reach the end of the gorge, which is a massive narrow vertical slope riddled with boulders. No way a herd of at least a few hundred wildebeest could manage to make it out of there so quickly.

tropes.name: Oh, Crap!
tropes.html:
• Zazu at the beginning when he realizes Scar is about to try and eat him. Luckily for him, Mufasa enters Just in Time and Scar spits Zazu out.
  • Zazu gets a couple of humourous ones near the end of the "I Just Can't Wait to be King" number, notably he screams in horror just before a troupe of animals trample over him and then at the song's conclusion, he looks straight at the viewer as he realises he's the only thing left holding up a rhino ( that's holding the tower of animals on its back) which promptly squashes him. In the same scene, the red elephants circling the tower of animals have this reaction and panic when the tower starts to crumble.
  • After Simba confidently laughs in the face of danger, he gets this reaction after he hears danger (i.e. the hyenas) laugh back.
  • And when Simba says to the hyenas, "Why don't you pick on someone your own size?!" to which Shenzi responds, "Like... you?" and Simba gets this reaction and says, "Oops."
  • Simba when he first sees the stampede heading straight for him, coupled with a very dramatic and iconic Vertigo Effect. One of the rare examples of this not being played for laughs at all, but instead for a dark kind of awesomeness. The iconic shot provides the main image for the trope.
  • Mufasa, when he realizes his son is in the middle of a wildebeest stampede, as well as, in his last moments of life, realizing how insane, dangerous, and power-hungry his brother really is.
  • After Mufasa is killed and Scar tells Simba to run away, Simba has one when he sees the hyenas are behind him and realises they intend to kill him.
  • Pumbaa, complete with Screams Like a Little Girl, when he happens to spot Nala lining up for a pounce - on him.
  • Nala gets one when Simba lunges at her when she's chasing Timon and Pumbaa. Though she quickly gets over it and begins fighting him evenly.
  • After smacking Sarabi to the ground for mentioning Mufasa in his presence, Scar notices a very angry looking Simba watching above. Punctuated since he actually thought it was Mufasa himself at first. Then, he realizes that Simba's returning to take his place as the rightful king.
  • Simba when Scar corners him on the cliff and whispers to him that Scar killed Mufasa. Seconds later, Scar has one of his own when Simba attacks him and has him tell the truth to the pride.
  • Banzai and Shenzi when they realize why calling Pumbaa a pig wasn't the smartest thing to do.
  • Scar when he realizes that he is about to be killed by his former mooks after being thrown off Pride Rock.

tropes.name: "Oh, Crap!" Smile
tropes.html: Shenzi and Banzai smile awkwardly after Mufasa caught them preying on Simba and Nala.

tropes.name: Oh, No... Not Again!
tropes.html:
When Zazu is caught by the hyenas, they proceed to force him into a geyser that they have dubbed the "birdie boiler", which blasts him off into the sky like a firework. Zazu's reaction implies this isn't the first time he's been forced into the boiler:
Banzai: Majordomo birdie hippity-hopped all the way into the birdie boiler!
Zazu: Oh, no, not the birdie boil-AAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHH!

tropes.name: One-Man Army
tropes.html:
• Don't underestimate Pumbaa; he tears through several dozen hyenas without breaking a sweat.
  • And of course there's Mufasa, who managed to take down three hyenas at once.

tropes.name: OOC Is Serious Business
tropes.html: Ed is usually seen laughing or goofing about. At the end, though, he is visibly pissed off and glaring straight at Scar. Even Shenzi and Banzai look worried at Ed's change of mood.

tropes.name: Orbital Shot
tropes.html: When Scar is interrogating Simba in front of his pride over his "responsibility" for Mufasa's death.

tropes.name: Orphaned Etymology
tropes.html:
• Scar uses several turns of phrase reliant on modern human society, such as the "shallow end of the gene pool" or "the lights are not all on upstairs."
  • When Banzai falls into the thorns and suffers some Amusing Injuries, Shenzi jokingly calls him "cactus butt". There are no traditional-looking cacti in Africa note  Except for those introduced by Europeans., and the plants that hurt Banzai don't look like cacti, so they probably just used this word because "cactus butt" sounds funnier than "thorn butt".

tropes.name: Outliving One's Offspring
tropes.html: Subverted, as Sarabi believes for a large portion of the movie that she has outlived her only child — but he's alive all along.

tropes.name: Overly Specific Afterlife
tropes.html: The film only mentions that the Great Kings live in the stars upon dying. Nothing is stated about other lions or non-lions.

tropes.name: Pacifism Backfire
tropes.html: Simba decides not to execute Scar, because "I'm not like you," and banishes him instead (the biggest mistake he makes is dropping his guard as well). Scar uses it as an opportunity to ambush him and nearly kill him. It doesn't work (and Scar gets killed by the hyenas instead).

tropes.name: Pain-Powered Leap
tropes.html: Banzai the hyena jumps about 30 feet into the air after he is knocked into a bramble thicket by the other hyenas.

tropes.name: Pale Females, Dark Males
tropes.html: Nearly all the lionesses are lighter compared to the lions, except Sarabi.

tropes.name: Parents Suck at Matchmaking
tropes.html: Zazu tells Simba and Nala that their parents will thrilled when they'll learn the two are getting along so well, since they are to be betrothed. Simba is disgusted and Nala comments it would be weird they get married because they are just friends. Subverted when Nala reunites with Simba after his exile and the two find out they actually love each other.

tropes.name: Perfectly Arranged Marriage
tropes.html: A roundabout example with Simba and Nala. As cubs, they are told by Zazu they are betrothed, meaning they will be married one day. This disgusts both of them, not because they dislike each other, but because they both think that marrying their best friend would be too weird. Though Simba says once he is king, he'll officially remove his and Nala's betrothment since he can do whatever he wants as king. When they meet again after several years when Nala thought Simba was dead, the two fall in love with each other and by the end of the film are married as they were originally betrothed to.

tropes.name: Perma-Stubble
tropes.html: All male hyenas have dark patches around their muzzles that look remarkably like stubble. It's one of the few things that distinguish them from the females. In The Lion King 1½, there is another female hyena — you can tell because she has no stubble and a thick tuft of fringe.

tropes.name: Pinned to the Ground
tropes.html: When Simba and Nala are play fighting as cubs, Nala beats Simba and pinned him down twice in a row, teasing him "Pinned ya," both times. They later end up fighting again as adults, with Nala doing the same thing to him again, with this being how Simba is able to recognize his best friend after being apart for years. Later during their Falling-in-Love Montage, the two accidentally tumble down a hill together, resulting in Simba landing on top of Nala and pinning her down for the first time.

tropes.name: The Pirates Who Don't Do Anything
tropes.html: Played With. No carnivorous characters are ever shown successfully killing any prey on screen (with the exception of some soulless bugs), but it's made clear that they do eat herbivores.

tropes.name: Platonic Co-Parenting
tropes.html: Timon and Pumbaa raise Simba for the remainder of his childhood after he runs away. They also insist on helping him on finding out he needs to fight his uncle to reclaim his kingdom.

tropes.name: Playing the Family Card
tropes.html: Finding himself cornered at the top of Pride Rock, surrounded by flames, and with a righteously furious Simba at his heel, Scar tries desperately blaming Mufasa's murder on the hyenas, saying, "They're the enemy, Simba! I'm your family!... You wouldn't kill your old uncle, would you?" Simba doesn't buy his uncle's lies for a second, (especially because he had earlier smugly admitted to the murder when he thought he had Simba at his mercy) but makes it clear that he's not going to sink to Scar's level, instead deciding to banish the Dirty Coward from the Pridelands. When Scar then tries sneak-attacking him anyway, Simba throws him off Pride Rock, but still doesn't kill him- but the hyenas, who overheard Scar trying to throw them under the bus, and have already been growing unhappy with his Bad Boss tendencies, have no such qualms.

tropes.name: Playing the Victim Card
tropes.html: Scar tries this after Simba has him on the ropes, blaming the hyenas for leading him astray. It bites him in the ass later. And the rest of his body.

tropes.name: Please, Don't Leave Me
tropes.html: When Mufasa's spirit appears to Simba, telling him to remember who he is and go back to reclaim his rightful place as king, Simba chases after him while he's disappearing, begging him not to leave him. However, Mufasa's words finally sink into Simba's mind and he decides to go back.

tropes.name: Please Wake Up
tropes.html:
Simba tells Mufasa to get up in the aftermath of the stampede. Simba was likely aware of what had happened, considering his Big "NO!" when Mufasa fell, so this scene comes more from denial.
Simba: Dad?...Dad, c'mon... you've gotta get up. Dad... we've gotta go home.

tropes.name: Plummet Perspective
tropes.html: Several times stones are shown falling off a cliff for effect.

tropes.name: Poor Communication Kills
tropes.html: When Mufasa's spirit confronts Simba during his Heroic BSoD, he simply tells him that he has "forgotten who he is" and must retake his place in the Circle of Life as the true king. While this does convince Simba to go back and confront Scar, it doesn't relieve Simba of the grief he feels from falsely believing he caused his father's death in the first place, and Scar uses this against him by forcing him to "confess" in front of the rest of the pride, turning everyone else against Simba. This could have been avoided if Mufasa hadn't been so vague with his guidance and told Simba that Scar was the one who actually killed him, not Simba. While there are various theories as to why he didn't (or perhaps even couldn't) tell him more, and the strongest is that he was afraid telling him the truth would make Simba go back for revenge rather than to take his place in the Circle (and so not grow as a character), leaving it unsaid was still a huge risk, as it left him open to the above emotional manipulation.

tropes.name: Pop-Star Composer
tropes.html: Elton John not only composed the songs for the film, but he also sang his own version of "Can You Feel the Love Tonight", as featured in the ending credits.

tropes.name: Population Control
tropes.html: Cleverly implied. Mufasa was a wise king, and learned 'the circle of life' means balance of predators, prey and the land's resources, and a king must understand, respect and maintain that balance. Scar on the other hand does not. In elevating the hyenas from scavengers to apex predators he creates an unholy union that overwhelms their food source. To sustain them, the prey must breed like wildfire, consequently resulting in overgrazing, turning the lush Pridelands into an arid wasteland. Resources exhausted, the herds have no choice but to leave. Scar however refuses to abandon his kingdom (as that would mean he's no longer king), thus condemning his subjects to death by starvation.

tropes.name: Post-Game Retaliation
tropes.html: After Nala pins Simba for the first time, Simba glares at her in frustration over being easily beaten by her. Immediately after this when he sees she's distracted feeling proud of herself, he pounces on her from behind to get revenge, but this doesn't work out for him either when they accidentally roll down a nearby hill together, resulting in Nala pinning him again and smugly rubbing it in his face.

tropes.name: Post-Kiss Catatonia
tropes.html: Downplayed and in the form of Alternate Animal Affection. Towards the end of "Can You Feel The Love Tonight?", Simba and Nala accidentally tumble down a hill together, resulting in Simba pinning Nala, with the two sharing an amused laugh over it together. As Simba continues to chuckle to himself though, Nala smiles up at him and rewards him finally beating her with an affectionate lick on the cheek. This sudden act surprises Simba, with him glancing down at Nala in silence as he processes this. But when Nala just gazes up seductively at him, Simba quickly understands her intentions, with him smiling back and the two embracing each other as they nuzzle.

tropes.name: Pre-Asskicking One-Liner
tropes.html:
• Simba attempts to use one against Nala during one of their play fights as cubs. When the two of them are arguing over who deserves credit for the idea of losing Zazu and Nala counters every argument Simba makes, Simba just smirks at her deviously and remarks "Oh yeah?" right before pouncing on top of her with a tiny roar as a surprise attack, intending to pin her and make her give him the credit. It ends up subverted though, when Nala easily flips him over and he ends up pinned by her instead.
  • After having his Berserk Button pushed by being called a pig, Pumbaa angrily shouts, "They call me, MISTER PIG!", charges at Shenzi and Banzai with a Battle Cry, and delivers an offscreen No-Holds-Barred Beatdown on the two hyenas.

tropes.name: Predation Is Natural
tropes.html:
Mufasa explains to Simba that hunting and eating other animals is part of the Circle of Life.
Simba: But, Dad, don't we eat the antelope?
Mufasa: Yes, Simba, but let me explain. When we die, our bodies become the grass, and the antelope eats grass. So we are all connected in the great Circle of Life.

tropes.name: Predator Turned Protector
tropes.html: Simba fiercely protects his surrogate parents, Pumbaa and Timon, from the hungry Nala. In fact, Timon, initially reluctant to adopt the orphaned Simba due to him being a predator, changes his mind after he realizes he can exploit this trope.

tropes.name: Pregnancy Does Not Work That Way
tropes.html: A relatively small thing, but none of the cubs in either of the movies seem to be part of a litter. Though lionesses typically have small litters (usually just two or three cubs at a time) and having a single cub is certainly possible, to have all of these cubs being single births is quite bizarre.

tropes.name: Pre-Mortem One-Liner
tropes.html:
• Scar says, "Long live the king", before he sends Mufasa to his death.
  • Banzai and Shenzi say, "Ed?...", when they are going to kill Scar for his betrayal.

tropes.name: Previously Overlooked Paramour
tropes.html: Simba and Nala initially react to the notion of their betrothal with revulsion as cubs, since they are Just Friends. When they become adults, they realize that their familiarity as cubs makes them more compatible than they thought.

tropes.name: Princeling Rivalry
tropes.html: Mufasa as the strong first born, and Scar as the smart, plotting second born who has been jealous of Mufasa for some time. He doesn't begin his betrayal in earnest until after Mufasa's son is born. Scar murders Mufasa and attempts to kill Simba, Mufasa's child son. Simba lives and leads a charge to defeat Scar in his adult years.

tropes.name: Prodigal Hero
tropes.html: The film follows this with Simba, invoking Rightful King Returns since he was royalty before fleeing.

tropes.name: Proper Pinky
tropes.html: Scar frequently sticks his pinky out, part of the image he cultivates of refinement that barely conceals the underhandedness and eventual savagery that he descends to in the final act.

tropes.name: Protectorate
tropes.html: Mess with his family, his friends, or his homeland, and you'll get a lot of attention from Simba that you won't like.

tropes.name: "Psycho" Strings
tropes.html: During the song "Be Prepared", the hyenas "he-he-he-he-he" chanting in the middle of the song eerily resembles this.

tropes.name: Public Execution
tropes.html: When Simba returns to Pride Rock and confronts his Evil Uncle Scar, the wicked lion takes the opportunity to exploit his nephew's guilt about his supposed role in his father's demise with the intent of getting rid of Simba once and for all in front of the entire pride. Scar gives Simba a fierce accusatory speech that causes him to experience a Heroic BSoD and successfully corners him up to the top of Pride Rock, with the intent of throwing his nephew to his own demise as he did with Mufasa years ago. However, at that very moment, Scar chooses to reveal to his nephew that it was him who murdered Mufasa, filling Simba with righteous wrath and sealing his own fate in the process.

tropes.name: Punctuated!  For!  Emphasis!
tropes.html:
• As Scar is about to throw Mufasa to the stampede, he delivers the line "Long. Live. The king."
  • When he has Simba in a similar situation towards the end of the movie, he whispers "I. Killed. Mufasa."
  • Pumbaa's Pre-Asskicking One-Liner in response to Banzai calling him a pig. "They! Call! Me! MIS-ter Pig!"

tropes.name: Putting on the Reich
tropes.html:
The hyenas goose-stepping in grid formations. The animators based the sequence on Triumph of the Will. On top of that, Scar's rhetoric is right out of Hitler's mouth:
Scar: I will be king! Stick with me, and you'll NEVER GO HUNGRY AGAIN!!!

tropes.name: The Quest
tropes.html: After his father is murdered, Simba flees into exile. Guided by a wise mandrill and a pair of outcasts, he must overcome the temptation of a carefree life to return home, defeat his usurping uncle, and reclaim his rightful throne.

tropes.name: Quirky Miniboss Squad
tropes.html: The hyenas always show up together, but they have distinct personalities: Shenzi is bossy, Banzai is grumpy and Ed is dim-witted. But of course all three are prone to laughing at everything.

tropes.name: Quotes Fit for a Trailer
tropes.html:
A few weeks into its initial run, newspaper ads for the film quoted characters as if they were reviewers praising the film, e.g.:
"It's to die for!" —Scar
"Ooh, do it again!" —Shenzi

tropes.name: Rack Focus
tropes.html: The opening song of the movie, when the focus shifts from a line of leaf-cutter ants on a branch in the foreground to a herd of zebra thundering by below.

tropes.name: Rage Against the Heavens
tropes.html: After a brief fight with Nala about returning to the Pride Lands to take his place as king, an upset and conflicted Simba yells up to the skies where he knows his late father now rests ("You [Mufasa] always said you would be there for me! But you're not... and it's because of me. It's my fault").

tropes.name: Rage Against the Mentor
tropes.html:
Simba briefly has this towards his dead father, before it turns into rage against himself.
Simba: You said you'd always be there for me! But you're not. It's because of me. It's my fault. It's my fault.

tropes.name: Ragtag Band of Misfits
tropes.html: • The hyena trio consists of the wacky and sassy Shenzi, the grouchy Banzai, and the speechless but frequently laughing Ed.

tropes.name: Rays from Heaven
tropes.html: Clouds part to let streams of sunshine through onto the cub Simba when Rafiki holds him in the air during the opening of the movie. And on his daughter and her husband at the end of the movie.

tropes.name: Ready for Lovemaking
tropes.html: Downplayed but still present with Nala. At the end of her Falling-in-Love Montage with Simba during "Can You Feel the Love Tonight?", when he has her pinned down she surprises him with an affectionate lick on the cheek. When Simba looks down at her in surprise at this, she just gazes up at him seductively with a "come hither" look as he lays on top of her. Simba quickly gets the message and smiles back at her, with the two sharing a deep Held Gaze before nuzzling each other lovingly. It is also implied that they mated together off-screen after this, leading to Nala getting pregnant with their daughter.

tropes.name: Recruit the Muggles
tropes.html: The lionesses provide an animal version. They are victims of Scar's cruel misrule for most of the film, but rise up to help Simba fight it in the climax.

tropes.name: Recurring Camera Shot
tropes.html:
First it's Mufasa dangling from a cliff, later we see Simba in the exact same situation. Lampshaded by Scar:
"Hmm, where have I seen this before? Let me think. Hmm. Oh yes. I remember. This is just the way your father looked before he died."

tropes.name: Recycled with a Gimmick
tropes.html: The film is based on Hamlet, recycled in the Serengeti.

tropes.name: Red and Black and Evil All Over
tropes.html: Scar is an evil lion with reddish-orange fur and a black mane.

tropes.name: Redemption in the Rain
tropes.html: It's raining when Simba climbs Pride Rock at the end. A clear case of the rain being "purifying" and symbolizing new life, as the sequence includes a gazelle's skull being dislodged and washed away.

tropes.name: Refusal of the Call
tropes.html: Simba's call to action actually comes further into the film than usual when Nala finds him alive and tries to convince him to return to the Pride Lands in order to oust Scar from power and take his place as the rightful king. Because of his guilt over what he thinks he did to his father as well as him having embraced living a life with, "No worries, for the rest of your days" he initially refuses. However after meeting with Rafiki and the spirit of his father, Simba reconsiders it and finds the courage and will to put his past behind him and return to the Pride Lands to accept his responsibility.

tropes.name: Rejected Apology
tropes.html: Scar, when being confronted and stalked by the hyenas after they reveal they know that he tried to blame them for the plot to murder Mufasa and the attempted murder of a then-child Simba. As he tries to beg for mercy, one of the last things he cried out is “I’m sorry,” but all it does is make the hyenas jump him moments later and maul him to death.

tropes.name: Relative Button
tropes.html: Simba is losing the fight against Scar, and about to die, when Scar makes the mistake of boasting that he killed Mufasa the same way, resolving Simba's guilt about being the cause of Mufasa's death and giving him the Heroic Second Wind to turn the tables.

tropes.name: Reports of My Death Were Greatly Exaggerated
tropes.html: After going into Self-Imposed Exile over thinking he was responsible for Mufasa's death (he thought his roaring frightened a herd of wildebeests into the gorge when really, the hyenas chased them there and Scar killed Mufasa himself), everyone in the Pride Lands believes that Simba is dead. Even Scar assumes this, as the hyenas didn't tell him he got away from them. When he returns to take back the Pride Lands, everyone (barring Nala, who had already found out he was alive and Rafiki, who was the first to learn he was alive and convinced Simba to come back in the first place) at first thinks he is Mufasa's ghost.

tropes.name: Request for Privacy
tropes.html: After Mufasa saves Simba from the hyenas, he requests Zazu to take Nala home so he can talk to his son alone. Simba tries to hide upon hearing this, fearing what his father will do to him, and Zazu wishes him good luck. Mufasa then gives him a stern talking-to about how he's disappointed with his behavior and how he irresponsibly put Nala in danger.

tropes.name: Rescue Introduction
tropes.html: Timon and Pumbaa's first scene is them emerging out of nowhere to shoot away the buzzards that would've eaten Simba.

tropes.name: The Resenter
tropes.html:
• Scar resents Mufasa and Simba being ahead of him in line for the throne, believing he should get it instead and bearing ill will against both of them because of it.
    "I was first in line - until the little hairball was born."
  • Also the hyenas toward the lions, the latter forcing the former to live on the outskirts of the Pridelands in the Elephant Graveyard due to their tendency to over-indulge in eating and their general bullying sadism. They turn to Scar to change things in their favor, but their cooperation in aiding in the regicide leads to them eating all the resources, leading to an even worse situation than before and ultimately getting fed up with Scar long before he attempts to throw them under the bus by framing them for Mufasa’s murder to avoid Simba’s righteous wrath, being the last straw.

tropes.name: Restrained Revenge
tropes.html: Downplayed and played for laughs; during "Can You Feel The Love Tonight" Simba pulls Nala into the oasis, which she is visibly shocked by. After getting out, she grins at Simba and playfully shoves him back in as revenge before running off. This is then followed by Simba chasing her into the forest, leading to them playfully wrestling like when they were cubs and Simba finally managing to beat Nala by pinning her, putting an end to her winning streak against him. The two just chuckle at this series of events before realizing they have fallen in love with each other.

tropes.name: Reverse Psychology
tropes.html: Scar implores Simba not to visit the elephant graveyard and tells him that only the bravest of lions dare to go there, knowing full well that Simba's ego and curiosity will get the better of him.

tropes.name: Revised Ending
tropes.html: The original ending to the movie would've had Scar actually throw Simba off Pride Rock at the end of the fight (after Simba tries to save his life). Scar then dies laughing hysterically as the fires surrounding Pride Rock engulf it, burning him to death. Simba survived the fall (ironically meaning Scar throwing him off Pride Rock saved his life) and then meets up with Nala after the fires are put out. This was changed as the filmmakers felt this wouldn't have really brought Scar to justice for his actions.

tropes.name: Ribcage Ridge
tropes.html: The elephant graveyard is filled with elephant bones, mainly ribcages, often used as terrain.

tropes.name: Right Behind Me
tropes.html: Scar doesn't realize the hyenas are close enough to hear him tell Simba that the hyenas were the real enemies. Unusually for this trope, Scar doesn't immediately find out they were right there. It's revealed to him a few minutes later when they decide to kill him.

tropes.name: Rightful King Returns
tropes.html: After being convinced to return and claim his birthright, Simba engages King Scar in an epic Final Battle and defeats him. Then he climbs Pride Rock and majestically roars, cementing his destiny as king.

tropes.name: Risqué Animal Business
tropes.html: The movie is basically Hamlet in lion form, making it one of Disney's darkest films. It's still Lighter and Softer than the play and ends on a happier marriage, but it's a relatively somber film featuring Sibling Murder, aversions to Carnivore Confusion, and generally dark themes; earlier scripts were even darker. The "Can You Feel The Love?" sequence is also rather sexual laced, with Nala's bedroom eyes and the sensual licking, and it's been confirmed that Nala and Simba did mate during that sequence, with the heavy implication that this is when their daughter was conceived.

tropes.name: Royal Harem
tropes.html: G Rated version. The lion king lives surrounded by females to mate with. They also qualify for Amazon Brigade, since they're the ones doing most of the hunting. Truth in Television in regard to lion behavior.

tropes.name: Rule of Cool
tropes.html: The ground rising up beneath Scar in the last verse of "Be Prepared" doesn't really make any sense, but looks quite epic.

tropes.name: Rule of Sexy
tropes.html: Zigzagged with Rule of Funny. From the standpoint of trichophilia, the ending of Hakuna Matata, where Adult Simba gets his mane completely drenched, shakes it dry (to the point it fluffs into a humongous ball of hair), and floats down back to normal on its own, functions on this. Even Cinema Wins used a clip of this very short scene twice in their Everything Great About The Lion King video when referring to “[Simba’s] sexy lion locks”. It also helps that Adult Simba has a smolder on his face during this scene and that he is rather studly for a lion. Unironically, Pumbaa makes soft trumpet noises during this moment.

tropes.name: Rule of Symbolism
tropes.html:
• Intentional or not, some Christian audiences have interpreted many parts of the film as this. There's Simba's apparent resurrection—Nala says to him "It's like you're back from the dead" and is informed "The King has returned" in a manner rather reminiscent of Mary Magdalene in the garden with the open tomb, and both Scar and Sarabi think he is his father come back from the dead. There's the Fisher King analogy, with Simba's fight with Scar being easily related to Jesus combating Satan after his Second Coming. There's Simba's anointment by Rafiki (who also then blesses him by (almost) shoving his head in the water—and note he's a "crazy wild man" who acts as a "voice in the wilderness"), his reluctance to do his father's will, and Mufasa's divine image declaring Simba his son and the true king.
  • Simba’s venturing into the Elephant Graveyard and the subsequent roaring in the gorge leading to the stampede that kills his father—both prompted by Scar’s manipulation, leading to Simba’s self-imposed exile into the desert and later, Timon and Pumbaa’s home to live carefree without responsibility—is akin to how Adam and Eve were manipulated by the Devil into eating the Forbidden Fruit and being cast out of the Garden of Eden to toil in the harsh world, having committed the Original Sin.
  • Scar allying with the hyenas and later transforming the Pridelands into Mordor as a byproduct of his thematically unholy alliance of hyenas and lions, brings up the symbolism of how Lucifer turned against God and with the aid of the demons he corrupted from the angels that followed his ideology, would corrupt mankind and the world into his warped image till the Messiah returns.
  • The story of Moses is heavily referenced, in that Simba, the would-be king, is driven into the desert where he spends years trying to forget his past while living with the local people he develops a close bond with—people who ultimately aid him when he returns for his mission—until a God-like apparition appears and tells him to liberate his homeland.
  • Scar is killed by being thrown into a fiery chasm of his own making and then eaten by the hyenas he double crossed, akin to someone being thrown into hell and tortured by demons and how the Devil himself will be brought down to Hell after he loses to the Messiah.
  • The directors' commentary says that the drought during Scar's reign is this, quoting "The King restoreth the land!"
  • An example without the religious undertones, but still fraught with portent: the image of Simba's little paw stepping into his father's huge pawprint, that one he will one day fill as king. After much hardship, he does. The directors' commentary highlights it as the image that sums up the plot, to the point the remake used it on the first poster◊.
  • Another non-religious example: when cub Simba first flees the Pride Lands, he does so by crawling through the cramped spaces between the thorn bushes; these exact same motions occur later as an adult, and even framed the same way, when he has to crawl through the jungle to "follow old Rafiki". Since his exile was the beginning of him not only abandoning the Pride Lands and his role as future king but also him "forgetting who he is" (suppressing his trauma), it makes sense that he'd have to mirror his path to find himself and his role again—which he does literally, since as a cub he crawls from left to right, while as an adult he crawls from right to left.

tropes.name: Rump Roast
tropes.html: Zazu is captured by the hyenas and shoved into a geyser dubbed "the birdie boiler" during our heroes' first encounter with them, launching him through the air like a rocket. "No! Not the birdie boiler!"

tropes.name: Running Gag
tropes.html: Simba's complete inability to beat Nala in a fight. She beats him twice in a row as cubs, even when he was the first to pounce, and later as adults he gets pinned through the same trick. It's even given a Continuity Nod in the sequel. The only time Simba ever was able to beat Nala was by complete accident, landing on top of her after tumbling down a hill together and finally pinning her.

tropes.name: Russian Reversal
tropes.html: The hyenas comment on Simba being a king fit for a meal.

tropes.name: Sacrificial Lion
tropes.html: A literal example. Mufasa's death is the most dramatic moment of the film and shows that it's a much darker, adventurous story where people can die. This violation of the circle of life changes the rest of the film and Simba's journey to the throne. Scar's successful assassination of his brother also has lingering consequences for the rest of the franchise.

tropes.name: Sapient Eat Sapient
tropes.html:
• Part of Shenzi, Banzai and Ed’s failure to kill Simba and Nala is that they're too busy taunting them with their dinner plans to actually kill them.
  • Timon and Pumbaa save Simba only after agreeing that they can convince him not to eat them.
  • The only one even remotely upset with Nala's attempt to eat Pumbaa is Timon, and only for a moment. Though he is still afraid of her when she wakes him up.
  • While left ambiguous, it's implied the hyenas ate Scar after turning on him.

tropes.name: Saying Too Much
tropes.html: Scar "accidentally" lets slip to Simba that the forbidden area beyond the Pride Lands has an Elephant Graveyard (which, of course, piques Simba's interest) and laments the fact that he said too much...but not really, as it's part of his Batman Gambit to get Simba killed.

tropes.name: Say My Name
tropes.html:
• In the elephant graveyard, Nala calls out "Simba!" when she starts falling behind. Simba rushes back to save her from Shenzi.
  • Also Scar's yell of "SARABI!" when Simba returns to the Pridelands, before they realise he's still alive.

tropes.name: Scared of What's Behind You
tropes.html: Simba and Nala get trapped by the hyena trio while exploring the elephant graveyard. Simba tries to roar at them to scare them off, but only a little wimpy roar comes out, him being a cub and all. Amused, the hyenas encourage him to try again, and this time there's a huge, scary roar. The hyenas, Simba and the audience all have a moment to be shocked before Mufasa (obviously the real source of the second roar) jumps in to save the day.

tropes.name: Scavengers Are Scum
tropes.html: Lions seem to only hunt (in Real Life lions scavenge as well). The series avoids Carnivore Confusion by presenting this as a normal part of "the Circle of Life". Despite this hyenas are the antagonists of the first film, and are portrayed as the constantly hungry and brutish lackeys of Scar.

tropes.name: Scenery-Based Societal Barometer
tropes.html: Though the effects of the king's leadership extend all over the Pride Lands, the narrative remains focused primarily on Pride Rock itself. As such, the Rock serves a gauge for the health of the Pride lands as a whole: under Mufasa, the Rock is lit by bright sunshine under blue skies, and the surrounding area is lush and green; during Scar's tyrannical reign, the Rock has turned barren and the skies seem perpetually dark and overcast - reflecting the fact that the rest of the Pride Lands have been gripped by a massive famine. When Simba unseats Scar, the Rock is green and flourishing once again.

tropes.name: Scenery Gorn
tropes.html: The Pride Lands are absolutely destroyed by the end of Scar's rule. When Simba returns home to challenge him for the throne, it has been reduced to a barren, lifeless wasteland riddled with the carcasses of the hyenas' dead prey, with not one patch of grass or a drop of water to be seen for miles around; all of it the result of unchecked consumption on the part of both Scar and his minions, who have driven all the herds away that once inhabited the lush plains. Even more so during the final battle, where a lightning storm sets the land aflame before the rains come to end the destruction.

tropes.name: Scenery Porn
tropes.html: The movie features several lush scenes, sometimes even zooming out so the viewers can appreciate the landscapes in full. Examples include the scene when Mufasa explains "The Circle of Life" to Simba (when the two of them witness the whole horizon of Pride Lands during sunrise), and the scene when Nala and Simba walk across the beautiful falls and follies during their time together. Just how gorgeous the animation is is lampshaded in-world when Simba gets a good look at Timon and Pumbaa's jungle and responds in awe, "It's beautiful!"

tropes.name: Screams Like a Little Girl
tropes.html: Pumbaa when he sees adult Nala about to pounce on him. Although Pumbaa screams quite a bit in this movie, he lets out a high girlish scream among catching sight of Nala instead of how he normally yells.

tropes.name: Screw the Rules, I Make Them!
tropes.html:
• Scar during his reign as king. He plainly states "I am the king! I can do whatever I want!"
  • Simba had this attitude as a cub too, though in a much more innocent way. He believed as king he could make or get rid of any rules with nobody to tell him what to do. He mainly wanted to get rid of his betrothal to Nala since neither of them wanted to marry their best friend, and later said he would fire Zazu.

tropes.name: Self-Deprecation
tropes.html:
When Zazu is asked by Scar to sing a more upbeat song while imprisoned.
Zazu: Nobody knows the trouble I've seen. Nobody knows my sorrow...
Scar: Oh, Zazu, do lighten up. Sing something with a little...bounce in it.
Zazu: It's a small world after all—
Scar: NO! No. Anything but that!
  • In the Broadway stage version, Zazu instead sings "Be Our Guest", and gets the same reaction from Scar. This doubles as a Mythology Gag, since Beauty and the Beast, was the first Disney animated film that became a musical and paved the way for the Broadway version of Lion King. When Beauty and the Beast closed, it got replaced with "Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious", and other performances have him sing "Let It Go." Cast Members at Disney Theme Parks also love taking potshots at "It's A Small World" in general.

tropes.name: Self-Imposed Exile
tropes.html: Simba, on the "advice" of Scar, runs away from the Pridelands after he's convinced that he killed his father.

tropes.name: Self-Made Orphan
tropes.html: Scar subverts this trope by framing Simba for Mufasa's death.

tropes.name: Sequel Hook
tropes.html: The birth and presentation of Simba and Nala's cub at the end. Sure enough, the sequel is centered on Kiara, Simba's daughter.

tropes.name: Sexy Discretion Shot
tropes.html: "Can You Feel the Love Tonight?" all-but averts this, by having Simba and Nala flirt, play, and roll around in the grass, then lie next to each other looking all googly-eyed at each other. The creators have confirmed that the newborn cub at the end was conceived during this time.

tropes.name: Shadow Discretion Shot
tropes.html: The camera pans to Scar's shadow when the hyenas gang up on him. All the audience gets is a silhouette of him when the hyenas pounce him and eat him alive.

tropes.name: Shipper on Deck
tropes.html: • Zazu is pleased to see Simba and Nala spending time together, as the two are betrothed to one another. Mufasa, being the one who has arranged this, mentions that he considers Simba endangering Nala to be much worse than his disobedience.

tropes.name: Shout-Out
tropes.html:
• To Hamlet: Scar talks briefly to the skull of a prey in what seems like a shout-out to the famous "Alas poor Yorrick" scene in Hamlet.
  • To In the Heat of the Night:
    Pumbaa: THEY CALL ME MR. PIG!
  • Pumbaa's repeated line of "Are you talking to me?" is reminiscent of Robert De Niro's in Taxi Driver.
  • There's a more subtle one as well: Timon riding Pumbaa out of a desert mirage in a manner very reminiscent of Don Quixote.
  • A quick, rather flippant one: While Scar is signing 'Lovely Bunch of Coconuts', he holds up a baboon skull and moves its jaw to the lyrics. While the context is very different from the original play, one can't help but be reminded by the Shakespearian inspiration of the film.

tropes.name: Shown Their Work
tropes.html:
• Yes, lion cubs can and do eat bugs, and live off them if necessary. (Though it's much more of a stretch to imagine an adult lion living off them).
  • The fight between Simba and Scar (rearing up and furiously cuffing each other) is based off of how male lions actually fight, as their manes provide some protection to the neck. The way they only swing one paw at a time is also accurate. Lions will hit with one paw and use the other for balance or support. Tigers use both at the same time.
  • Shenzi leads Banzai and Ed, and appears to hold high authority among the other hyenas in the climax. In Real Life, spotted hyenas have a complex matriarchal society: each hyena clan is led by a dominant female, and males are smaller and weaker than females.
  • Zazu briefly mentions elephants getting annoyed at tick birds pecking at them. Contrary to popular belief, tick birds/oxpeckers are thought by many zoologists to actually be parasitic birds that are really after an animal's blood (they typically eat ticks that are already bloated with blood, which seems contradictory to their supposed duties as custodians) and even when they do seem to be trying to help, it's clear from their hosts' reactions that they don't appreciate it. Elephants have actually been reported to try and dislodge tick birds, in fact, an occurrence which Zazu may well be referring to.

tropes.name: Sibling Murder
tropes.html: Scar kills his brother Mufasa to take over the Pridelands. He even makes his nephew Simba believe he killed his father and lets him run away, though Simba doesn't end up dying like expected and comes back after a Time Skip.

tropes.name: Sic 'Em
tropes.html:
As soon as Simba runs away on his Self-Imposed Exile, the hyena trio appear behind Scar:
Scar: Kill him.

tropes.name: Sickly Green Glow
tropes.html: Much of "Be Prepared" and the dialogue leading up to it is suffused with lime green light, before changing to a hellish red as the song comes to the final chorus.

tropes.name: Sidekick Song
tropes.html: "Hakuna Matata", sung by the main character as well.

tropes.name: Significant Name Shift
tropes.html: While little Simba was always excited to hang out with "Uncle Scar", grown-up Simba is furious at how Scar corrupted the Pride Lands and no longer calls him "Uncle". Strangely, he no longer calls his mother and father “Mom” and “Dad”, either.

tropes.name: Silence Is Golden
tropes.html: The movie only features two simple lines of dialogue in its final non-musical scene — the Arc Words "It is time" from Rafiki, and "Remember" from Mufasa. Originally Zazu would've greeted Simba as "your majesty", but the filmmakers agreed the scene worked best with minimal if any dialogue, and cut the line.note It was cut so late, however, that Zazu's mouth still visibly mouths the line in the final product. There was also no dialogue during Simba's presentation (aside from the "Circle of Life" number).

tropes.name: Silence, You Fool!
tropes.html:
Mufasa, when he encounters the hyena trio at the elephant graveyard to rescue his son Simba and Nala from them.
Shenzi: Oh, please, please. Uncle, uncle.
Banzai: Ow, ow, ow.
Mufasa: Silence!
Banzai: Oh, we’re gonna shut up right now.
Shenzi: Calm down. We’re really sorry.

tropes.name: Sky Face
tropes.html: Simba sees his deceased father's face in the night sky, telling him, "Remember who you are. You are my son, and the one true king."

tropes.name: Slasher Smile
tropes.html: One of the hyenas during Scar's final scene, complete with Blank White Eyes.

tropes.name: Sliding Scale of Anthropomorphism
tropes.html: Animals are anthropomorphised to varying extents. This even varies with animals of the same species — compare Timon with the meerkats that appear in the opening of "Circle of Life".

tropes.name: Small Role, Big Impact
tropes.html: The random chameleon that just happens to be passing by when Simba is considering practicing his roar, which he then does on the chameleon, seemingly alarming the wildebeest and thus (in Simba's mind) kicking off the point when things go south for him.

tropes.name: Smooch of Victory
tropes.html: During "Can You Feel The Love Tonight" Nala surprises Simba with a lick on the cheek after he finally pins her and the two begin to nuzzle shortly afterwards, the animal style of kissing.

tropes.name: Smug Smiler
tropes.html:
Downplayed. The first time Nala pins Simba, she giggles and playfully teases him "pinned ya", but after he tries pouncing her again and they roll down a hill, she once again beats him and smirks down at him and teases him for losing again, more smug than playful.
Nala: Pinned ya again.

tropes.name: Smug Snake
tropes.html: Scar certainly loves to think that he's a Magnificent Bastard, but as smart as he is, he tends to be a little too impulsive and openly cruel for his own good. He also had absolutely no idea what he was doing during his time as king.

tropes.name: Something Only They Would Say
tropes.html: A non-verbal example occurs when Simba first encounters Nala as an adult. When she uses her trademark flip-and-pin move on him, he realizes her identity.

tropes.name: Sore Loser
tropes.html: When Simba and Nala are arguing over who deserves credit for losing Zazu, Simba pounces on top of Nala after she counters all his arguments, but ends up easily flipped and pinned by her. After she playfully teases him for his loss, he shoves her off him and tells her to let him up and glares at her silently, embarrassed over getting beaten by her in a fight that he started. Once she turns her back to him, he immediately tries to get revenge by pouncing on her from behind while she's distracted, essentially resorting to cheating. When Nala pins him again anyway despite this and smugly rubs it in his face, all he can do is silently glare at her in defeat.

tropes.name: Soundtrack Dissonance
tropes.html: While "Be Prepared" is an ominous song overall, the hyenas' counterpoint melody ("We'll have food/Lots of food/We repeat/Endless meat!") is sung in a major key and would on its own sound cheerful.

tropes.name: So Unfunny, It's Funny
tropes.html:
• This is the main appeal of Timon's character. His jokes are so lame you can't help but chuckle- this was intentional of course.
    Pumbaa: What's eating you, kid?
    Timon: Nothing, he's at the top of the food chain! Hahaha!!! The food chain! Ha ha ha ha... [realizes that his joke has failed]
  • And later:
    Simba: What's a motto?
    Timon: Nothing. What's a motto with you?
  • Shenzi and Banzai also get a few of these earlier on.
    Banzai: I'll having whatever's lion around.
    Shenzi: Wait, I've got one — make mine a cub sandwhich.

tropes.name: Spared by the Adaptation
tropes.html: If the film is taken as an adaptation of Hamlet, then the equivalents of Hamlet himself (Simba), Gertrude (Sarabi), Polonius (Zazu), Laertes (Shenzi, Banzai and Ed) and Rosencrantz and Guildenstern (Timon and Pumbaa), all live, whereas the play has them all die in the end. Zigzagged with Nala, as she’s a Composite Character based on Ophelia and Horatio: Ophelia died, while Horatio was the only main character to survive.

tropes.name: Spirit Advisor
tropes.html: Mufasa becomes one of the "great kings of the past" and advises his son on the responsibilities of his birthright from beyond the grave.

tropes.name: Staredown Faceoff
tropes.html: While Simba and Nala are fighting each other in the jungle, the two at one point briefly pause from fighting to stare each other down while growling at each other. After a moment though, Nala ends the staredown by clawing at Simba's mane, briefly covering his eyes, and the fight continues.

tropes.name: Stargazing Scene
tropes.html: Simba, Timon and Pumbaa spend a night staring at the stars and wondering exactly what they're made of. Timon guesses fireflies, Pumbaa guesses they're "giant balls of gas", and Simba mentions the story he was taught as a cub, that stars are really the ancient kings of the past watching over them, showing how he still hasn't fully moved on from his past.

tropes.name: Stars Are Souls
tropes.html: Simba says he was taught that the stars are the spirits of the old kings, which gets a confirmation when he later receives a starry vision of his father. Timon, on the other hand, claims that stars are fireflies that got stuck in the sky. That also got confirmed... by The Princess and the Frog.

tropes.name: Stealth Insult
tropes.html:
• This exchange between Simba and Scar:
    Simba: When I'm king, what'll that make you?
    Scar: A monkey's uncle.
  • This bit when Shenzi, Bandai and Ed notice Scar.
    Banzai: Oh Scar. It's just you.
    Shenzi: We were afraid it was somebody important.

tropes.name: Steamrolled Smart Guy
tropes.html: Zazu tries to teach a young Simba about the responsibilities of being a king. Simba is completely disinterested in these lessons. Zazu shows his frustration with birdlike screeches and squawks as he tries to keep Simba's attention.

tropes.name: Stink Snub
tropes.html: In one scene, the hyenas are spitefully listing things they don't like about the lions and Shenzi calls them "stinky”.

tropes.name: Stopped Dead in Their Tracks
tropes.html: Trickster Mentor Rafiki taunts the exiled Simba by saying that he knows who he is. Simba, who thinks Rafiki is just a "creepy little monkey", starts to leave when Rafiki says, "You're Mufasa's boy!" Simba stops and looks back at Rafiki, who just says, "Bye!" and runs off, leading the now curious Simba to follow him.

tropes.name: Strike Me Down with All of Your Hatred!
tropes.html:
Scar attempts invoking this on Simba during the climax, but despite being tempted to kill him for Mufasa's murder, Simba ultimately refuses, asserting that he won't sink low as Scar.
Scar: What are you going to do? You wouldn't kill your own uncle?
Simba: No, Scar. I'm not like you.

tropes.name: Stunned Silence
tropes.html: After Nala flips and pins Simba for the first time, Simba is so shocked by this that he looks up at Nala with wide eyes and a dropped jaw, unable to say anything. After Nala chuckles at him and playfully teases him for his loss though, he quickly overcomes his shock and rudely tells her to get off him while pushing her off. Simba has the same reaction years later when Nala pins him again, staring up at her in shock realizing who she is. After a moment of silence where she holds him down while growling at him, he says her name in shock, surprising her into getting off him.

tropes.name: Subverted Rhyme Every Occasion
tropes.html:
Pumbaa: And I got down-hearted...
Timon: How did you feel?!
Pumbaa: Every time that I—
Timon: Pumbaa! Not in front of the kids!

tropes.name: Surprisingly Bad Native Language
tropes.html: Rafiki's Swahili chant "Asante sana, squash banana, we we nugu mi mi apana" which he translates as "You are a baboon, and I'm not.", is not grammatically correct.

tropes.name: Surrounded by Idiots
tropes.html: Scar says this exact quote about the hyenas. Interestingly, he said this about said hyenas playing their species' trope straight, more specifically them goofing around with Banzai saying Mufasa's name to Shenzi's delight, and not the mission they had recently failed.

tropes.name: Sustained Misunderstanding
tropes.html:
Nala: Have you guys seen Simba?
Timon: I thought he was with you.
Nala: He was but now I can't find him. Where is he?
Rafiki: [chuckles] You won't find him here. The King has returned.
Nala: I can't believe it. He's gone back!
Timon: "Gone back?" Whaddaya mean?
[looks up and sees Rafiki has disappeared]
Timon: Hey, what's going on here? Who's the monkey?
Nala: Simba's gone back to challenge Scar.
Timon: Who?
Nala: Scar.
Pumbaa: Who's got a scar?
Nala: No, no, no. It's his uncle.
Timon: The monkey's his uncle?
Nala: No! Simba's gone back to challenge his uncle to take his place as king.
Timon and Pumbaa: [beat] Oh.

tropes.name: Switching P.O.V.
tropes.html: The scenes leading up to the wildebeest stampede seem to be from the perspective of Scar and the hyenas, but just before it begins, it shifts to Simba's perspective. The wildebeests arrive right after he pulls off a loud and impressive roar, making it appear as if his roar frightened the wildebeests into the gorge, leading up to Mufasa's death.

tropes.name: Take a Moment to Catch Your Death
tropes.html:
• Mufasa successfully saves Simba from being trampled to death by a stampeding herd of wildebeest provoked by Scar and the hyenas. However, shortly after getting Simba to safety, Scar arrives and tosses Mufasa off the cliff Mufasa was trying to climb and into the gorge below, killing him.
  • After seeing Mufasa plunge to his death, you would think a similar thing would happen to Scar. He survives the fall, but not the angry horde of hyenas waiting below.

tropes.name: Talks Like a Simile
tropes.html: When Zazu's intervention lets the field mouse Scar was going to eat escape, Scar dryly notes, "Now look, Zazu, you made me lose my lunch." Zazu replies, "You'll lose more than that when the king gets through with you! He's as mad as a hippo with a hernia."

tropes.name: Tastes Like Chicken
tropes.html: Timon says this phrase word-for-word while eating a grub as big as himself in the middle of "Hakuna Matata".

tropes.name: Tempting Fate
tropes.html:
• "Danger? I walk on the wild side! I laugh in the face of danger! Ha ha ha!" Cue the hyenas laughing back...
  • When Simba roars at the hyenas, Shenzi taunts him into doing it again. Then Mufasa shows up...

tropes.name: That Reminds Me of a Song
tropes.html: Many fans old enough to remember when The Lion King first came to DVD find that "Morning Report" was an unneeded addition to the film, since the movie didn't have it originallynote and as such, the animation is distractingly different to the rest of the film, nor in prints and home video releases struck from 2011 onward. It isn't a terrible song, nor completely irrelevant (it's in the stage versions of the movie, too), but it didn't exactly advance the plot or provide much (if any) character development.

tropes.name: There's No Place Like Home
tropes.html: Simba runs away from home following his father's tragic death. Though he enjoys his time with Timon and Puumba, reuniting with an adult Nala makes him feel guilty for running away. He eventually does come back home, defeats his evil uncle (who, it turns out, orchestrated his brother's murder), and takes his rightful spot as king.

tropes.name: They Call Me MISTER Tibbs!
tropes.html:
• When Simba says "Banana Beak is scared", Zazu says "It's MISTER Banana Beak to you, fuzzy!"
  • Pumbaa does NOT like being called a "pig" (at least, not by strangers), and when the hyenas do so towards the end, he says "They call me MISTER PIG!" before kicking their butts.

tropes.name: They Died Because of You
tropes.html: Right after murdering Mufasa, Scar tells Simba that he's responsible for Mufasa's "accidental" death.

tropes.name: Think of the Censors!
tropes.html:
during "Hakuna Matata":
Pumbaa: And I got downhearted / Every time that I...
Timon: Wait, Pumbaa! Not in front of the kids!
Pumbaa: Oh! Sorry...

tropes.name: Third Wheel
tropes.html: Timon and Pumbaa certainly become third wheels once Simba and Nala meet up again. Simba kind of politely lets Timon know that the two of them aren't wanted.

tropes.name: This Bear Was Framed
tropes.html: Scar uses stampeding wildebeests to murder Mufasa — an odd example of an animal using other animals to make the murder of another animal look like an (accidental) animal attack.

tropes.name: This Cannot Be!
tropes.html:
Inverted: when Simba arrives just in time to witness Scar fighting with his mother Sarabi, he steps in to protect her. A terrified Scar replies to that with "Mufasa? No. You're dead." And he's right. Earlier on in the film, Scar killed Mufasa by shoving him back into the wildebeest stampede, therefore resulting in his death. With Simba's return, Scar ends up mistaking him for Mufasa until he reveals to his mother that he's her son, causing Scar to be both relieved to know he's correct and surprised to know that Simba is indeed alive.
Scar: Simba? Simba! I'm a little surprised to see you... [angrily looks at the hyenas] alive? [the hyenas gulp and back away]

tropes.name: This Is Gonna Suck
tropes.html:
• Mufasa is angry at Simba after needing to save him at the elephant graveyard and says he needs to teach his son a lesson. Simba cowers and hesitates before coming to his father's side. Even Mufasa himself has this feeling before he scolds Simba, judging by the pained look in his eyes.
  • Timon points this out to Pumbaa after realizing Simba is more interested in Nala than them.
  • Scar famously has this reaction when his entire hyena army confront him about him calling them “the enemy”.

tropes.name: This Is Unforgivable!
tropes.html: Simba says "You don't deserve to live" to Scar as soon as he corners him after hitting him with a "Murderer" to which Scar had responded with "Simba, Simba, please. Please have mercy. I beg you."

tropes.name: Those Two Guys
tropes.html: Timon and Pumbaa are close friends, contrast each other visually and personality-wise, and act as comic relief in an otherwise fairly serious story. They generally provide funny comments, such as singing about how they are aghast that Simba and Nala have reunited in "Can You Feel the Love Tonight".<!--** Banzai and Ed-->

tropes.name: Throw 'Em to the Wolves
tropes.html: Played with. After being thrown off a cliff by Simba, Scar apparently survives the fall. Although Simba never intended to kill his uncle, his act of self-defence still sealed his relative's fate. In fact, a cornered Scar finds out his "friends" the hyenas were ready to finish him off.

tropes.name: Title-Only Chorus
tropes.html: "Can't Wait to be King".

tropes.name: Toilet Humour
tropes.html: During the "Can't Wait to be King" number, a parade of zebras turn their bottoms towards Zazu and lift their tails. Zazu understandably cowers from what is potentially about to be dumped on him!

tropes.name: Tomboy Princess
tropes.html: Nala (although she's never called a princess), as seen when she play-wrestles with Simba on her way to an elephant graveyard with him. That far into the movie, they're just friends (and they don't take seriously the idea that they'd grow up to be more than friends) and you could almost forget they're opposite genders if not for the voices. The Lion King has its protagonist and princess more similar to each other than most Disney movies do. Her rebellious, boisterous young daughter Kiara is another example, especially as Nala matures and becomes more regal. It helps that both characters are lionesses, who hunt and fight by nature.

tropes.name: Too Clever by Half
tropes.html: Scar schemes to take the throne, believing himself to be smarter than his brother, Mufasa, and actually succeeds in doing so without anyone suspecting he played a role in Mufasa's death. The only real hole in Scar's plot, unbeknownst to him, is that the hyenas failed to kill Simba, but the young lion is still ashamed and runs away. However, after the Time Skip, it becomes clear that while Scar is certainly a cunning schemer, he puts no thought into being an actual ruler. In a few years under his rule, Pride Rock has fallen into ruin, the lions are running out of food, and even the hyenas who had been loyal to Scar, are about ready to revolt, and eventually turn on him, literally ripping him to shreds after he tries to blame them for the coup. It seems that Mufasa was much smarter than Scar gave him credit for. Or at least, Mufasa was much wiser than Scar.

tropes.name: Too Dumb to Live
tropes.html: Scar really shouldn't have lied to Simba about Mufasa's death by blaming it on the hyenas. He pays for it dearly.

tropes.name: Toxic Friend Influence
tropes.html:
• Timon and Pumbaa, while helpful in raising Simba and bringing him out of misery, convince him to ignore his past and responsibilities. Justified in that they didn't know he was the king; when Timon finds out, he wants to know why Simba didn't tell them. He and Pumbaa also come to Pride Rock to help Simba take it back, because he's family.
  • Had Mufasa not lectured Simba for going into the elephant graveyard, it’s highly likely he could’ve eventually become this to Nala.

tropes.name: Translated Cover Version
tropes.html: The songs got this in many countries. In the French version, Scar's voice actor Jean Piat also famously did his singing for "Be Prepared".

tropes.name: Travel Montage
tropes.html: There's the "Circle of Life" musical sequence at the very beginning of the movie showing the animals' journey to Pride Rock to view Simba's christening ceremony. Another example shows up near the end when an adult Simba runs across the desert back to Pride Rock so he can challenge his Evil Uncle Scar for the throne.

tropes.name: Triggered by the Name
tropes.html: One of the many changes Scar brings on to the Pride Lands is the name of the previous King, Mufasa, is forbidden to be uttered. Scar reacts to it by Suddenly Shouting at the sayer.

tropes.name: Truck Driver's Gear Change
tropes.html:
• "Circle of Life" begins in B-flat major, then shifts to D-flat for the last part of the final chorus.
  • "I Just Can't Wait to Be King" starts in G-flat major, then shifts up to G for the final verse.
  • "Can You Feel the Love Tonight" begins in F major, shifting up to G for the final chorus and outro.

tropes.name: Turn the Other Cheek
tropes.html: Once Simba and Nala recognize each other, Simba instantly forgives her for trying to eat his friends. Pumbaa is also instantly forgiving and happily introduces himself. Timon is the only one who is confused by this sudden turn of events and does not immediately trust Nala.

tropes.name: Two-Act Structure
tropes.html: The first half of the movie is about Simba's childhood and Scar's plot to become King. The second half is adult Simba coming to terms with his guilt and grief and deciding to reclaim his throne from Scar. The musical similarly follows this thread by ending Act 1 with Hakuna Matata and the reveal of Adult Simba.

tropes.name: Tyrannicide
tropes.html: At the end of the movie it is implied that the tyrannical Scar is killed (and devoured) by his own starving hyena henchmen.

tropes.name: Tyrant Takes the Helm
tropes.html: The movie's main plot is set off when Scar "reluctantly" assumes the Pride Lands' throne after murdering Mufasa to get it, and begins his Nazi-esque hyena regime. Within the span of a few years, he runs the Pride Lands into the ground, and even the hyenas who serve him agree that Mufasa was a much better king than Scar ever was — though not within earshot of Scar.

tropes.name: Underestimating Badassery
tropes.html: As cubs, Simba tries to pounce on Nala after they get into an argument over who deserves credit for the two of them losing Zazu, with Simba trying to give himself credit for both the plan and pulling it off but Nala saying it was her idea and he pulled it off with her. After pouncing Nala, she easily flips Simba and pins him with almost no effort, much to his shock and embarrassment. After shoving her off him he tries to pounce her again while she isn't looking but after sending them over a hill she ends up pinning him once again, and smugly rubs it in his face.

tropes.name: Undying Loyalty
tropes.html:
Zazu and Rafiki display unwavering loyalty to the royal family. Timon and Pumbaa develop the same loyalty through their friendship with Simba.
Timon: Well Simba, if it's important to you, we're with you to the end!

tropes.name: Unintended Kinslayer
tropes.html: While the audience sees Scar very intentionally killing his brother Mufasa, he frames it in a way to make Simba think he’d caused his father's death by stampede by accident, pressuring him into running away as an exile out of fear nobody would believe it was an accident... then Scar sics the hyenas on his nephew just to cover his bases. Simba would live with the apparent guilt of his actions until he grows up to face off against Scar, where Simba would learn he wasn't responsible at all.

tropes.name: Unsportsman Like Gloating
tropes.html: Downplayed with Nala teasing Simba after pinning him as cubs. During their brief scuffle, after Nala flips Simba over, she lets out a brief triumphant "Ha!" right before slamming him down. The first time she beats him she chuckles and playfully teases him "Pinned ya" with a big smile, showing it's in good fun. After he pushes her off him though she has a smug victorious smile on her face and turns away from him while holding her head high, clearly feeling proud of herself for her victory against Simba. After she immediately beats him again after he pounces her again, she smirks down at him and taunts him "Pinned ya again" in a more smug and arrogant voice than her previous playful one. Possibly justified as Simba had previous tried to take credit for her ideanote Though it might actually not have been HER idea and he was the one who started both of the fights, but still noticeable as Simba is her best friend and was prince at the time.

tropes.name: Vengeance Denied
tropes.html: Played for Laughs with Simba and his best friend Nala. After Nala beats Simba in a playfight, pinning him down and teasing him for it, Simba pushes her off him and glares at her bitterly for it. Immediately afterwards though, he realizes she's distracted feeling proud of herself and pounces on her while her back is turned to get revenge. This backfires when he accidentally sends them tumbling down a nearby hill, resulting in Nala once again flipping and pinning him, smugly rubbing her victory in his face while all he can do is pout at her.

tropes.name: Verbal Backspace
tropes.html:
A few examples:
  • When Scar is king, Zazu and Banzai have to back up from mentions of Mufasa, which Scar has forbidden.
  • Then at the end, Scar has to defend himself from the hyenas, whom he tried to scapegoat while bargaining for his life against Simba. They were too enraged and hungry to listen to him.

tropes.name: Verbal Deflection
tropes.html: After Scar confesses to murdering Mufasa, Simba confronts him atop Pride Rock. Knowing he's outclassed physically, Scar tries to pass off blame to the hyenas, claiming it was all their idea. Unfortunately, the hyenas overheard him, and after Scar is defeated, they enact their revenge.

tropes.name: Vertigo Effect
tropes.html: Used very effectively and iconically at the start of the wildebeest stampede, as Simba realizes they are heading straight for him.

tropes.name: Villain Decay
tropes.html: Scar starts out as a Manipulative Bastard that manipulates everybody and actually achieves his goal by usurping the throne. And after that he degrades into a whiny oaf, a terrible leader, and a Manchild, as he acts like an overgrown toddler. Granted, that's the entire point: Scar wants the title and privileges of being king, not the responsibilities, and indeed only becomes a threat again when he's challenged.

tropes.name: Villainous Badland, Heroic Arcadia
tropes.html: Scar and the hyenas lurk in the Elephant Graveyard, a grey, rocky wasteland filled with bones and massive skeletons and visible from Pride Rock as a patch of shadow on the horizon. Scar manages to turn the Pride Lands into a second version of this once he takes over — somehow, he's such a terrible ruler that the rain stops falling, the rivers dry up and all the animals leave; the first thing that happens when Simba kicks him out is that the rain starts falling again. A big part of the hyenas' motivation for following Scar to begin with is based on getting access to the Pride Lands and the abundant food there, which they normally can't get because the lions keep them out and their own home base has nothing to eat.

tropes.name: Villainous Glutton
tropes.html: The hyenas were driven away from the Pride Lands prior to the film both due to the species' apparently innate sadism and because their over-eating habits are capable of throwing off the balance of the circle of life. Once Scar usurps the throne and allows them to hunt freely in his kingdom, it only takes a few years for the lush fields to be replaced by a wasteland, rivers to dry out and prey populations to decay.

tropes.name: Villain Reveals the Secret
tropes.html: Scar exploits this trope to blame Simba for his father's death. Much to the latter's mother's horror and awe, the young lion publicly admits his crime. It turns out in the following Near-Villain Victory that Simba was innocent in the first place (well, the audience knew that since the first part of the movie).

tropes.name: Villain Recruitment Song
tropes.html: Much of the song "Be Prepared" is Scar persuading the hyenas to support him.

tropes.name: Villain Song
tropes.html: "Be Prepared" is a song about Scar's plans to take over the land.

tropes.name: Virtuous Character Copy
tropes.html: As the story is largely based on Hamlet, Timon and Pumbaa are based on Rosencrantz and Guildenstern. However, unlike their Hamlet counterparts, Timon and Pumbaa never betray their friend, the protagonist (Simba in The Lion King, Hamlet in Hamlet.) Instead, they are completely loyal to Simba.

tropes.name: Visual Pun
tropes.html: In "I Just Can't Wait to be King", Simba says that "I'm gonna be the mane event" while he has a mane of leaves on his face.

tropes.name: Vine Swing
tropes.html: Simba swings on vines, usually with his mouth, a few times.

tropes.name: Voodoo Shark
tropes.html: A common criticism is how the film tries to explain the lions living in harmony with the rest of the animals, despite the fact that the former constantly kills the latter for food. The explanation? When lions die, their bodies fertilise soil for grass, which herbivores eat. This has several problems: 1) Grass doesn't hunt lions down and decide when they die. Instead, the lions are allowed to die peacefully of natural causes. 2) The amount of grass one dead lion fertilises after its death is small compared to the number of animals one lion eats in its lifetime. 3) Lions aren't the only animals that decompose into fertiliser after death.

tropes.name: Walk Into Camera Obstruction
tropes.html: During the song "I Just Can't Wait to be King" where the giraffes are throwing Simba and Nala and Simba's stomach fills up the screen.

tropes.name: Was It All a Lie?
tropes.html: Invoked; when Scar cowers before Simba and says the hyenas made him kill Mufasa, Simba doesn't buy it. He growls, "Why should I believe you? Everything you told me was a lie." That includes professing he cared about Simba as a cub, blaming him for his father's death, and calling him a murderer.

tropes.name: Watch Out for That Tree!
tropes.html: During "I Just Can't Wait to be King," Zazu flies sideways when singing to Simba, "I think it's time that you and I arranged a heart-to-heart," and slams into a rhino.

tropes.name: Water-Geyser Volley
tropes.html: The hyenas put Zazu into "the birdie boiler", which rockets him, apparently, straight to Mufasa.

tropes.name: Water Is Dry
tropes.html: Downplayed. At the end of Hakuna Matata, Timon and Pumbaa show no signs of being soaked and seemed to have dried instantly. Meanwhile, an Adult Simba climbs out with his mane drenched, waterlogged, and draping his eyes. Even then, Simba focuses more on getting his mane completely dry instead of any other part of his body.

tropes.name: Weakness Is Just a State of Mind
tropes.html: Scar accuses the lionesses of not looking hard enough when his negligence in controlling the Hyenas results in the Pride Lands becoming deprived of food.

tropes.name: Weird Moon
tropes.html: There is a shot at night at Pride Rock where we see the moon and the horns of the crescent extending an average of three-quarters of a circle, essentially rendering Earth smaller than the moon.

tropes.name: "Well Done, Son" Guy
tropes.html: In an interesting variation, Simba becomes this for the second half of the movie. Although anything but an emotionally distant father, Mufasa is often preoccupied with the duties of the throne, and Simba certainly sees him as a hero, worshiping the ground his paws tread upon◊. But there is no indication Simba ever doubts he has his father's love or respect... until Scar convinces him he is to blame for his father's death. Then, overcome with remorse and believing no one could ever forgive him, he voluntarily goes into exile. It is Mufasa's ghost, chiding him for forgetting telling him "You are my son and the one true king," that sets him back on the right path again. And with a simple, single word, "Remember..." he lets his son know that while he was disappointed in him for abandoning the Pride Lands and forgetting who he used to be, as long as he is true to himself and who Mufasa raised him to be, his spirit will be very proud of him indeed.

tropes.name: We Need a Distraction
tropes.html:
When Simba, Nala, Timon and Pumbaa sneak back to Pride Rock they encounter a pack of hyenas blocking their way, leading to a classic Gilligan Cut.
Timon: Hyenas. I hate hyenas. So what's your plan for getting past those guys?
Simba: Live bait.
Timon: Good idea... [Beat] Hey!
Simba: C'mon, Timon, you guys have to create a diversion!
Timon: What do you want me to do, dress in drag and do the hula?
[Gilligan Cut to Timon doing exactly that]

tropes.name: Whack-a-Monster
tropes.html: During "The Morning Report" (a song added for the 2003 special edition), Simba uses his front claws to repeatedly clobber Gopher while he pops out of dirt holes.

tropes.name: Wham Line
tropes.html:
• When Scar shows up to feed the hyenas and chide them for not killing Simba or Nala. Banzai asks, "What were we supposed to do? Kill Mufasa?" Scar leans forward and smirks. "Precisely." Scar then starts explaining via "Be Prepared" his plan to get rid of Mufasa and Simba.
  • The hyenas approach Scar after Simba tosses him off Pride Rock. When he calls them friends, Shenzi laughs and says, "Friends? I thought he said we were the enemy." Cue a horde of hungry hyenas eating Scar alive.

tropes.name: What Happened to the Mouse?
tropes.html: Where did Scar's hyenas go after they ate him?

tropes.name: What Measure Is a Non-Cute?
tropes.html: While mammals and birds are shown to be intelligent and capable of speech and forming relationships, insects are treated like, well, insects, with the insectivores Timon and Pumbaa eating live insects at the same leisure as a herbivore eating grass.

tropes.name: What's a Henway?
tropes.html:
This bit from "Hakuna Matata":
Pumbaa: It's our motto!
Simba: What's a motto?
Timon: Nothing, what's a-motto with you?

tropes.name: What Song Was This Again?
tropes.html: "Be Prepared" gets changed a lot in foreign language dubs.

tropes.name: Where It All Began
tropes.html: The movie ends with Simba returning to the Pride Lands to defeat Scar and take his rightful place as king.

tropes.name: While Rome Burns
tropes.html: Under Scar's terrible reign, the Pridelands become a barren hellhole and everyone under his command is facing starvation. Even Scar's hyena minions grudgingly acknowledge that while Mufasa didn't like them, at least he was a far more competent ruler than his younger brother. Scar is fully prepared to let everyone drop dead instead of allowing them to leave all for the sake of preserving his hold on power, and if that weren't enough, the Pridelands actually do burn as a violent storm sets fire to the long-dead savannah surrounding his domain, and he isn't the least bit fazed by it as he prepares to murder Simba. In a nutshell, this trope essentially deconstructs Scar's bratty "I'm the king, I can do whatever I want" attitude, as he proved to be an incompetent king, and he even refuses to acknowledge for his disastrous reign out of pride. As a result, all of his subjects, including his hyena lackeys, despise him for this reason.

tropes.name: Who's on First?
tropes.html:
Nala's attempt to explain matters to Timon and Pumbaa after Simba decides to return home:
Timon: Hey, what's going on here? Who's the monkey?
Nala: Simba's gone back to challenge Scar.
Timon: Who?
Nala: Scar.
Pumbaa: Who's got a scar?
Nala: No, no, no. It's his uncle.
Timon: The monkey's his uncle?

tropes.name: Widely-Spaced Jail Bars
tropes.html: Scar has Zazu trapped in a cage that appears to be made of bones that it looks like he could easily walk right out of if he just tucked in his wings and sucked in his gut a little.

tropes.name: Winds of Change
