  • During their confrontation against the real Ranchodas, Farhan and Raju are clearly scared out of their wits of being held at gunpoint, but their desire to uncover the truth in regards to their Best Friend outweighs that fear enough to steal the urn that contains the ashes of Ranchodas' father as a hostage. They are also shown to be accepting to the revelation that their best friend's an impostor.

tropes.name: Two Aliases, One Character
tropes.html: The impostor known as "Ranchodas Chanchad" (the servant of the Chanchad family and Farhan and Raju's long-lost best friend) and Phunsukh Wangdu (the scientist that Chatur wants to sign an important deal for his business) are the same person. Phunsukh Wangdu is actually his true name.

tropes.name: Übermensch
tropes.html: Rancho openly defies all the systems of his university from day one, starting from standing up against an abusive senior up to clashing with the director himself. And he's a brilliant enough student to pull it off.

tropes.name: The Ugly Guy's Hot Daughter
tropes.html: Mentioned by Rancho when flirting with Pia, saying that her mother must've been so beautiful, because Pia is and... well, her dad isn't what you'd call handsome.

tropes.name: Unknown Rival
tropes.html: Chatur has always been hell-bent on defeating Rancho, but always fails. Rancho doesn't seems to care about Chatur though. He's attending ICE to learn, not to compete.

tropes.name: Walking Spoiler
tropes.html: Two walking spoilers, in fact. It is impossible to further discuss Rancho, the long-lost college friend of Farhan and Raju, without spoiling the fact that he is an impostor of the original Ranchodas Chanchad. Furthermore, the one who claims himself as Ranchodas Chanchad at Shimla is actually the real deal. This impersonation pretty much explains why the impostor cuts off all contact with his two closest friends and Pia.

tropes.name: Wardrobe Wound
tropes.html: Rancho inflicts this on Pia's fiancé, Suhas, to show her how vain he is. Later used a second time by pretending Pia lost the watch Suhas bought her. In the future, Raju continues the tradition by ruining his wedding robe. Knowing that Farhan failed in convincing Pia to elope due to her being kept in the dark about Rancho and his sudden disappearance leaving her wondering whether their relationship was just a dalliance to him, Raju uses the stained wedding robes and poses as the groom to convince Pia himself.

tropes.name: "Well Done, Son" Guy
tropes.html:
• The song "Give Me Some Sunshine" is this.
  • Mr. Qureshi, who is the sole reason why Farhan even bothers to enter the Imperial College. Heck, since birth he has made it his goal to see his son become an engineer. Eventually, he relents and allows Farhan to quit school and pursue the career he wants.
  • Virus was and is also revealed to be one. Him pressuring his son to become an engineer instead of a writer directly caused the latter's suicide. Later, when Mona becomes pregnant with a boy, he consults an astrologist and determines that he will become an engineer. Again, he eventually softens up and decides that his grandson can become anything the latter wants.

tropes.name: Wham Shot
tropes.html:
• The trio discovering that their senior Joy died from suicide.
  • Farhan, Raju and Chatur discovering that Rancho wasn't in the class picture, and that the "fake" Rancho has been shopped in.
  • Raju's attempted suicide.

title: Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan
original_title: Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan

tropes.name: Accentuate the Negative
tropes.html: The further into the south he goes, the more Borat is seemingly surrounded by people who are evidently just as if not more bigoted and backwards than he is (with the people in the rodeo and the frat boys being perhaps the worst), and the movie spends over half of its screentime in those states. That said, Baron Cohen has mentioned that over 400 hours of footage were recorded, so it's easy to imagine what got cut. Even so, it's worth noting that the final footage still shows people who are accommodating, if perhaps with Condescending Compassion.

tropes.name: Action Film, Quiet Drama Scene
tropes.html: Played for Laughs when, in the middle of their brawl, Borat and Azamat run naked and screaming in gibberish into a crowded elevator. They immediately stop screaming and face quietly ahead as the elevator goes up, and then immediately start screaming and fighting again the moment the doors open.

tropes.name: Adaptation Expansion
tropes.html: Borat started as a cultural commentary character in a series of sketches on Da Ali G Show.

tropes.name: Alter-Ego Acting
tropes.html: A Type 1 example. The film revolves around Sacha Baron Cohen interacting with real-life people as his fictional Borat persona, and the individuals in question are shown being completely fooled without ever realizing that he's actually an actor in disguise. Baron Cohen and Ken Davitan (Azamat) would also remain in-character throughout the press tour and various special features, rarely ever appearing as their actual selves to promote the film.

tropes.name: Angry White Man
tropes.html:
Borat meets several examples during his journey, some of which stem from him intentionally provoking them, while others display their hatred without any prompting.
  • Borat frequently greets people by shaking their hand and then kissing them on the cheek, implied to be a standard greeting in the film's fictionalised Kazakh culture, and many of the men he tries this on don't take kindly to it. Even before Borat travels South, one of the men he greets in New York is especially hostile.
    Borat: I kiss you!
    Yuppie: You kiss me, and I'll pop you in the fucking balls!
  • When Borat interviews one of the organizers of the rodeo, the man calmly expresses his disdain for Muslims and homosexuals, and even suggests that Borat shave his signture moustache as it makes him look like a terrorist. Later in the scene, the predominantly white crowd also quickly turn on Borat when he sings his botched national anthem.
  • After being abandoned by Azamat, Borat briefly travels with a group of college frat boys on his way to California. They're shown to be loud and boisterous thugs who have extremely low opinions of women and minorities, and when partying ways they unironically encourage Borat to not let any woman tell him what to do. In real life, these people eventually tried to sue the film's producers for defamation, but lost the case on the grounds that they weren't forced or tricked into saying anything.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Politics
tropes.html: Kazakhstan is actually nowhere near as antisemitic as portrayed; the state works to support synagogues and Jewish schools and at the time of release was one of only a few Muslim countries in the world to recognize Israel. The Kazakh embassy actually had to push back on insinuations to the contrary.

tropes.name: As Long as It Sounds Foreign
tropes.html:
Invoked and Played for Laughs. The film's depiction of Kazakhstan has virtually nothing in common with its real life counterpart, and yet the ignorant people that Borat interacts with in America are none the wiser that he isn't actually Kazakh.
  • Borat's hometown in the opening and ending of the film is actually a Romani village in Romania.
  • When Borat and Azamat's speak to each other in "Kazakh", the conversations are mostly comprised of them speaking Hebrew and Armenian, respectively. The written language used in the film's credits is actually Polish.
  • Borat's female family members are referred to by the surname Sagdiyev. As Kazakhs, they would use the feminine form Sagdiyeva.

tropes.name: The Backwards Я
tropes.html:
• The Cyrillic character Д used in the movie's title is really pronounced similar to "d", not an "a". In fact, reading the title of the film poster in Cyrillic would be "Voyadt", with the R being the wrong way round.
  • The DVD release also had a literal backwards R. (The goal was to make the DVD look like a cheap bootleg.)
  • Played for Comedy with the map of Kazakhstan at the start of the movie. The faux-Cyrillic map renders Kazakhstan as "КфялыЕЙ", which is complete gibberish that roughly reads as "Kfyalyyey". The actual way to spell Kazakhstan is Қазақстан (or Казахстан in Russian).

tropes.name: Bad Humor Truck
tropes.html: Borat and Azamat's choice of cross-country conveyance, complete with <strike>trained guard animal</strike> a black bear named Oksana.

tropes.name: Bag of Kidnapping
tropes.html: What a "traditional marriage sack" actually is. It doesn't work quite the way he planned.

tropes.name: Barely There Swimwear
tropes.html: We see an example at the end, worn by Borat. In one of the deleted scenes, Azamat wears one in a Baywatch parody.

tropes.name: Bears Are Bad News
tropes.html: Borat and Azamat secure a black bear as a guard animal to protect their truck. This works out as well as could be expected.

tropes.name: Bestiality Is Depraved
tropes.html:
• Before leaving to shoot his documentary in America, Borat tells the town rapist, Urkin, not to do too much raping while he is away and stick to "humans only". The implications are pretty clear.
  • A deleted scene also shows Borat asking a woman working at a pet shelter if he can buy a Dog so he can either eat or have sex with the dog. She objects and tells him to leave, for obvious reasons.

tropes.name: Betty and Veronica
tropes.html: Hooker with a Heart of Gold Big Beautiful Woman Luenell is the Betty and celebrity sex symbol Pamela Anderson is the Veronica to Borat's Archie. Played for Laughs as the love triangle only exists in Borat's head.

tropes.name: Big Damn Movie
tropes.html: Notably averted, particularly compared to Da Ali G Show's previous movie spinoff, Ali G Indahouse. Though it definitely has a much more focused plot than most of Borat's segments on the show, and it spends more time letting Borat express himself through his monologues, the movie more-or-less plays out like an extended episode of the TV show. Interestingly, it turned out to be much more successful than Indahouse, which was a clear-cut example of a Big Damn Movie.

tropes.name: Black Comedy Animal Cruelty
tropes.html: Borat and Azamat break into a hearty laugh once they learn that Pamela Anderson recently attended a protest against the mistreatment of animals. In that same scene, the head of Oksana the bear can be briefly seen in Azamat's refrigerator.

tropes.name: Black Comedy Rape
tropes.html:
• Borat is flabbergasted to learn that in the United States, women have the right to say no to sexual advances.
  • Also, Borat recalling he was nearly violated with a sex toy at a Gay Pride parade.

tropes.name: Bland-Name Product
tropes.html: The DVD's top part is printed to look like it was burned onto a Demorex brand recordable disc. It even has a parody of the Memorex slogan — "Is life? No. Demorex."

tropes.name: Brick Joke
tropes.html:
• When Borat explains where Kazakhstan is located, he refers to the neighbouring country of Uzbekistan as "assholes", implying some animosity between the two countries. Later, when he and Azamat are driving through Washington D.C., they pass the real-life Embassy of Uzbekistan, and angrily shout verbal abuse at it.
    Borat: Wawawewa, Uzbekistan! (leans out the window, Flipping the Bird) Fuck a-you! Motherfuckers!
  • Early in the film, Borat meets with a professional comedy trainer, who tries to teach him the proper use of the word "NOT!" in a joke and he doesn't seem to get it. Near the end of the movie, he nails it at a particularly inappropriate, but hilarious, time.
    (while being arrested for trying to kidnap Pamela Anderson, as she's running away)
    "Pamela! I am not attracted to you anymore....NOT!"
  • At the rodeo, Borat attempts to sing the (fictitious) national anthem of Kazakhstan to the tune of the American national anthem. The “original” version of this Kazakh anthem plays in full over the film’s end credits, complete with an onscreen demand for the viewer to stand for it

tropes.name: Brooklyn Rage
tropes.html: Borat's reception on the streets of New York is less than friendly, with people shouting obscenities in his face just for introducing himself. When he tries to shake hands with and kiss a subway passenger: "Touch me and I will punch you in your fucking balls!"

tropes.name: Camera Abuse
tropes.html: At one point in his naked fight with Azamat, Borat launches the camera directly into him.

tropes.name: Combat Breakdown
tropes.html: Borat and Azamat's naked fight gets broken up by security when it enters into a public gathering.

tropes.name: Continuity Reboot
tropes.html: Several of Borat's segments on Da Ali G Show, where the character made his debut, show him visiting America and learning about its culture. The film's plot is presented as Borat's first ever trip to the United States.

tropes.name: Contrived Coincidence
tropes.html: Borat is infatuated with Pamela Anderson and wants to marry her, but he doesn't want to be unfaithful to his wife back in Kazakhstan, because she'll snap his cock off. In the very next scene, he gets a letter from back home: his wife is dead, freeing him to pursue Pam. High five!

tropes.name: Credits Gag
tropes.html: Costume designer Jason Alper is also credited as providing "Mr Baron Cohen's feces".<!--* CringeComedy-->

tropes.name: Culture Clash
tropes.html: The movie is all about this Played for Laughs.

tropes.name: Deliberate Values Dissonance
tropes.html:
Parodied. The film's fictional portrayal of Kazakhstan is depicted as a caricature of rural Eastern European and Central Asian countries, with Borat and its other natives all being xenophobic, misogynistic anti-Semites. Much of the film's humor is derived from Borat interacting with American culture and how it clashes against (and occasionally aligns with) his own backwards beliefs.
  • The whole movie could be seen as one giant parody to this trope.

tropes.name: Despair Event Horizon
tropes.html: Parodied in which Borat has Azamat walk out of him, he falls into despair over thinking he'll never be a man (despite the reassurances of an RV-full of chauvinists).

tropes.name: Developing Nations Lack Cities
tropes.html: The film exaggerates this trope for humor in the most hilariously vulgar ways imaginable. The country of Kazakhstan is portrayed as consisting of a single village that combines all the worst aspects of Ruritania with The Dung Ages: the inhabitants are all inbred and treat Black Comedy Rape and Brother–Sister Incest casually, cattle are kept inside people's houses, glass windows are considered an expensive luxury, people barely live past 43, the village blacksmith doubles as the abortion-provider, the villagers shun Jews with superstitious horror and even hold an annual "Running of The Jew", and where (according to the national anthem) a fairly average modern swimming pool is considered a "marvel to behold". That said, the country is credited as the world's number one exporter of potassium...

tropes.name: Disproportionate Retribution
tropes.html: Borat and Azamat both claim numerous times that any major incidents while making the film - such as them running out of money - will get them both executed by the Kazakh government.

tropes.name: Double-Sided Book
tropes.html: After the film came out, a double-sided book was released, supposedly written by the titular character. One side was titled "Touristic Guidings to Minor Nation of U.S. and A." and the other side was "Touristic Guidings to Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan". They were both, of course, riddled with broken English and glaring factual errors, as per the usual for Borat.<!--* {{Eagleland}}: We see a lot of Flavor 2.-->

tropes.name: Elevator Action Sequence
tropes.html: During the naked brawl, and interrupted by a number of baffled witnesses.

tropes.name: Everything Is Racist
tropes.html:
Most people shown in the South in the movie.
  • The dinner party guests disperse as soon as they see Luenell (although she is quite conspicuously a streetwalker).
  • The antique store is filled with Confederate flags and other pro-secession merchandise, with the owner claiming he is "honoring" his heritage.
  • The college students who are nice to Borat complain that "minorities run the world."
  • The guy behind the counter of the gun shop doesn't bat an eyelid when Borat asks for the best weapon for which to kill Jews and recommends a 9mm or a .45, even giving Borat a Desert Eagle to sample.
    • Of course handing him the Desert Eagle is itself Fridge Brilliance because it's an Israeli gun.

tropes.name: Fan Disservice
tropes.html:
The naked fight between Borat and Azamat.
  • Also the bonus scene of Borat and Azamat's Sexydrownwatch Baywatch idea. It can be found here (NSFW...a lot).

tropes.name: Freeze-Frame Bonus
tropes.html: Not in a visual sense, but if you pay close attention to Borat when he's speaking to Pamela Anderson at the film's climax, he mentions that both he and his deceased wife were children of Bogdev the village rapist.

tropes.name: Funny Background Event
tropes.html: When Borat finally catches up with Azamat, they go to his apartment. When Azamat opens his fridge, a bear's head is clearly visible on a plate, implying that Azamat has been eating the bear.

tropes.name: Gilligan Cut
tropes.html: During one of Borat's monologues, he laments that he cannot pursue Pamela, lest his wife snap off his cock. Cut to the concierge of the hotel Borat is staying at informing him that she died.

tropes.name: Greedy Jew
tropes.html: Spoofed, especially with "The Running of the Jew."

tropes.name: Holiday of Hate
tropes.html: The film's version of Kazakhstan has a cultural event called the Running of the Jew, in which a person dressed as a hideously caricatural Greedy Jew chases after a bag of money, while the female counterpart lays an egg that the participants attack before it hatches another Jew.

tropes.name: Honest John's Dealership
tropes.html: Reversed here, as the dealer sells them a vehicle that is exactly as described: a used ice cream truck.

tropes.name: I Ate WHAT?!
tropes.html: Borat feeds cheese made with his wife's breast milk to an unsuspecting person, only telling him this after he's eaten it.

tropes.name: Inn Security
tropes.html: Parodied. The old couple who run the bed and breakfast Borat and Azamat stay at seem to be perfectly nice and accommodating, but instill great terror in their guests due to being Jewish.

tropes.name: Intentional Engrish for Funny
tropes.html: All over the place, starting with the movie's subtitle.

tropes.name: Irony
tropes.html: When visiting a gun store, Borat asks for the best weapon to kill Jews with. He's briefly given an Israeli-manufactured Desert Eagle.

tropes.name: Lyrical Dissonance
tropes.html: Borat sings the national anthem of fictional Kazakhstan to the tune of "The Star-Spangled Banner".

tropes.name: Mid-Battle Tea Break
tropes.html: The elevator interlude during the naked fight. Of course, as soon as the doors open, pandemonium continues.

tropes.name: Mockumentary
tropes.html: In-universe, Borat and Azamat have been sent to America by Kazakstan's Ministry of Information, and are tasked with documenting Western culture in order to improve Kazakhstan's own. The entire film is formatted as a real documentary, complete with fake logos at the start.

tropes.name: Naked People Are Funny
tropes.html:
• The naked brawl. Also present in the massage scene on the DVD, though Borat spends a lot of time in that under a towel.
  • When practicing for the dinner, Borat shows a picture of his son Hooeylewis, played by transsexual porn star Brittany CoxXx (before her transition and during the time she was still a man known as Stonie). The tutor is disturbed when Borat starts showing picutres of his son with no clothes on, especially when one of the pictures shows Borat with his head next to his son's penis.

tropes.name: No Woman's Land
tropes.html:
One of the main aspects of the film's fictionalised Kazakh culture is its blatant disrespect and dehumanization of women. The women in Kazakhstan are forced to marry young and work long hours in the fields, rape and kidnapping are apparently normalised, they have competitions for best prostitutes (with Borat's sister Natalia being the fourth highest ranked) and during their trip to America, Borat and Azamat are both surprised when they see the various ways that women there have equal rights to men.
Borat: In Kazakhstan, it is illegal for more than five women to be in the same place, except in brothel or in grave.

tropes.name: NOT!
tropes.html: A "comedy expert" struggles to teach Borat the intricacies of this witticism. It takes him the whole movie to catch on.

tropes.name: Overly Long Gag
tropes.html:
• Played for Laughs. When Borat is told he has to include a pause in a NOT! joke, he sits in complete silence for nearly ten seconds. The tutor decides to change the subject, only for Borat to suddenly cut him out with a loud “NOT!”.
  • A deleted scene included on the DVD involves Borat asking a grocery store employee what lots and lots and lots of items are. (They're all cheese.)

tropes.name: Overly Narrow Superlative
tropes.html:
According to the anthem, Kazakhstan has the "cleanest prostitutes in the region, except, of course, for Turkmenistan".
  • Not to mention the famous pool whose filter is a "marvel to behold" in that it removes 80% of human solid waste.

tropes.name: Plot-Mandated Friendship Failure
tropes.html: Happens between Borat and Azamat when the former finds the latter masturbating to a picture of Pamela Anderson, which leads to Borat revealing to Azamat his true motives for traveling to California, the two of them brawling naked all over their hotel, and Azamat abandoning Borat for the remainder of the movie until he returns at the end. All Played for Laughs, of course.

tropes.name: Ruritania
tropes.html: Unlike Kazakhstan in real-life, which is a central Asian country dominated by the open steppe, the film's version of Kazakhstan is more like an amalgamation of the former Warsaw Pact countries with their backwardness and social problems exaggerated to ghoulish, comedic extremes. In real life, the Kazakhs are a Turkic people who've historically had more in-common with the Mongolic peoples than any Slavic culture. Reinforced by the borderline incomprehensible mix of Polish, Hebrew, Romanian, and Armenian words in the place of any actual Kazakh language.

tropes.name: Scare Chord
tropes.html: Parodied, upon Borat's discovery that his hosts for the night are Jewish.

tropes.name: Scylla and Charybdis
tropes.html: The interviewees in the film often find themselves in this sort of dilemma: Accommodating Borat's culture, with its innocent, but genuine, bigotry is one thing. Making clear that you don't agree is another. Trying to somehow do both is well-nigh impossible.

tropes.name: Self-Deprecation
tropes.html: All the jokes mocking Judaism can be countered by the fact that Sacha Baron Cohen himself is Jewish. Fair enough.

tropes.name: Short Title: Long, Elaborate Subtitle
tropes.html: Used for comedy. Also taken to the next level with the soundtrack: Stereophonic Musical Listenings That Have Been Origin in Moving Film "Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan"

tropes.name: Shout-Out
tropes.html:
• Azamat is dressed as Oliver Hardy when he and Borat reunite, and even tells him that "this is another fine mess [he's] gotten them into."
  • Borat's neighbour, Nursultan Tulyakbay, is named after two real prominent Kazakh politicians, Nursultan Nazarbayev and Zharmakan Tuyakbay.

tropes.name: Simple Solution Won't Work
tropes.html: Parodied. When Borat and Azamat agree to travel to California, they decide against travelling by plane — fearing they may get caught up in a follow-up attack to 9/11 — prompting them to buy an old ice cream truck and drive across the country instead. As the film goes on, the pair encounter a number of comical misadventures and setbacks on their road trip — getting publicly humiliated, nearly dying several times, wasting all their money and briefly going their separate ways after a falling-out — all of which would have easily been avoided had they simply flown there directly.

tropes.name: Stylistic Suck
tropes.html:
Borat's MySpace page, as well as the original official web site for the movie, which was done as an atrocious personal home page. Also used in-film with the faux-Kazakh Stock Footage.
  • The DVD itself also deliberately looks like a burned copy bootleg, and the poster is printed to look it has crease marks and other damage.

tropes.name: Super-Stoic Shopkeeper
tropes.html:
• Charting the lack of reactions to Borat's insane and offensive behavior is just as big a part of the comedy as their befuddlement and outrage.
  • The gun shop owner barely bats an eye before recommending a Desert Eagle to "kill Jews." In his defense, he might have simply been recommending a large purchase to an obviously ignorant customer, or playing a subtle joke by selling an Israeli weapon to an obvious anti-semite.
  • When Borat asks what speed he should drive to kill gypsies, the driving instructor merely tells him to keep it at around 40 mph.
  • In one of the deleted scenes, Borat visits a supermarket and asks the supermarket manager what every single item in the cheese section is...he very patiently replies "That's cheese" to every single one.

tropes.name: Tempting Fate
tropes.html: Before Borat goes to browse the antique shop, Azamat warns him not to spend more than 3 dollars. Borat ends up causing over 400 dollars worth of damages just through his own clumsiness.

tropes.name: Thousand-Yard Stare
tropes.html: That poor man in the corner of the elevator had this when Borat and Azamat got on, completely naked. Honestly, you can't really blame him.

tropes.name: Uncomfortable Elevator Moment
tropes.html:
Quite possibly the most uncomfortable one in cinematic history. To elaborate, both men have been running around naked through a hotel, screaming in foreign-sounding gibberish. One of the men was threatening to beat the other silly with a huge rubber dildo. The prop is brought along for the ride in an already occupied elevator. Both men face forward, stand quietly, and enjoy the elevator ride. DING! Doors open. Running and screaming resume.
  • When Borat and Azamat enter the elevator naked, nearly all of the people on the elevator immediately get off. In fact, at first it looks like they're the only ones standing in the elevator until the camera quickly shifts and reveals a stone-faced man tucked in the corner.

tropes.name: Understatement
tropes.html:
The very first person Borat introduces to the audience is Urkin, "the town rapist".
"Naughty, naughty!"

tropes.name: Unusual Euphemism
tropes.html:
• Chocolate face and vanilla facenote black person and white person respectively.
  • Hand partynote Masturbation.
  • Romance explosionnote Ejaculation.

tropes.name: Vulgar Humor
tropes.html: After politely asking a group of Southern ladies if he could be excused to use the restroom, Borat comes back with a baggie of his own poop, politely asking where he can place it.

tropes.name: What Happened to the Mouse?
tropes.html: The bear's head can be seen inside the fridge when Borat and Azamat make up, but the rest of its body? God knows.

tropes.name: World of Jerkass
tropes.html: Although he sometimes brings it upon himself, a lot of the people that Borat meets are hostile towards him for basically no reason whatsoever, such as the guy who callously told Borat to "mind (his) own fucking business" just because Borat asked what his name was.

tropes.name: Younger Than They Look
tropes.html: Borat's mother, the "oldest woman in whole of Kuzcek", looks like a shriveled old woman but is actually only 43.

tropes.name: The '90s
tropes.html:
Ska (lots of it), The Real World, Dawson's Creek, and Jared Leto references.
Patrick: You know, these guys are no Bikini Kill or the Raincoats, but they're not bad.

tropes.name: Adaptation Title Change
tropes.html: Ten Things I Hate About You is a modernised adaptation of Shakespeare's The Taming of The Shrew.

tropes.name: Adaptational Jerkass
tropes.html: All Bianca's suitors in the original had a Friendly Rivalry, and Lucentio (Cameron's counterpart) just convinced his biggest rival that Bianca wasn't worthy of his affections, and he bowed out gracefully when he was outbid. This version has a Jerkass called Joey, who's only out to sleep with Bianca for a bet and dumped Kat when she wouldn't sleep with him a second time.

tropes.name: Adaptational Nice Guy
tropes.html: Petruchio from the original was absolutely vile to Kate in his attempt to "tame" her. Patrick's worst aspect is being initially paid to date Kat before falling for her, beyond that he's just a touch condescending early on and gives mixed signals sometimes.

tropes.name: All Girls Want Bad Boys
tropes.html:
Subverted.
  • Kat only starts to like Patrick when he's not being a jerk and it's his persistence that wins her over, not his bad boy charms.
  • But played straight with Bianca falling for Joey. That is, until she also subverts it by falling for Cameron.

tropes.name: Alliterative Name
tropes.html: Robert "Bobby" Ridgeway.

tropes.name: All Periods Are PMS
tropes.html: Katerina's father calls her out on this, after she dents Joey's car in a bout of anger: "My insurance does not cover PMS!"

tropes.name: Almost Kiss
tropes.html: After the party Kat leans in for a kiss and Patrick pulls away, showing he was starting to connect with her.

tropes.name: Amusing Injuries
tropes.html: Bianca accidentally firing an arrow into her teacher's backside.

tropes.name: And This Is for...
tropes.html:
Bianca does this to Joey near the end of the movie. It's immensely satisfying.
Bianca: That's for making my date bleed, that's for my sister, and that’s for me!

tropes.name: Armor-Piercing Question
tropes.html:
When Cameron calls out Bianca on her self-centeredness.
Cameron: (very perturbed) Have you always been this selfish?
Bianca: (in a small voice) Yes.

tropes.name: Artists Are Attractive
tropes.html: Patrick starts to fall for Kat, in no small part, because of their similar tastes in music His Apology Gift to her is a specific guitar she's wanted for some time. It proves his sincerity not because of its financial value (though that is also substantial) but because it shows he was listening to her and cared about her desires.

tropes.name: Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other
tropes.html:
• Kat reluctantly agrees to go to Bogey's party so that Bianca can, even if it means Bianca will likely run into Joey.
  • Kat also agreeing to go to the prom, despite having criticised it repeatedly earlier, so that Bianca can attend.
  • Mr. Stratford sends Sarah Lawrence a check at the end so Kat can attend, even though he initially wanted her to stay close to home. When he tells Kat this, she's so happy she actually hugs him.

tropes.name: Bad News in a Good Way
tropes.html:
Cameron: We're screwed.
Michael: Hey, no, hey. I don't want to hear that defeatist attitude. I want to hear you upbeat.
Cameron: [upbeat)] We're screwed!
Michael: There you go.

tropes.name: Because I Said So
tropes.html: Their father, sort of, and also Kat towards Bianca's wish to date Joey. She doesn't explain why till the end of the movie. Kat slept with Joey once. When she said she didn't want to do it again, he dumped her.

tropes.name: The Bet
tropes.html: Subverted and, in a way, played straight. Joey is actually just after Bianca because his friends bet him he couldn't sleep with her, but by the time Bianca finds out about this she's already become disenchanted with Joey and realized that Cameron is the better guy. Patrick, while not betting on anything himself, is the one who catches the consequences of the trope when Kat finds out that he was paid to take her out.

tropes.name: Beta Couple
tropes.html: Cameron and Bianca become this to Kat and Patrick after Bianca realizes Cameron is a better person than Joey.

tropes.name: Betty and Veronica
tropes.html: The sweet, genuine Cameron and the shallow Joey for Bianca. She chooses Cameron.

tropes.name: Bilingual Bonus
tropes.html: Unlike the other French lesson dialogue, Cameron's French cursing is not subtitled.

tropes.name: Boyfriend-Blocking Dad
tropes.html: Mr. Stratford is an obstetrician and frequently has to deal with teenage pregnancies, which fuels his rules against Bianca dating. With the comments that Mrs. Stratford ran out on the family, he admits late in the film he was also worried about becoming "a spectator" in the lives of his daughters rather than "a player."

tropes.name: Brick Joke
tropes.html: Early in the movie Patrick drills a hole in Cameron's French textbook. The hole remains for the rest of the movie, making for several scenes where the already clueless Cameron is attempting to learn French from a useless book.

tropes.name: Calling the Old Man Out
tropes.html: Mr. Stratford, being an Boyfriend-Blocking Dad, gets three small ones, one from Kat and two from Bianca, where Kat lays into him for not letting her attend Sarah Lawrence and to stop trying to control her life because he can't seem to control his, and Bianca even calls him severely unhinged when he won't allow her to attend the prom if Kat isn't going.

tropes.name: The Cast Showoff
tropes.html:
In-universe. Averted with Cameron, who signs up as Bianca's French tutor in order to get close to her, despite being unable to speak French. In real life, Joseph Gordon-Levitt speaks fluent French.
Michael: She's actually looking for a French tutor...
Cameron: Are you serious? That's perfect!
Michael: Do you speak French?
Cameron: Well, no, but I will!

tropes.name: Chekhov's Gun
tropes.html: The money Joey is paying Patrick to date Kat, and the Fender Strat guitar Kat is seen with in the music store. At the end of the film, Patrick reveals to Kat he used the money to get the guitar for her. Possibly subverted in that it may not be the same guitar, but the idea still stands.

tropes.name: Clique Tour
tropes.html: Michael gives new boy Cameron a tour of the high school social scene.

tropes.name: Composite Character
tropes.html: Joey is one for the original Taming of the Shrew's Gremio and Hortensio.

tropes.name: Culturally Sensitive Adaptation
tropes.html: The Taming of the Shrew is one of the most difficult Shakespeare plays to adapt due to having a lot of questionable material regarding the treatment of women, with the "comedy" coming from a man setting a shrewish woman "in her place" by humiliating and torturing her until she becomes submissive. This film opts to keep the bones of the comedic setup, but dramatically overhauls the relationship between the leads to be more respectful and sincere, with meaningful Character Development between both Patrick and Kat that ends with them happily being together. A common alternate interpretation of the original play is that it was actually meant as a satire of misogyny-ridden romantic comedies of the era, and as such meant to be laid thick with irony, including Kate's "submission" to her male partner. This subsequently led to the interpretation that Kate and Petrucio "tame" each other, and in both being equally tempestuous hotheads, they're actually perfect for each other. 10 Things commits as an adaptation to this interpretation, elevating it from irony-driven subtext to actual text.

tropes.name: Death Glare
tropes.html:
• Kat gives the preppy girls a surly glare when we first see her. It comes with an Establishing Character Moment.
  • Walter angrily stares down Joey on prom night when the latter turns up at the Stratford house to pick up Bianca, before wordlessly slamming the door in Joey's face.

tropes.name: Distracted by the Sexy
tropes.html: Kat deliberately invokes this to get Patrick out of detention.

tropes.name: Dysfunctional Family
tropes.html: The Stratfords, largely due to Mr Stratford being a Boyfriend-Blocking Dad who doesn't want his daughters to grow up and live their own lives. In Kat's words, he controls their lives because he can't control his.

tropes.name: Establishing Character Moment
tropes.html:
• The movie opens with a perky pop song*Specifically, Barenaked Ladies' "One Week" playing over fun, bouncing credits, as four perky pretty girls roll up to a stop sign in a brightly-coloured sports car... then the pop music is rapidly drowned out by Joan Jett's "Bad Reputation", as a lone, sour-faced young woman rolls up next to them in a beat-up Ford, glaring. Six minutes before we learn her name, five minutes before she ever speaks, and we already know Kat's basic character.
  • Also captured in that wonderful exchange with Miss Perky:
    Ms. Perky: People perceive you as somewhat...
    Kat: Tempestuous?
    Ms. Perky: "Heinous bitch" is the term used most often.
    Kat: [pleased smile]

tropes.name: Establishing Character Music
tropes.html: The film establishes Kat quite well by having her pull up next to a bunch of peppy popular girls in a '60s beat-up Dodge Dart, glaring, to the tune of Joan Jett's "Bad Reputation".

tropes.name: Exact Words
tropes.html: Kat tells Joey to stay away from Bianca during the party scene. Joey responds with this: "Oh, I'll stay away from your sister. But I can't guarantee she'll stay away from me." Sure enough, Bianca runs into Joey, but she soon sees Kat's point about him.<!--* EvenTheGuysWantHim: After Creator/HeathLedger finished his audition, the director turned to his mostly female staff and said "I'm not gay. But if I was, that is the kind of guy I'd want to sleep with."-->

tropes.name: Everything Sounds Sexier in French
tropes.html:
• Subverted with Cameron and Bianca's decidedly unromantic French tutoring sessions, to Cameron's disappointment.
    Cameron: I thought we could start with pronunciation?
    Bianca: Ugh, not the hacking and gagging and spitting part, please.
  • It doesn't get any better once they actually start speaking French either, since he's struggling with basic sentence structure, and she's speaking rapid-fire fluent French about how pissed she is that he's not asked her out yet.

tropes.name: Face Doodling
tropes.html:
Actually took place while the character was awake. Joey doodles on Michael's face as he's trying to speak.
Michael: I have a dick on my face, don't I?

tropes.name: Faux Fluency
tropes.html: Cameron falsely claims to know French so that he could get closer to Bianca as a tutor. Later in the film she is more fluent than he is.

tropes.name: Foreshadowing
tropes.html:
• Mr Morgan insulting Joey in his class ("Someday you're gonna get bitch-slapped, and I'm not going to do a thing to stop it" and then "Unless she kicked the crap out of your dumb butt, I don't want to hear about it") sets up how Joey will get his ass handed to him by Bianca at the prom.
  • Bianca tells Cameron in their first meeting that Kat used to be popular but an "unsolved mystery" caused her to become cold and antisocial. Bianca later finds out that it was because Kat went out with Joey before and they went all the way, but when Kat told Joey she wasn't ready to do it again, he dumped her.
  • At Bogey's party, when Kat saw Bianca with Joey, Kat tried to get Bianca alone, but Bianca told her to go away. Kat was going to tell Bianca about her past relationship with Joey that she (and the audience) find out about later.

tropes.name: Full-Name Basis
tropes.html: We only hear Kat's full name of Katarina spoken twice, first by Mr. Stratford when he first appears and again when Cameron asks a group of guys if any of them would be interested in dating her.

tropes.name: Funny Background Event
tropes.html:
• As Bianca is trying to fire her bow, Joey tries to talk to her. The result is that the arrow misses the target and hits the teacher insteadnote The Coach was kind of asking for it standing in front of the firing line. He was clearly away from the line of fire but Bianca had turned about 60 degrees to her left between Joey's appearance and letting the arrow go. Regardless, that's why the general rule is to stay behind the firing line. Bianca even stops to look before going right back to her conversation.
  • When Coach Chapin is supervising detention several scenes later, he still visibly has trouble sitting down due to his earlier injury.

tropes.name: Get Out!
tropes.html: Mr. Morgan sends Kat out of his class twice. The second time, she's genuinely interested, but he thinks she's mocking him.

tropes.name: The Glorious War of Sisterly Rivalry
tropes.html:
As in the Shakespearean source material, the Stratford sisters. Kat is the bitchy and high-minded Smart, while Bianca is the gregarious and not-as-intellectual Pretty.
Kat: You don't always have to be who they want you to be, you know.
Bianca: I happen to like being adored, thank you.

tropes.name: Groin Attack
tropes.html:
• Bianca to Joey after finding out he placed a bet to nail her on prom night. And the audience cheers.
  • A Noodle Incident equivalent happens in Kat's backstory. ("I still maintain that he kicked himself in the balls.")
  • When Michael is on his bike and accidentally goes tumbling down a hill, he shouts "My balls!" during one of the bounces.

tropes.name: Held Gaze
tropes.html: One between Kat and Patrick, which turns into an Almost Kiss but then Patrick looks away, killing the moment. This also happens between Cameron and Bianca as well.

tropes.name: "Hey, You!" Haymaker
tropes.html: The previously mellow Bianca does this to Joey at the prom, combining it with And This Is for......: "That's for making my date bleed, that's for my sister, and that's for me!"

tropes.name: High School AU
tropes.html: It's intentionally The Taming of the Shrew in a 1999 American high school.

tropes.name: High-School Dance
tropes.html: Patrick needs to convince Kat to go with him to prom so that Bianca can also attend. Kat finds it an outdated and misogynist event, and her father (a gyno) views it as a prelude to an orgy.

tropes.name: Hilarious Outtakes
tropes.html: Some play over the end credits: when Kat attempts to kiss Patrick instead of pulling back Heath pulls in Julia for a sloppy kiss, when Joey punches Cameron he No Sells with "Is that it?" and a scene of Kat dragging Bianca through the hallway and turning a corner finds Ms. Perky making out with another teacher.

tropes.name: Hollywood Geography
tropes.html: Anyone who's ever lived in Seattle will be somewhat bemused by how everything is situated. The establishing shot of Seattle indicates they are on the north side, but Padua High School is filmed at Stadium High School in Tacoma about 45 minutes south. They escape detention and go back to Seattle from there to the docks where they rent the boat.

tropes.name: Hypocrite
tropes.html: Kat wants to protect Bianca from making her mistakes with boys, but she also wants her to make up her own mind, so she won't tell her anything.

tropes.name: Hypocritical Humor
tropes.html: While Cameron and Bianca are going through Kat's bedroom so that Cameron can clue Patrick in on Kat's likes and dislikes, Bianca refuses to let Cameron see her own room because "a girl's room is very personal". Bear in mind this is after Bianca has shown Cameron a pair of Kat's panties.

tropes.name: I Just Shot Marvin in the Face
tropes.html: More like "I just shot my teacher in the ass", but it works. It's actually a large part the teacher's fault, as he wandered into the target area while someone still had a bow drawn.

tropes.name: I Meant to Do That
tropes.html: Michael, on his scooter, swerves out of the way of an oncoming truck and careers down a grassy hill towards the sports field. After he falls off, he gets up, sees the crowd up at the top and cheers with his arms in the air, invoking this trope.

tropes.name: Instantly Proven Wrong
tropes.html: When New Transfer Student Cameron meets Michael, he comments that he's thankful that for once the teachers didn't send down "one of those audio-visual geeks" to show him around on his first day. Michael laughs, at which point a guy carrying a bunch of AV equipment walks to him and asks "Hey Michael, where should I put those slides?"

tropes.name: Kick the Dog
tropes.html: Joey steals Bianca away from Cameron at the party and as they walk away from him, Joey flashes him a smug smile and a sarcastic thumbs-up.

tropes.name: Laser-Guided Karma
tropes.html:
• For parking in the middle of the road, right behind Kat's car to annoy her, Kat delivers instant karma by reversing into Joey's car, denting it.
  • Michael is kicked out of the Ivy League group at Padua for a petty reason by Bogey Lowenstein, so Michael gets his revenge by planning a house party at Bogey's house without Bogey knowing about it. It also has a side effect for the main characters in that it gives Joey, then Cameron, an excuse to get with Bianca.
  • Also, when Bianca finds out about Joey's ultimate aim to have his way with her on prom night, and now knowing about what he did to Kat in the past, she furiously attacks him.

tropes.name: Lighter and Softer
tropes.html:
• The Taming of the Shrew was a good bit more misogynistic, with the "taming" of Kate being far more one-sidedly based around Petrucio torturing and humiliating her until she becomes a perfectly subservient wife as a means of proving that any woman can be "put in their place". Here, while aspects of the setup are the same — Patrick starts wooing Kat because of a bet — the romance is almost completely overhauled to be much more sincere, the friction between the two has little that can be described outright as "abusive," and the two end with mutual feelings and respect for one another.
  • Also received a tone-shift between script drafts; the original screenplay is much darker, including a subplot about a suicidal Mandella.

tropes.name: Light Is Not Good
tropes.html: Joey wears a few white outfits, such as a white tank top, which he wears when he first bribes Patrick to go out with Kat, and the white suit jacket he wears to the prom.

tropes.name: Meaningful Name
tropes.html:
• Kat's (abbreviated form) name, although she spells it with a K, seeing as how cats are sterotyped. Cats Are Mean is not a trope for nothing.
  • Kat and Bianca's last name (after Stratford-upon-Avon), as well as Patrick's last name, and Padua High School.
  • Cameron James is named after King James, who ruled during Shakespeare's life.

tropes.name: Megaphone Hanging
tropes.html:
Stacks of Shakespeare references.
Cameron: I burn, I pine, I perish!
Michael: ...Sure you do.

tropes.name: Mills and Boon Prose
tropes.html:
A guidance counselor, who writes bad sex novels, wants to know another word for "engorged".
  • Swollen.
  • Turgid.
  • Tumescent?
  • Perfect!
  • Bratwurst.
    "I'll let you get back to Reginald's quivering member."
    "I've got deviants to see and a novel to finish... now SCOOT!"

tropes.name: Missing Mom
tropes.html: Kat and Bianca's mother is absent. She gets a few mentions, the implication being that she left the family, and that left the dad feeling out of control, explaining why he's so overprotective of his daughters.

tropes.name: Moment Killer
tropes.html: While sitting on the swings outside Bogey's party, Kat remarks on Patrick's eyes. It looks like there will be a tender moment between the two, only for Kat to vomit seconds later.

tropes.name: Mood Whiplash
tropes.html:
• Kat makes a remark on Patrick's eyes, only for the moment to be ruined when she vomits on the ground.
  • During the paint-balling session, a tender kiss between Patrick and Kat is interrupted when Kat hits Patrick on the forehead with another paintball.

tropes.name: Mr. Fanservice
tropes.html: Patrick and Joey. In Joey's case, it's what attracted Kat to him in the backstory.

tropes.name: Nice Guy
tropes.html: Cameron, Michael, and Patrick, on the whole. While all 3 do have their flaws, they all do look out for each other, and Bianca and Kat.

tropes.name: Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!
tropes.html: Nearly the entire movie could have been avoided had Patrick just written Kat a private note inviting her out to a local pool hall or somewhere similar, where she would have immediately seen his bad boy attitude and demeanor in action and probably started becoming attracted to him from the outset instead of repelling her by trying to force her attention and making the job so much harder than it needed to be. The note wouldn't even have had to be anonymous, as Kat doesn't know Patrick at this point in the film and therefore has every reason to give him a chance and especially if she's being asked to a place where she can mostly act out her own violent tendencies with only minimal consequences at worst.

tropes.name: No Full Name Given
tropes.html: Occurs with all four members of staff at Padua we see: Miss Perky, Mr. Morgan, Coach Chapin, and Miss Perky's secretary, Judith.

tropes.name: Oh, Crap!
tropes.html: Michael at the prom when he realizes Kat knows the truth about the bet, and he promptly tells Cameron the shit has hit the fan.

tropes.name: Pair the Spares
tropes.html: Chastity ends up with Joey; Michael starts dating Kat's best friend Mandella.

tropes.name: A Party, Also Known as an Orgy
tropes.html:
Said by Mr. Stratford when Bianca and Chastity tried to convince him that them going to Bogey's party wasn't the end of the world.
Walter: Where are we going?
Bianca: Well, if you must know, a small study group of friends...
Walter: ...otherwise known as an orgy?
Chastity: Mr. Stratford, it's just a party.
Walter: And hell is just a sauna.

tropes.name: Pet the Dog
tropes.html: At Bogey's party, Joey is about to ask Patrick how he was able to get Kat to come to the party (he didn't, Bianca did, but Joey doesn't know that), and when, seconds later, Kat starts a drunken table dance, Joey encourages her for a moment and is quite impressed by it.

tropes.name: Pretty Boy
tropes.html: In doing some research Cameron and Michael figure Kat likes girl bands, poetry and "pretty guys." They relay this to Patrick and imply the pretty guy part will be an issue, and Patrick actually gets offended that they don't think he's pretty.

tropes.name: "The Reason You Suck" Speech
tropes.html: Cameron was set to go with Bianca to Bogey's party, but she brushed him off to hang with Joey. He's devastated but she loses interest in Joey after realizing how vapid he was. She asked Cameron to drive her home, and as they arrived he called her out on being selfish.

tropes.name: Reconstruction
tropes.html: Has some elements of this with regards to the teen comedy. Kat's anti-social behavior stems from past high school drama and Bianca has a Heel Realization with her It's All About Me attitude.

tropes.name: Red Is Heroic
tropes.html: Inverted. Joey's sports car is red, but he's a Jerk Jock.

tropes.name: Red Oni, Blue Oni
tropes.html: Kat is blue, Bianca is red. This is also shown in the colours of a good number of their respective outfits in their scenes together, including their prom dresses near the end of the film.<!--** Kat is also the red to Patrick's blue.-->

tropes.name: Rooftop Concert
tropes.html: The movie ends with a crane shot, revealing the band Letters to Cleo playing on top of Padua High School.

tropes.name: Rule of Three
tropes.html: In all three scenes in Mr. Morgan's English class, Kat leaves while each is in progress. The first two times, Mr. Morgan tells her to Get Out!. The third, however, she starts crying as she reads her poem and walks out.

tropes.name: Screams Like a Little Girl
tropes.html: When Cameron asks the guys Michael has gathered about whether they will date Kat, the final guy has this reaction.

tropes.name: Screw the Rules, I'm Beautiful!
tropes.html:
• Bianca believes she can manipulate Cameron's feelings for her based on this. When he finds out, Cameron disagrees.
  • Joey feels that, as the most handsome man on campus, he can have any woman he wants and be damned her feelings on the matter.

tropes.name: Second-Act Breakup
tropes.html: Played mostly straight with Kat and Patrick, although most of the movie is them getting close and then getting in a big fight anyway.

tropes.name: Serenade Your Lover
tropes.html: The famous "Can't Take My Eyes Off of You" scene in the stadium. With a parade.

tropes.name: Sesquipedalian Loquaciousness
tropes.html:
Thanks to Dawson's Creek, this is one of the many teen-oriented projects in which the kids arrange their words in such a manner that they sound like a college freshman who's trying too hard to make an essay sound more sophisticated than it actually is.
Bianca: Can we for two seconds ignore the fact that you're severely unhinged and discuss my need for a night of teenage normalcy?

tropes.name: She Cleans Up Nicely
tropes.html: Kat and Patrick have this effect on one another. Kat in particular wears casual clothes for most of the film (save for donning a strapless top for the concert) but looks positively stunning in a blue prom dress with her hair done and her mother's pearls.

tropes.name: Sheep in Sheep's Clothing
tropes.html: After a Heel Realization courtesy of being called out by Cameron, Bianca becomes one of these.

tropes.name: Shot in the Ass
tropes.html: A distracted Bianca looses an arrow into her gym teacher's posterior.

tropes.name: Show Some Leg
tropes.html:
It isn't exactly her leg.
Patrick: So how did you keep him distracted?
Kat: I dazzled him with my... wits.

tropes.name: "Shut Up" Kiss
tropes.html:
• Bianca does this to Cameron when he calls her out on her actions at the party (He was technically her date, but she spent more time with Joey only to recognize Joey for what he was. Cameron was being a gentleman by driving her home). Probably the best way to get back in his good graces.
  • Subverted later when Kat finally finds out that Patrick was paid to date her. He tries resorting to this to convince her that he really did love her, but she was too angry and pushed him away.
  • Played straight again at the very end of the movie, after Patrick finally wins Kat back by buying her dream guitar for her.

tropes.name: Small Reference Pools
tropes.html: Kat complains about not discussing women authors in English class, but only names Sylvia Plath and Charlotte Brontë (she does name Simone de Beauvoir, however).

tropes.name: Smoking Is Not Cool
tropes.html: Kat certainly thinks so, and according to Bianca she once said she would rather die before dating a guy who smoked. Patrick gives up to try and appeal to her. She walks away from him after the paint-balling session when he lights up (she also takes the cigarette from his mouth).

tropes.name: Social Circle Filler
tropes.html: Patrick is seen at the start of the film hanging around with a bald biker guy, with whom he smokes and who is his lab partner. As Patrick becomes more involved with Kat, the character disappears altogether. Later on, when Patrick needs someone to talk to, he goes to Cameron.

tropes.name: Speaking Like Totally Teen
tropes.html:
Walter Stratford's various attempts at speaking 'teen' in an effort to get his point across to his daughters aren't as successful as he hopes. Nobody calls it out, but it's clear it's just as embarrassing for them to hear as it is for the audience.
Walter: I'm down, I've got the 411, and you are not going out and getting jiggy with some boy, I don't care how dope his ride is. My momma didn't raise no foo'!

tropes.name: Tap on the Head
tropes.html: Kat's drunken table dance ends when she hits her head on the chandelier above the table and Patrick catches her before she can hit the ground.

tropes.name: This Is Gonna Suck
tropes.html: Mr. Stratford says "This is not good" as Cameron and Bianca leave his house to go the prom.

tropes.name: Title Drop
tropes.html: The title comes from the poem Kat composes as part of an English assignment.

tropes.name: Token Black Friend
tropes.html:
• Chastity is seemingly there just as a friend for Bianca to sound board ideas off in the first act. This gets arguably subverted when at Bogey's party, she gets annoyed with Bianca pawning her off on Cameron and hooks up with Joey in retaliation.
  • Joey has a black friend who exists only to listen to his evil plans and gets minimal lines or characterization.

tropes.name: Tomboy and Girly Girl
tropes.html: Kat is an aggressive, casually dressed lover of punk music, and her younger sister Bianca is a glamour-obsessed fashionista.<!--* TrademarkFavouriteFood: Possibly. Cameron finds out from Bianca that Kat really likes Thai food.--><!--* {{Tsundere}}: Kat is a definitive type A.-->

tropes.name: Two-Teacher School
tropes.html: The gym teacher/soccer coach and the English teacher are the only ones seen.

tropes.name: Unusual Euphemism
tropes.html:
• This exchange:
    Patrick: Joey can plough whatever he wants.
    Cameron: Hey! There will be no ploughing!
  • "Bratwurst? Well, aren't we the optimist."

tropes.name: Unusually Uninteresting Sight
tropes.html: A couple cartoonish sight-gags are brushed off by the characters. The most notable is that during gym class doing archery Bianca accidentally shoots her teacher in the ass while Joey is trying to flirt with her. They briefly glance at him writhing in pain and some other students move to help, but they continue their teenage drama conversation.

tropes.name: Vanity Is Feminine
tropes.html: Poked fun at when Patrick is told Katerina prefers "pretty guys." "... Are you telling me I'm not a pretty guy?"

tropes.name: What the Hell, Hero?
tropes.html:
Cameron gives Bianca a piece of his mind when he learns that she was just manipulating him and his feelings towards her to try and get closer to another guy. This is, of course, after Bianca has decided that maybe he's the better choice after all.
Cameron: Just 'cause you're beautiful, that doesn't mean that you can treat people like they don't matter. (cue "Shut Up" Kiss)

tropes.name: Wild Teen Party
tropes.html: Michael and Cameron commandeer a party intended for the small posh crew and made it into a crazy event with free beer.

tropes.name: World of Snark
tropes.html: Kat, Bianca, Michael, to name only a few, and plenty of Snark-to-Snark Combat, especially between the Stratfords.

tropes.name: Worst Aid
tropes.html: Patrick thinks Kat might have a concussion, so he tries to stop her from falling asleep - which is a complete myth. As long as the person isn't displaying any difficulties holding a conversation or walking, or displaying symptoms like dilated pupils, sleep is actually good to help the brain rest

tropes.name: Ye Olde Butcherede Englishe
tropes.html:
Parodied.
Michael: [in character] The shit hath hitteth the fan... eth.

tropes.name: Your Approval Fills Me with Shame
tropes.html: In a variation, when Kat offers excitement when the English teacher invites them to write their own Shakespearean sonnet he sends her to detention. Since she spends all her time on a soapbox and criticizing his curriculum, he took it as sarcasm.

tropes.name: Accidental Innuendo
tropes.html:
In-Universe. When Henry talks to Lucy again, he makes a joke about him and his walrus that Lucy finds suggestive and insulting and believes him to being a stalker as she claims to have never even met him. This confuses Henry, prompting Sue to explain things to him.
Henry: My hands are extra fishy if you care to take a whiff.
Lucy: (confused) What...was that?
Henry: I was petting my walrus all morning and I was thinking about you the whole time.
Lucy: Okay, pervert. I think you should leave.

tropes.name: The Ace
tropes.html: Ula's four sons and one daughter are all athletically gifted, which frustrates him because of how bad at sports he is.

tropes.name: Action Girl
tropes.html: When Henry has Ula pretend to beat him up as one of his attempts at a Meet Cute with Lucy, Lucy takes a baseball bat and comes to his "rescue."

tropes.name: Actor Allusion
tropes.html: Dan Aykroyd plays Lucy's neuro-physician, who mentions that their clinic is funded by TB Callahan in Sandusky, Ohio, as a shout-out to his role from Tommy Boy.

tropes.name: All in the Manual
tropes.html: The photos and drawings scribbled in the end credits reveal that Henry and Lucy's daughter is named Nicole.

tropes.name: Almost Kiss
tropes.html: Defied. When Henry reunites with Lucy after several weeks of separation, they are about to kiss...until 10-second Tom breaks in for no apparent reason. But then, Henry shoos him away and continues the kiss, anyway.

tropes.name: Ambiguous Gender Identity
tropes.html:
• Alexa. It's unknown if they're a effeminate guy, an androgynous woman or genderqueer.
  • Kevin James' character talking about his 'date' with Henry Roth in the prologue. It's unknown if they're a gay man or transgender.

tropes.name: Ambiguously Gay
tropes.html: Doug speaks with a lisp and fits into the Gym Bunny stereotype. He's also seen with Alexa at the end.

tropes.name: Ambiguously Bi
tropes.html:
• The opening montage hints that Henry has had a relationship with a man (played by Kevin James), though it might have just been a one-sided crush.
  • Alexa, who nervously hits on a woman that Henry rejected in a bar, gives Henry advice on how to please a woman and later hits on Doug.

tropes.name: Amnesiac Resonance
tropes.html: Lucy is an amnesiac who only remembers her life until an accident she had. She wakes up every day thinking it's the day of the accident, when in reality it's been over a year. She can't seem to remember her boyfriend, but near the end of the movie, she makes paintings with "eggmen" (Henry was made fun of for his egg-shaped head).

tropes.name: Anguished Declaration of Love
tropes.html:
Henry delivers one to Lucy after returning to her and visiting her art studio.
Henry: You erased me from your memories because you thought you were holding me back from having a full and happy life. But you made a mistake. Being with you is the only way I could have a full and happy life. You're the girl of my dreams... and apparently, I'm the man of yours.

tropes.name: Armour-Piercing Question
tropes.html: Henry calls out Marlin about how he clearly hasn't thought about how exactly they can keep their ruse going when eventually Lucy will wake up one day and find she's aged years overnight. Marlin tells him he thinks about that exact thing all the time.

tropes.name: Artistic License
tropes.html: A Spam truck is shown arriving at the diner with the tins out in the open on it's bed. This is NOT how packaged meat is delivered as the tins in direct sunlight and in the humid Hawaiian air would warm up the inside and not only cause the meat to spoil faster but allow bacteria harmful to humans to grow in and contaminate the meat. It is for this reason that meat is almost always delivered in a refrigerated truck.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Medicine
tropes.html:
• The name of Lucy's condition is fictional, but a very rough approximation of other memory loss types. The neat 24 Hour, reset when you fall asleep is too simple and most short-term memory loss patients have trouble remembering things throughout the day. (The duration between "resets" is much shorter in real life; particularly unlucky amnesia patients forget things about every thirty seconds.) However, her still being able to paint is accurate.
  • No mental health care facility in the world would assign nicknames to their patients based off of their condition. Such behaviour is incredibly unprofessional and demeaning.

tropes.name: Award-Bait Song
tropes.html: "Love Song" by 311. Though because it's a cover, it wouldn't be able to get a nomination.

tropes.name: Awful Wedded Life
tropes.html:
Ula complains constantly about his wife and how miserable he is with her. He even rags on her while officiating Henry and Lucy’s wedding.
Ula: Really? Even though in like, ten years she could really let herself go and sex could be like, nauseating for you?
Henry: What are you nuts? Your wife’s right there!
Ula’s Wife: (flips him off)
Ula: I was just kidding, Muu-Muu!

tropes.name: Bait-and-Switch
tropes.html:
• After Henry first meets Lucy, he manages to whack his golf ball of a cliff. He encounters her while looking for it, and they begin to have sex...and then it turns out it never happened and the golf ball flew off the car and whacked him in the head and knocked him out.
  • The final shot of Henry's "meeting on the road" montage has him be Bound and Gagged so Lucy will stop and help him... and then the people who stop are Marlin and Doug.

tropes.name: Batter Up!
tropes.html:
Henry has Ula pretend to beat him up so that Lucy could help him and therefore greet her. Lucy ends up beating Ula up with a metal baseball bat and chases him off while still beating him up.
Ula: (running off) OH, YOU CRAZY BITCH!
Lucy: Yeah, KEEP RUNNING!!

tropes.name: Big "WHY?!"
tropes.html: Lucy appears to be yelling one of these when she discovers the truth about her memory being wiped due to an accident that happened to her a year prior and runs out on the deck in tears.

tropes.name: A Birthday, Not a Break
tropes.html: Lucy's accident happened on Marlin's birthday. The poor guy has to recreate his birthday over and over again to keep his daughter from being traumatized.

tropes.name: Bittersweet Ending
tropes.html: Lucy never truly recovers, though she does dream about Henry enough to almost remember him. The two marry and have a child, though Lucy still has to watch tapes of the events of her life since the accident to truly remember both of them. While it's clearly not ideal, they are making the best of a bad situation and living a happy life overall.

tropes.name: Bound and Gagged
tropes.html: Henry does this to himself as the final part of his meet ups with Lucy...and then he finds the people who stopped are Marlin and Doug.

tropes.name: Break His Heart to Save Him
tropes.html: Lucy does this to Henry to prevent him from throwing his Alaska traveling plans and walrus studying career away for her.

tropes.name: Brick Joke
tropes.html: Averted: (or done in reverse) Kevin James has a bit part as the only male in the opening sequence recounting Henry's hookups, three years before I Now Pronounce You Chuck & Larry.

tropes.name: But Liquor Is Quicker
tropes.html: Subverted. One of the male lead's seduction techniques involves plying his dates with non-alcoholic beverages but telling them they're alcoholic for a placebo effect. This lets the women lower their inhibitions without reducing cognitive function, so nobody has to feel guilty.

tropes.name: Convenient Escape Boat
tropes.html: Parodied when Henry pretends to be a CIA agent, he leaps off the dock and onto some guy's jet ski. He bribes the guy to just keep driving as if this was normal.

tropes.name: Cordon Bleugh Chef
tropes.html: Averted. Tattoo-Face suggests putting Peanut Butter Cups in Henry's eggs just because he heard they're his favorite. Henry politely declines.

tropes.name: Didn't Think This Through
tropes.html: Subverted. Henry tells Marlin they can't keep their ruse going forever because eventually Lucy will wake up one day and find she's aged years overnight. Marlin tells him he thinks about that exact thing all the time. He just doesn't have any better ideas.

tropes.name: Disability Distress
tropes.html: The film is about a young woman who suffers a car accident and develops a form of anterograde amnesia that prevents her from forming long-term memories. When she finds out about her condition, she breaks down crying and screams in anguish, with her family's dialogue implying that she suffered similar bouts of despair previously. The film's plot then revolves around her boyfriend's efforts to remind her of her condition and help her cope with it every day.

tropes.name: Discount Lesbians
tropes.html: The end credits feature Jocko the walrus and his three mates Candace, Bernice and Rose exchanging kisses between one another. Yes, this means that Jocko's three mates are all bisexual... but since they're, you know, walruses, the audience doesn't think about it too deeply.

tropes.name: Distant Finale
tropes.html: Lucy wakes up and watches the "Good morning, Lucy" video, which shows her the October 13 accident and her friends wishing her happiness as usual... except that it ends with her and Henry's wedding. And then she comes outside to find that she's on board Henry's boat to Alaska, with Henry, Marlin, and her toddler daughter, Nicole, for company.

tropes.name: Dramatic Irony
tropes.html:
The primary conflict of the film. Because Lucy's anterograde amnesia makes her unable to form new memories after a period of 24 hours, she wakes up everyday thinking that it's October 13 of the previous year. Unless she is told herself, she doesn't follow any developments of her social circle afterward, including her friends' marriage or parenthood. The most important thing, however, is that she doesn't remember ever falling in love with Henry, as to her, he's a new person everyday, even though they've been dating for weeks and possibly months. Exemplified best during a montage of the falls-in-love.
Lucy: Nothing beats a first kiss.
Henry: Yeah.
(the next day)
Lucy: Nothing beats a first kiss.
Henry: Yeah.
(repeated several times)

tropes.name: Dramedy
tropes.html: The movie deals with a soul-crushingly tragic situation, a woman with incurable amnesia, spliced with some absurd and funny moments.

tropes.name: Easy Amnesia
tropes.html: Averted. Also, Lucy is suffering from post-trauma memory loss. While it's much more common in real life, it's rarely depicted in cinema. She never gets cured in the end, and she and Henry have to use unconventional means to make the relationship work.

tropes.name: Empathic Environment
tropes.html:
• When Henry returns to the cafe for his breakfast date with Lucy it is raining. That is also when he learns about her rather tragic condition.
  • It is also raining when Henry is leaving Lucy's house after she decides to remove any mentions of him from her journal.

tropes.name: Enabled Delusion
tropes.html: After Lucy's car accident permanently damaged her short-term memory a year before the start of the film, she cannot form any long-term memories, meaning she wakes up each day believing it's the day of the accident. Her father, brother, and friends have all been acting out that day along with Lucy so she won't get upset, going so far as to refill her shampoo and conditioner every night. Deconstructed, since her loved ones have essentially had to put their lives on hold to keep up the delusion, and Henry points out how her family won't be able to keep up the act forever — eventually Lucy will wake up looking visibly older in the mirror with seemingly no explanation. Subverted when Henry comes up with the alternative solution of making her a videotape to ease her into her new existence each morning.

tropes.name: Engineered Heroics
tropes.html: Happens a couple of different ways in the movie. Among the ploys Henry uses to get Lucy to notice him are a penguin he places in the road (which she nearly kills), and his friend staging an attack on him (she beats him within an inch of his life with a baseball bat she keeps in the car). Basically, he's engineering chances for her to be heroic.

tropes.name: Even the Guys Want Him
tropes.html: In the opening monologue with the women describing their fling with Henry Roth, one of them is a man (played by Kevin James).

tropes.name: Exact Words
tropes.html:
• After Marlin makes Henry promise to stay out of the cafe, he starts engineering ways for them to meet “naturally” on the road.
  • When Henry rushes to the institute because he thinks Lucy might remember him, he asks her if she knows who he is. She tells him she doesn't. But then she shows him a gallery of paintings of him she's painted based on her dreams, showing that while she doesn't know who he is, she does remember him.

tropes.name: Faked Rip Van Winkle
tropes.html: Inverted. Lucy was in a car accident that caused anterograde amnesia, and is unable to form new memories after she goes to sleep at the end of every day, meaning every day she wakes up thinking it's the day of the accident, her father's birthday, when really it's been over a year. To minimize the shock of this, her father and brother go to great lengths to keep up the charade that it's the same day, from having fake newspapers printed out to watching a recorded football game and celebrating her dad's birthday every night and watching her present to him, a VHS of The Sixth Sense. The stress and tedium of keeping this up is starting to wear them down. This changes when Henry, a man who has been trying to date Lucy despite her condition, comes up with the idea to gracefully reveal the truth to her as soon as she wakes up every morning via a video which gives a cliff notes version of the events of the accident, her condition, and what's changed in the time since, while also showing how much her friends and family love her and are there to support her.

tropes.name: Falling-in-Love Montage
tropes.html: Which repeats itself because of Lucy's amnesia, although Henry does his best to make it different each time.

tropes.name: Foreshadowing
tropes.html:
• Hints are dropped that something is off with Lucy. On the first day she meets Henry she’s wearing a pink shirt and white pants and complements Sue’s “new” haircut. On the second morning, she’s wearing a pink shirt and white pants and complements Sue’s “new” haircut.
  • One of the books Lucy reads while enjoying her breakfast is Still Life With Woodpecker - A Sort Of A Love Story by Tom Robbins. The story of two different people managing to "make love stay" foreshadows Henry and Lucy managing a long-term relationship together despite Lucy's amnesia.

tropes.name: Funny Background Event
tropes.html: In one scene, Doug climbs to a chandelier and starts doing vertical sit-ups there. Both the chandelier and Doug then fall down.

tropes.name: Gentle Giant
tropes.html: Nick, Sue's husband and the café's fry cook, is a brick wall of a man who is nothing but friendly and easy-going. Even when Sue has him intimidate Henry, Nick is still polite about it.

tropes.name: Gory Discretion Shot
tropes.html: When Sue is telling Henry about the car accident that happened to Marlin and Lucy, in a few shots shows a pineapple flying out of the car and onto the grass, as the same time the car collides into a tree.

tropes.name: "Groundhog Day" Loop
tropes.html:
Due to Lucy's amnesia and her family’s decision to let her relive the day again and again rather than explain the truth and hurt her every morning. Sue puts it perfectly:
Sue: She eats breakfast here every morning because that’s what she did on Sundays and October 13th was a Sunday... Lucy does the same thing, every day.

tropes.name: "I Have a Boyfriend" Excuse
tropes.html: Justified and parodied with Lucy Whitmore, because she has short-term memory loss. Lucy repeatedly says that her boyfriend's name is Ringo every time Roth asks her on a date.

tropes.name: Helicopter Parents
tropes.html: Lucy's father does everything to make sure his daughter keeps reliving the same day and won't freak out. He also repeatedly tells Henry to stay away from Lucy. In the end, he joins Henry and Lucy as they leave Hawaii. Doug and the cafe denizens definitely have this vibe, too, possibly to a greater extent. Justified because of Lucy's condition. Henry actually calls Marlin out for enforcing this trope to an extreme extent by continually making Lucy living in a state of denial and not taking into factor of her future, or what would happen if she suddenly wakes up to see an old woman looking at her back from a mirror. Marlin actually has thought that part through, and dreads it. He just doesn't have any better ideas and is doing the best he can to shield her from further trauma.

tropes.name: Here We Go Again!
tropes.html:
Marlin on the day Lucy finds out the truth. His tone and Doug’s reaction says they’ve been through this many times.
Marlin: Having a bad day, Doug!

tropes.name: Hollywood Science
tropes.html:
• The exact type of amnesia depicted in film where an individual loses their memory of the last 24 hours when they wake up in the morning, referred to in the film as Goldfield Syndrome, does not exist. However, in the years since the film came out, a woman named Michelle Philpots was discovered to suffer from a case of anterograde amnesia that closely resembled the fictional condition in the film. Though in her case, she also has severe problems with memory over the course of the same day (as opposed to the film's neat "24 hour memory" plot).
  • Ten-Second Tom: there are people whose memory "resets" every few minutes or even seconds (as described by Oliver Sacks in The man who mistook his wife for a hat), but the length depends on how long they keep their current train of thought, rather than having a fixed duration.

tropes.name: Hooked Up Afterwards
tropes.html: Alexa is hitting on Doug at the wedding, though he looks noticeably uncomfortable.

tropes.name: If It's You, It's Okay
tropes.html: Might be the case with Doug and Alexa, who are paired up at Henry and Lucy's wedding.

tropes.name: I Have This Friend
tropes.html:
Used by Doug about his steroid use.
Doug: Listen, doctor, this... friend of mine's been experimenting a little with steroids. He's been having a lot of wet dreams. Could there be a connection between them?
Dr. Keats: Douglas, get off the juice. As for the nocturnal emissions, why don't you take a swim, buy a shirt with no holes, find a wahine, and take her to dinner?
Doug: I'll tell my friend you said so.

tropes.name: In the Local Tongue
tropes.html:
After Ula says something deep and meaningful sounding to Henry as they are saying goodbye:
Henry: Thanks buddy, that's beautiful. What's it mean again?
Ula: Bring me back a t-shirt.note  What makes this scene even funnier is the fact that Ula doesn't wear a shirt when he says that.

tropes.name: Internal Reveal
tropes.html: The audience already knows Lucy's predicament, but Lucy herself doesn't realize this until the expired licence plate ticket incident. Which she has to relieve every single day after for the rest of her life.

tropes.name: I Want My Beloved to Be Happy
tropes.html: This is why Lucy tries to cut Henry out of her life so he doesn't have to dedicate his life to caring for her.

tropes.name: Jerk with a Heart of Gold
tropes.html: Marlin and Doug are understandably bitter about Lucy's situation and don't take kindly to what they see as Henry taking advantage of her. However, as Henry sticks around and tries to help her recover, they warm up to him.

tropes.name: Ladykiller in Love
tropes.html: Henry's love-life consisted entirely of vacation flings with tourists until he met Lucy.

tropes.name: Laser-Guided Amnesia
tropes.html: Lucy's condition is Handwaved away as being because "she can't convert her short-term memory into long-term memory in her sleep". Basically, she is totally normal except that every time she goes to sleep, she forgets everything that happened since a car accident a year before the story starts. Her family and friends go to great lengths to keep her from noticing that years have passed since the day of her accident. When Henry learns about this, he calls bullshit on them, asking if they haven't wondered what will happen when Lucy suddenly wakes up and is in her forties.

tropes.name: Luke, You Are My Father
tropes.html: At the end of the film, Henry introduces the amnesiac Lucy to their toddler Nicole.
