tropes.name: Ambiguously Bi
tropes.html: April and Ferrari flirt with the boys, but seem to be romantically or at least sexually involved off-camera, as shown when they kiss in the limo.

tropes.name: Ambiguously Gay
tropes.html: Eli loudly performs heterosexuality but is very uncomfortable being sexual with women in practice. He also seems to get off on watching porn with his male friends, even getting touchy with with Klitz at one point.

tropes.name: Auto Erotica
tropes.html: Matt and Danielle have their first time in the back of a limo.

tropes.name: Badass Fingersnap
tropes.html: Kelly bursts into Matthew's physics classroom and instantly silences his teacher with a snap and glare in his direction.

tropes.name: Bait-and-Switch
tropes.html:
After Danielle catches Matthew peeping, she marches over and has a brief off-camera conversation with his parents. His father calls for Matthew to come downstairs, twice, and asks what he was doing in his room, in a pretty impatient tone, terrified he will chewed up for spying on Danielle... but turns out to just be volunteering Matthew to show Danielle around town.
  • At the end when Kelly is about to show Matthew's parents and principal the porn he, Eli, and Klitz shot at their prom was seemingly for Hugo Posh, but it turns out to be a sex education video featuring porn stars as "teachers".

tropes.name: Bait-and-Switch Character Intro
tropes.html: Mule first appears to be a tough guy who's about to react violently to hearing that Eli and Klitz would "use" his girl. But as soon as he hears they're porn directors, he becomes an enthusiastic advocate for hiring her, even offering for them to "give her a throw". It's double subverted in the end when he discovers they're in high school, and lives up to his "violently overprotective" vibe after all.

tropes.name: The Big Damn Kiss
tropes.html: When Matthew and Danielle share their first kiss. Matthew just takes charge and kisses Danielle; everything slows downs and they got lost in the moment.

tropes.name: Big "SHUT UP!"
tropes.html: Eli tells an audience member to "shut the FUCK up, next question!" when challenged on his age and inexperience in the Q&A he's doing in the epilogue.

tropes.name: Bigger Is Better in Bed
tropes.html: Klitz is self-conscious about his looks for most of the film, which makes public acknowledgement of his "huge" penis especially satisfying.

tropes.name: Black Comedy Rape
tropes.html: During the making of the sex ed video, one porn star says she lost her virginity at prom, then asks the other when she lost hers. She quietly replies that she was 10, then there's an awkward silence before they abruptly move on.

tropes.name: The Cameo
tropes.html:
Then-WWE wrestler Luther Reigns as Chloe's boyfriend Mule at the porn convention.
  • Porn star Steven St. Croix as the sensei in the karate porno Eli shows Matthew that Danielle stars in.

tropes.name: Can't Act Perverted Toward a Love Interest
tropes.html: Matthew refuses to watch Danielle's porn movies or sleep with her just for the hell of it, because he's genuinely in love with her.

tropes.name: The Casanova
tropes.html: Kelly seems pretty successful at this, although he may tend to go after low-hanging fruit, first flirting with some high school girls, then the middle-aged bank teller who handles Matthew's fundraising project. "This guy's unbelievable," as Matthew comments. He also used to date Danielle.

tropes.name: Chekhov's Gun
tropes.html:
• An abysmal sex education video from (apparently) the 1970s makes the heroes wonder why it's never been updated. What saves the day for them in the end? Eli directing a modern, topical, and engrossing sex education video.
  • The drawing Danielle makes Matthew when they first meet. He eventually uses it to convince her how he really sees her.

tropes.name: Chekhov's Skill
tropes.html: Eli's tendency to find and watch adult films allows him to eventually uncover Danielle's past as a pornstar.

tropes.name: Chekhov's Gunman
tropes.html: Hugo Posh, Kelly's former business partner from the porn industry.

tropes.name: Cringe Comedy
tropes.html: The segment where Matthew is briefly convinced by Eli to act like an asshole to try to seduce Danielle is kind of funny in its clumsiness, and Danielle is even amused a few times, but ultimately it's very awkward to watch.

tropes.name: Deconstructed Trope
tropes.html: Matthew gives his big damn improvised speech, after having his favorite quote stolen by his rival Ryan and being too drugged to give the one he'd prepared. It even earns a standing ovation, despite the cursing. Then Ryan wins the scholarship anyway.

tropes.name: Dirty Kid
tropes.html: Eli spends most of his free time digging up and watching adult films even with his friends beside him and merely tells them to get used to it when they become uncomfortable. This hobby makes him the first person to discover Danielle's past as a pornstar when he digs up one of her old films.

tropes.name: Distracted by the Sexy
tropes.html: When Matthew sees Danielle for the first time, he walks into a trash can and knocks it over.

tropes.name: Double Standard: Rape, Female on Male
tropes.html:
Played with. Danielle forces Matthew to strip naked and then steals his underwear, forcing him to run after the car fully nude. On the one hand, she only did it because he watched her undress (and she didn't tell his parents), but on the other, would a man forcing a teenage girl to do this be Played for Laughs?
  • That said, the fact that one of the (female) porn stars was raped as a child is also played for (very dark) laughs; see Black Comedy Rape above.

tropes.name: Do You Want to Copulate?
tropes.html:
• Danielle basically asks this of Matthew, once she realizes he's treating her like a sex worker and seems resigned to go along with it.
  • Chloe, an extremely bubbly porn star at the adult convention, thinking Eli and Klitz are porn directors, encourages them to "try me out!"

tropes.name: Establishing Character Music
tropes.html:
The movie has an extensive soundtrack, and character introductions are no exception.
  • Danielle gets a dreamlike sequence as she walks from her car to her aunt's house set to "The Killing Moon".
  • Hardcore punk track "Break Down the Walls" by Youth of Today plays as the camera takes in its first shots of Kelly striking a very intimidating pose in a wifebeater.

tropes.name: Even the Guys Want Him
tropes.html: Samnang for some reason.

tropes.name: Everyone Loves Blondes
tropes.html: The sexy outlandish adult film actress Danielle has curly blond hair.

tropes.name: Earn Your Happy Ending
tropes.html: Hugo Posh advances Matthew enough money to pay back the Samnang fund and attend Georgetown, the sex-ed video put Eli's career as a filmmaker on the map, Klitz is enjoying his new fame as a porn stud, and Danielle is finally able to escape her porn career.

tropes.name: Fanservice
tropes.html: There are more than a few nude and nearly nude attractive women in this movie.

tropes.name: Freeze-Frame Ending
tropes.html: The last shot freezes after Matt and Danielle kiss, then fades out.

tropes.name: Funny Background Event
tropes.html: While the guys are debating who will do a difficult scene, April can be seen idly blowing into a condom, and appears to have already tied one into a balloon.

tropes.name: Gilligan Cut
tropes.html: Matthew telling Danielle he is not taking his clothes off. It cuts to him standing in his underwear.

tropes.name: Girl Next Door
tropes.html: Referenced by title but ultimately averted; Danielle is a porn actress played by Elisha Cuthbert and only just met Matthew.

tropes.name: Girl-on-Girl is Hot
tropes.html: When Matthew imagines Danielle making out with his mother, and later with her two friends in the limousine.

tropes.name: Graceful Loser
tropes.html: Once Kelly finds out that Matthew was making a sex-ed film that his parents and principal approved of instead of a raunchy porno, Kelly smiles while realizing he has no cards left to play to steal Matthew's money.

tropes.name: Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold
tropes.html: Danielle has light blonde hair and is shown to be a kind and supportive girl once Matthew gets to know her.

tropes.name: Happily Ever After
tropes.html: The Sealed with a Kiss ending for Matthew and Danielle makes this such.

tropes.name: Hate Sink
tropes.html: Kelly is Danielle's ex-boyfriend and manager from the porn industry. At first he seems charming, but after Danielle leaves the industry for good because of Matt, Kelly retaliates by twice assaulting him, and tries to ruin his life by setting him up as the fall guy for theft, as well as stealing all the money Matthew raised for a charity, and finally a bungled attempt to ruin his image by showing his family a "porn video" Matthew and his friends made, which turns out to be a sex education tape.

tropes.name: Have I Mentioned I Am Sexually Active Today?
tropes.html: Eli does a twist on this where he talks a big game about wanting to have sex all the time and how he would've done it, but when the opportunity actually comes up to either touch a porn star's breast or film a sex scene with April, he gets nervous and makes excuses not to. (In both cases, Klitz does it instead.)

tropes.name: Hypocritical Humor
tropes.html:
Kelly storms into Matthew's classroom yelling at him, drags him out, then turns back around to the students and gives this priceless line:
Stay in school!

tropes.name: Imagine Spot
tropes.html:
Matthew does this a few times.
  • He imagines a disaster scenario resulting in the security guard being killed if he tried to ditch school.
  • After Matthew finds out that Danielle used to be a porn star, he has a Brain Bleach version of the trope when he imagines her making out with both his parents in front of him. Although that doesn't stop him from picturing her naked and having sex with him a few minutes later.
  • He imagines Samnang and his mother cursing a lot more than in their past communications, in reaction to his losing all the money.
  • Another disaster scenario near the end when he imagines the video production getting caught.

tropes.name: Implausible Deniability
tropes.html: During the gang's post-mortem of Matthew's attempt to date Danielle, Eli smirks that bringing her to a motel "was a little forward", despite being the one to convince Matthew to try it, then acts oblivious at Matt's incredulous reaction.

tropes.name: Ironic Echo
tropes.html:
"It's like a gift, you know? It's like I can't control it..."
  • It's not emphasized, but Matthew explains his attempt to extremely awkwardly seduce Danielle with "just chillin'", the same response she gave after bringing him to a party he had no interest in.
  • When Matthew first meets Kelly, Kelly asks what he wants to do later in life, to which Matthew responds that he wants to be president. Kelly tells him that the first rule of being a politician is to make sure "the juice is worth the squeeze." At the end of the film, as Kelly prepares to shoot a very low budget porno movie, he opens a cigar box from Matthew with a note that reads "the juice was worth the squeeze," causing him to smile.
  • One of the jocks tries to eject Matthew from a house party by saying it's getting too full, and he has to go. Later Matthew uses the same line to reject him from the porn/sex ed video shoot.

tropes.name: Jaded Professional
tropes.html:
Mr. Salinger, Matthew's principal, does still try to do his job, but he doesn't seem too upbeat about it.
"The hell with it. The kids today are so goddamn screwed up, maybe this is the only way you can reach 'em."

tropes.name: Jerkass
tropes.html: Danielle's ex, Kelly.

tropes.name: Literally Loving Thy Neighbor
tropes.html: It's easy for Matthew to fall into this when his beautiful neighbor leaves her shades open while changing. Also what the title is referring to rather than the Girl Next Door trope, which is not present.

tropes.name: Manic Pixie Dream Girl
tropes.html: Danielle comes off this way initially, and certainly has this effect on Matthew. However, she herself is more complex and pragmatic than she first appears.

tropes.name: Mood Whiplash
tropes.html: Kelly tends to cause this, unpredictably veering between smirkingly friendly and not-playing-anymore scary. Most prominently, he goes from seemingly pressuring Matthew to give him a blowjob, to laughing about how he was just kidding, to punching Matthew in the head, in the space of about 10 seconds.

tropes.name: Not What It Looks Like
tropes.html: The tape that Matthew, Danielle and the others filmed on prom night. It was a sex-ed video, not porn.

tropes.name: Mr. Vice Guy
tropes.html: Hugo Posh. He's a wealthy porn director and comes off as more than a little sleazy towards Danielle, but next to Kelly, he seems like a pretty solid Reasonable Authority Figure who actually goes out of his way to help Matthew make his sex ed video, and even makes him a silent partner when he distributes it.

tropes.name: Ms. Fanservice
tropes.html:
Danielle subverts this once it's revealed that she wants to escape that life. Notably for a film with a lot of explicit nudity, she is never shown fully nude.
  • Danielle's porn star friends April and Ferrari fit the trope more, both in the context of the film and in-universe. They both show full nudity and at one point they make out in front of the boys even off-camera.

tropes.name: Nerds Are Virgins
tropes.html: While this isn't explicit in the film, the director's commentary mentions that Matthew is losing his virginity during his and Danielle's first time.

tropes.name: Official Couple
tropes.html: Matthew and Danielle.

tropes.name: Oh, Crap!
tropes.html:
• When Chloe's boyfriend finds out that Klitz and Eli are in high school.
  • When Matthew finds out Kelly cleaned out the Samnang bank account.

tropes.name: Orbital Kiss
tropes.html: The Big Damn Kiss.

tropes.name: Phrase Catcher
tropes.html: Danielle elicits "Dude..." "I know" at least three times among guys who witness her. Once each upon being introduced to Eli and Klitz in a wet T-shirt, and again between the two of them when Matthew goes for his Big Damn Kiss.

tropes.name: Politically Incorrect Villain
tropes.html: Kelly expresses casually racist views towards Asian people.

tropes.name: Reasonable Authority Figure
tropes.html: Surprisingly enough, Hugo Posh. He forgives Matthew for stealing his trophy when he learns that he was set up by Kelly and lets him go, and also helps him make a sex ed video with pornstars under his payroll, and even makes him a silent partner, giving him enough money both to help Samnang get to the States and for Matthew to pay for his education at Georgetown.

tropes.name: Sarcastic Confession
tropes.html: When Matthew's parents ask Eli if his and Klitz's porn star prom dates go to their school, Eli just says "No... they're porn stars", and everybody laughs.

tropes.name: Sealed with a Kiss
tropes.html: Matthew and Danielle end the movie with a kiss.

tropes.name: Sexy Soaked Shirt
tropes.html: Invoked by Danielle who turns up on Klitzy's doorstep with a damp blouse (from being in the pool). "I'm all wet, can I come in?"

tropes.name: Sex Miseducation Class
tropes.html: The sex education film that the school uses seemed to have been made sometime in the 1970s and warns of the dangers of premarital sex. Later, when Kelly shows up at Matthew's house to show the movie he and Danielle's friends filmed at the high school to his parents and the principal, it features Danielle's porn star friends narrating an actual sex-ed video that is more relevant to the modern day.

tropes.name: Shameful Strip
tropes.html: Light-hearted example when Danielle forces Matthew to strip in public in front of her, as punishment for spying on her changing. And then she steals his underwear and drives away. (But only briefly.)

tropes.name: Shout-Out
tropes.html: Eli coaches Ferrari for her porn/sex ed video shoot by reminding her "think Meryl Streep, Sophie's Choice."

tropes.name: Single Woman Seeks Good Man
tropes.html: Danielle's attraction to Matthew is his genuinely kindhearted nature. He sees her as a person first and foremost and is willing to move heaven and earth to get her out of her old life.

tropes.name: Sir Swears-a-Lot
tropes.html: Kelly is by far the most potty-mouthed character in the film and is so vulgar that he has to catch himself before swearing out loud while posing as an authority figure around Matthew's parents.

tropes.name: Sleeves Are for Wimps
tropes.html: Kelly's introduction is an aggressive rock-backed sequence of shots highlighting Timothy Olyphant's sharply dressed lower half contrasting with his wifebeater-clad torso, muscular tattooed arms and Perma-Stubble and all. It rivals Danielle's introduction for hammering home a first impression, and would almost qualify as Female Gaze if not for the fact that it's Matthew's point of view and leans more toward "intimidating" than "sexy". Or at least, intimidating in addition to sexy.

tropes.name: Slow Clap
tropes.html: Downplayed after Matthew's improvised scholarship speech about not being a fucking boy scout and fighting for something (someone) where the juice is worth the squeeze, there's only scattered applause in the first few moments, but more and more people join in until there's a standing ovation.

tropes.name: Slow-Motion Drop
tropes.html: Well, it's a Solo cup, so it doesn't actually shatter when it hits the grass, but Danielle drops her beer when Matthew finally works up the nerve to give her The Big Damn Kiss, and the camera does watch it slosh around in slow motion.

tropes.name: Smug Snake
tropes.html: Kelly.

tropes.name: So Bad, It's Good
tropes.html: In-universe, Mr. Salinger is repulsed by the sex ed tape and calls it "atrocious", but he acknowledges that the tapes they've been showing to the kids at school have been mostly ineffective, and as such, was willing to let it be shown at the school.

tropes.name: Spiky Hair
tropes.html: Kelly. Notably when he's pretending to be a less-shady character in front of Matthew's parents, his hair is slicked down.

tropes.name: Stage Names
tropes.html: Danielle's porn star name is Athena.

tropes.name: Their First Time
tropes.html: Matthew and Danielle have sex for the first time in a limo. In the director's commentary, Luke Greenfield describes it as follows: "This scene. My first love scene I have ever shot was a scene of loss of innocence. Matthew's losing his virginity, and Danielle's making love for the very first time."

tropes.name: Throwing Out the Script
tropes.html: Matthew appears to do this, but it's a subversion. While it appears this way to the audience (who think he's incredibly sweet), he actually has nothing written down. He'd been too busy slacking off (and, in fairness, falling in love and learning life lessons) to write the speech.

tropes.name: Threat Backfire
tropes.html: Ever since Danielle started getting friendly with Matthew, Kelly warned him not to steal his top performer or he would make him regret it. Near the end, Kelly finds out that they, Matthew's friends from school, and Danielle's porn star friends made a movie, and he shows up at Matthew's house to show the film they made in school to his parents and the principal. It works out at the end since the movie was a comprehensive sex ed video that was more in tune to the modern day, as opposed to the original film which was at least thirty years old and warned of the dangers of premarital sex. The principal decides they will use Matthew's video, and the latter also makes a fortune when he signs a deal with a competing porn company to distribute the video.

tropes.name: Title Drop
tropes.html: Early on, said by Matthew on the phone to Eli, to clarify (in a bit of ironic Foreshadowing) that he is not watching dirty movies, but rather a girl in real life. At the end, Matthew's final answer to the yearbook fill-in-the-blank "I will always remember..."

tropes.name: Trailers Always Spoil
tropes.html: It's actually a while before Danielle is revealed to be a porn star in the film, but none of the marketing makes any secret of it.

tropes.name: Two-Person Pool Party
tropes.html: Daniele and Matthew have one by sneaking into a neighbor's backyard. It gets ruined when the homeowner returns home. And he is Matthew's school principal.

tropes.name: What the Hell, Hero?
tropes.html: "Is this what you think of me?"

tropes.name: Whip Pan
tropes.html: Matthew grabs the adult film award in Hugo's house and turns to leave, glancing over Hugo's kitchen, sculpture, nearly naked man, plant, parrot... then whips back to look at Hugo staring at him wearing nothing but his briefs.

tropes.name: Worthy Opponent
tropes.html: When Kelly finally runs out of cards to play, he silently acknowledges Matt as this with a smile.

tropes.name: Abortion Fallout Drama
tropes.html: Paul learns his wife Mary had undergone an abortion when they had separated in the past. Seeing as she's trying to get artificially inseminated in a last-ditch effort to get pregnant when Paul finds out, his angered reaction is justified.

tropes.name: Abusive Parents
tropes.html: In an Establishing Character Moment, Jack not only lets his son hit his daughter, but forces her to take another hit, quoting scripture. Then hitting his son for his act to begin with.

tropes.name: Anachronic Order
tropes.html: For example, the reactions of the other two in the motel after Paul shot himself is seen about a half-hour in. Though the plot becomes more understandable about an hour in.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Biology
tropes.html: Iñárritu and Arriaga even admit that they used the "losing twenty-one grams" motif as a form of this.

tropes.name: The Atoner
tropes.html: Deconstructed with Jack. He genuinely wants to do good and atone for his actions, but comes across as condescending, hypocritical, and selfish, not really thinking how his actions will affect his family.

tropes.name: Babies Ever After
tropes.html: Rare dark example. Christina is pregnant with Paul's baby, but the news is broken at the same time he dies.

tropes.name: Billy Needs an Organ
tropes.html: Paul, due to a heart condition.

tropes.name: Bittersweet Ending
tropes.html: Albeit a borderline Downer Ending. On one hand, Jack reunites with his family after his BSOD, but Paul, in the midst of having a heart attack due to his heart failing him, shoots himself in the chest, leading Jack and Christina to rush him to the hospital. It's too late, Paul dies, and the conflict between Paul and Christina is unresolved.

tropes.name: City with No Name
tropes.html: The city that the characters live in is unidentified, though implied to be Memphis, Tennessee (where the film was shot).

tropes.name: Driven to Suicide
tropes.html: Jack and Paul both attempt suicide, the former in prison, the latter in the climax. Paul is the only one who succeeds.

tropes.name: Flipping the Bird
tropes.html: Cristina's sister does this to her when Cristina walks away from her at the pool.

tropes.name: Grey-and-Grey Morality
tropes.html: Jack is a man who wants to do good, but comes off as selfish and hypocritical, Paul is stalking Christina, and it may seem that Christina is the most sympathetic main character, until she ropes Paul into trying to kill Jack.

tropes.name: Heel–Faith Turn
tropes.html: Jack Jordan (Benicio del Toro), but whether he's really better than before becomes a critical question of the film.<!--* TheHeroDies: [[spoiler:Paul.]]-->

tropes.name: Holier than Thou
tropes.html:
• Jack, or at least he tries to be.
  • Zig-Zagged with Reverend John. In his sermons, he definitely sounds this way, but he has more of a common touch, and is less unyielding (when Jack acts this way towards a kid at the church, Reverend John points out, "He's just a kid!").

tropes.name: Irony
tropes.html: Mary's (Paul's wife) motivation is getting his sperm so she can have his child. Christina is the one who ends up impregnated by Paul.

tropes.name: R-Rated Opening
tropes.html: The first shot is Paul smoking a cigarette next to a sleeping Christina. Both are naked.<!--* ShootTheShaggyDog-->

tropes.name: Sliding Scale of Idealism vs. Cynicism
tropes.html: As per the director's other works, this is far on the cynical end.

tropes.name: Stalker with a Crush
tropes.html: Paul follows Christina around for a while without revealing how he knows her.

tropes.name: Absurdicorn
tropes.html: Colt drinks a "dirtied" Shirley Temple at a night club, and starts to experience a Mushroom Samba of heightened colors and impact special effects, and seeing unicorns. After he chases down the guy who drugs him, the dealer gives him the information he was looking and mentions that if he's still seeing unicorns the drug is still working, implying that hallucination is very specific for the unnamed drug.

tropes.name: Accidental Murder
tropes.html: Ryder, attempting to prove that he's capable of doing his own stunts, challenges his then-stunt double Henry Herrera to a fight, in the process kicking Henry off camera, who falls on furniture and breaks his neck. His and Gail's efforts to sweep it under the rug lead them to bring Colt over to Australia to serve as an unwitting patsy.

tropes.name: The Ace
tropes.html: Colt is a certified badass. Not only is he a very successful stuntman, but he can hold his own in a real fight even while drugged, and can think on his feet with creative solutions even in the most stressful situations such as shouting for help when Ryder's goons start drenching him in gasoline just so he can get a mouthful of it, which he then spits into the goon's lighter to get an opportunity to escape. The only failure he ever had understandably put him out of the game for a good while, and it turns out the stunt's failure wasn't even his fault, or a freak accident, it was sabotage.

tropes.name: Action Survivor
tropes.html:
• Jody Moreno, despite not being a trained fighter like Colt, can really hold her own. Successfully attacking and taking down Colt when she mistook him for an attacker even stabbing him in the leg with a pen. Though to be fair, he was in a big, non-flexible alien costume and he didn't want to actually harm her. She also is able to hold herself against an armed Gail and a professional armed mook, knocking him out with a prop weapon.
  • Alma, a personal assistant with no combat experience, is able to successfully fight off one of Tom's goons with Jean Claude's help.

tropes.name: Actor Allusion
tropes.html: This isn't the first, or even the second time Ryan Gosling plays a Stunt Performer, although this time his job is more in focus and he's a straightforward hero instead of an Anti-Hero/Anti-Villain.

tropes.name: Actually Pretty Funny
tropes.html: When Colt starts doing reckless stunts with an obnoxious customer's car while working as a valet, the customer's date looks amused by the show.

tropes.name: Adaptational Job Change
tropes.html: In the TV series, Jody is a fellow stunt performer alongside Colt. In the film, she starts as a camera operator and becomes a film director.

tropes.name: Adaptational Nationality
tropes.html: Jody, an American in the TV series, is British in the film.

tropes.name: Adaptation Name Change
tropes.html: Jody's last name is changed from "Banks" in the TV series to "Moreno" in the film.

tropes.name: Adapted Out
tropes.html: Howie Munson, (Colt's Cousin and stuntman in training) Big Jack and Terri Michaels (The bail bonds women from the series) aren't even mentioned in the film, despite being strong supporting characters from the TV show.

tropes.name: Addled Addict
tropes.html: It goes without saying that Tom Ryder's Hookers and Blow lifestyle has seriously dented his decision-marking skills and possibly also his acting chops, turning him into a complete diva who's impossible to work when he even bothers to show up. He also killed his second stuntman Henry by accident after getting into an ill-advised altercation with him during a drug and alcohol-laden party.

tropes.name: Affably Evil
tropes.html: Iggy shares a friendly, if slightly condescending, conversation with Colt after having just tried to fight him off with a prop sword. She's later revealed to have been involved with Tom and Gail's plan and helped to cover up Henry's death.

tropes.name: The Aggressive Drug Dealer
tropes.html: Played with, Doone, Ryder's dealer complains that "no one ever wants to know how the drug dealer is doing". While he was tasked with drugging Colt to help the Frame-Up, he's also quick to fold and tells Colt where he needs to go.

tropes.name: Alcohol-Induced Idiocy
tropes.html: Tom Ryder and his stunt double Henry have been drinking and then some when a party goer asks Ryder if he does his own stunts, which prompts Tom to have an impromptu show off of his skills culminating in a kick to Henry's chest which causes him to fall over and break his neck.

tropes.name: Arc Symbol
tropes.html: The "Thumbs Up" gesture, universal in the stunt community to let people know you're okay after rolling a truck or slamming into a boulder. Colt later turns it around explaining no stuntman ever wants to admit they're hurt, and a "Thumbs Down" is the worst thing imaginable for them.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Film Production
tropes.html: The movie exaggerates and speeds up the process of how a film is made. Colt shows up and is immediately recruited for a car flip being done that day, when such drivers are usually involved in the planning stages for accountability purposes. Pyrotechnics are also being set off as pranks, which would be a quick way to get fired. The film shows three different filming locations, one on a beach, one on the steps of the Sydney Opera House and one at what looks like a modified quarry/sand dunes and is said to be the final filming day, when all three locations look to be epic set pieces and would spend weeks at each one. All that said, the film generally winks at these inconsistencies and includes several things going wrong that feel like it is taken from real-life incidents.

tropes.name: As Himself
tropes.html: Jason Momoa makes a cameo appearance as Tom Ryder's replacement following Tom being exposed as a murderer and accidentally blowing himself up near the end of the movie.

tropes.name: As You Know
tropes.html: Played with during Colt's opening narration: "She's talkin' about Tom Ryder, who happens to be the biggest action star on the pl... Wait, why am I explaining this? You know who Tom Ryder is. He's Tom Ryder."

tropes.name: Attaque Animal
tropes.html: Jean-Claude is a stunt dog that is trained to follow instructions in French, most notably "Attaque" which will cause him to perform a Groin Attack.

tropes.name: Attention Whore
tropes.html: Tom Ryder is the biggest movie star in the world and revels in the attention. Stuntmen like Colt and Dan joke behind his back at how Ryder brags about doing his own stunts, while bullying the stuntmen who actually do it when he feels they’re stealing the limelight from him. He even attempts to murder stuntmen on two separate occasions for getting more attention than him, and succeeds in one.

tropes.name: Bad "Bad Acting"
tropes.html: Tom Ryder's "Metalstorm" monologue in the leadup to the final battle. While it's not THAT apparent Ryder isn't very gifted as an actor, the delivery of the speech is nowhere near as powerful as he comes away thinking it is. This is even lampshaded at the end of the film when Ryder's replacement leading man - Jason Momoa - recites similar lines with the same staging and makes it sound MUCH more effective and rousing.

tropes.name: Batman Gambit
tropes.html: Colt pulls one off in the space of seconds as Tom's goons are dousing him with gasoline to set him on fire and kill him. He starts yelling for help loudly, and one of them pours it directly into his mouth to shut him up. Just as the thug is starting up a lighter to do the deed, Colt sprays out the mouthful of gasoline and sets him on fire instead, making a distraction that allows him to escape.

tropes.name: Big Bad Duumvirate
tropes.html: Ryder and Gail. The former is responsible for the inciting incident by accidentally killing his Metalstorm stunt double Henry, while the latter plans the cover-up and gets the idea to frame Colt for the murder.

tropes.name: Big Badass Battle Sequence
tropes.html: Metalstorm has several, and a fair chunk of the plot is devoted to filming them.

tropes.name: The Big Damn Kiss
tropes.html: Colt and Jody share an epic one after all the action is finally over and they get back together, complete with explosions going off in the background.

tropes.name: Big "NO!"
tropes.html: Tom lets out an epic one when Colt leaps out of the helicopter with the recording of Tom confessing to his crimes in hand.

tropes.name: Blatant Lies
tropes.html:
• Tom insists he does all his own stunts directly in front of his stuntman.
  • Colt tells Jody that the day-glo night club clothes are exercise clothes and his injuries are from just going out for a run.

tropes.name: Bookends
tropes.html:
• The film begins with Colt performing a stunt fall, which goes wrong and ends up breaking his back, halting his career as a stuntman and ending his relationship with Jody. The final action scene ends with Colt legitimately leaping out of the helicopter that Gail and Tom are trying to flee in, with the incriminating recording of Tom's Engineered Public Confession in hand, landing safely in a crash pad that the stunt performers had hastily placed beneath the aircraft. Then the reunited Colt and Jody celebrate with a Big Damn Kiss.
  • In Colt’s opening narration, he describes his relationship with Jody as something you only find in the movies. He revises this statement in his closing narration: what he has with Jody is even better than what you find in the movies.

tropes.name: Brick Joke
tropes.html:
• While Colt and Dan are searching the hundreds of Post-its covering Ryder's home looking for the password for his phone, they come across one of them that has "Ma-moa or Mo-moa?" written on it. Come the final scene of the movie, and an In-Universe trailer reveals that Jason Momoa has replaced Ryder as the star of the now completed Metalstorm.
  • When Colt is trying to get answers from Alma, she demands a producer's credit in the movie as her price. The aforementioned trailer has a very gratuitous producer's credit in her name during the middle of the trailer, and the post-credits scene reveals that her swiping the previous producer's phone to send a well-timed call to Jason Momoa's agent may have saved the picture.

tropes.name: The Brute
tropes.html: Dressler. Both Colt and Dan despite their best efforts can't put him down with regular fisticuffs. Ultimately, Dan has to resort to a wire rig to throw and suspend Dressler in mid-air.

tropes.name: Bunny-Ears Lawyer
tropes.html: Despite being an awful and deeply weird human being, Tom actually is a pretty good actor according to the rest of the cast.

tropes.name: Butt-Monkey
tropes.html: Nigel, the set supervisor for Metalstorm, gets zero respect from the rest of the crew and repeatedly gets undermined by everyone else, though Jody notes that it is partly his own fault since he keeps yelling at the crew members abusively instead of actually trying to communicate with them. He does get to catch a bit of a break when Venti expresses attraction to him while watching his terrible, yet passionate karaoke cover of "Genie In a Bottle", and it's implied they might become an item.

tropes.name: Calling Your Attacks
tropes.html: In a fight, Dan copies fighting moves from different movies and yells the name of the actor who did them as he does so, such as Daniel Day-Lewis and Dwayne Johnson.

tropes.name: The Cameo
tropes.html:
• Logan Holladay, the stunt man who did the car rolling stunt is shown as the assistant who both straps Ryan Gosling in, and is the first to come pull him out of the car.
  • Lee Majors and Heather Thomas, the stars of the original show, appear briefly in The Stinger as movie police officers who "arrest" Gail and Tom.
  • At the end of the movie during the Comic-Con trailer for Metalstorm, it is revealed that Jason Momoa has replaced Ryder as the film's lead.

tropes.name: Camera Abuse
tropes.html: While filming a scene on a beach where the car is going to roll, Colt struggles to keep the right distance from a lead car and ends up hitting the camera mounted on a jib. The scene is still in motion and they have seven other cameras so they elect to keep going. Colt outright warns them this was a risk beforehand, and suggests shooting the scene at a different time when the sand is easier to drive on.

tropes.name: Career-Ending Injury
tropes.html: Early on in the film, Colt suffers one from a fall stunt gone wrong, leading him to cut himself off from Jody and the film industry because he no longer felt confident in his own abilities and safety standards. It is later revealed that Tom sabotaged the stunt himself, due to him feeling that Colt was showing his face too much during the stunt and stealing the spotlight from him. Also subverted, as Colt walks on to the new set and immediately performs a world-record car stunt while still jet-lagged from his plane trip over there. He then spends the rest of the film doing various amazing feats both on-set and in his real life. If he has any ongoing limitations from his fall, it's never apparent.

tropes.name: Car Fu
tropes.html: Inverted, Colt uses his body to stop a car, specifically, performing a stunt roll over the hood of a taxi to scare the driver into stopping so he can get to the passenger.

tropes.name: Casting Gag
tropes.html: Just the fact that Metalstorm ultimately ends up casting Jason Momoa as the lead is this if only for his role as part of the main cast of Dune (2021), which inspires this In-Universe fictional production.

tropes.name: Celebrity Paradox
tropes.html:
• Most of the Metalstorm stunt crew wear jackets with a logo of 87North Productions, David Leitch's production company that also produced this film.
  • One of Tom's many Post-It notes around his apartment says "Download Bullet Train", another film directed by Leitch and also starring Aaron Taylor-Johnson.

tropes.name: Chekhov's Gun
tropes.html:
• When Cole first visits Tom's condo on the waterfront, right next to it is a large yacht. That is where Tom has been hiding all this time, which Cole finds out later jumping from a crane onto the yacht.
  • A literal example: one of the props from Tom's movies that's in his condo is a pistol which Colt examines, taking out the magazine and seeing it's labeled as only holding blanks. When he needs a "weapon" later, Colt takes the prop gun and briefly "uses it" against a goon but is disarmed and shot with it, doing a stunt fall to fake being killed. When the goon's back is turned, he takes the opportunity to make an escape.
  • Jody is seen at one point watching footage of Ryder, who is complaining about how uncomfortable and sweaty his costume is, noting that he has a habit of forgetting that he has been fitted with a microphone. This is how he is ultimately undone, when Colt traps him in a stunt car and gets him to confess to his crimes, forgetting that he is wired and Jody is recording him.

tropes.name: Chekhov's Skill
tropes.html:
• Colt began his career as a stuntman at the Miami Vice Action Spectacular at Universal Studios, and still wears the crew jacket every day. Said show apparently included him driving an exploding speedboat on a jump and diving off unseen just before the explosion, several times a day, so he was able to put these skills to use to fake his death when pursued by Ryder's goons in Sydney harbor. He'd also gotten so good at the stunt that he can do it with his hands tied behind his back, which is exactly what he needs to do.
  • Colt knows that Tom's dog is trained to attack by biting people in the groin, but only if the commands are given in French.

tropes.name: Company Cross-References
tropes.html:
• The film opens with a montage of stunt sequences from various movies, one of them being the train escape scene from Fast Five, another Universal release.
  • Colt is a veteran of a Miami Vice stunt show at Universal Studios.
  • Colt and Dan both mention doing “Jason Bourne shit”, Bourne being another Universal Studios protagonist.
  • A Shrek cosplayer appears at the Metalstorm SDCC panel.

tropes.name: Complexity Addiction
tropes.html: After accidentally killing his current stunt double, Tom and Gail come up with an overly complicated plan to bring Colt to Australia and frame him for the death… but using his yacht and the large number of ruthless mercenaries he currently employs as security to simply dispose of the body and then track down and dispose of all the video apparently never crosses his mind.

tropes.name: Conversational Troping
tropes.html: The movie is not shy about discussing various tropes. Colt gets a call from Jody where she discusses Split Screen as a cliche and when she says she thinks she'll do it the scene becomes a split screen of her and Colt. One even suggests they patch over a weak third act by having the characters in the movie comment on weak third acts.

tropes.name: Counting Bullets
tropes.html: In the final showdown, Colt gives Gail a smirk after she takes the gun from the reluctant Tom, and tells her she's out of bullets. Then he jumps out of the helicopter anyway.

tropes.name: The Cover Changes the Meaning
tropes.html: Blake Shelton's cover of "The Unknown Stuntman" (the original series' theme tune) that plays on the end credits changes the lyrics from Colt talking about how his work as a stuntman is an unsung and painful job to a romantic ballad.

tropes.name: Creative Closing Credits
tropes.html: The end credits are styled like a script (just like the opening credits).

tropes.name: Creator Breakdown
tropes.html: invoked When Jody sees Colt on set, she has him do numerous takes of being set on fire and thrown by wires into a boulder. In between takes, she takes time in front of the entire crew to explain the whole story to Colt, a Star-Crossed Lovers angle where the Space Cowboy just stops talking to Aliana and disappears. It's quite evident this movie is her trying to deal with the fallout of their relationship.

tropes.name: Creator Cameo
tropes.html: The stunt team for Metalstorm all wear jackets indicating they work for 87 North, the production company for the actual film, in the climax.

tropes.name: Cringe Comedy
tropes.html: There's a sequence where Jody, absolutely furious with Colt for appearing on set after ghosting her for 18 months and leaving her heartbroken, forces him to do an incredibly painful stunt while she "gives him a script read" about the love lives of the main leads falling apart and failing to give the Show Within a Show a Downer Ending, which is totally not based on her and Colt's relationship. This is in front of nearly all the production crew, and even the stunt performers in the alien suits are visibly cringing. On top of this, an extra tries to break up the awkwardness by jumping in with how this was exactly like the time he fell in love with his wife's sister, to which Colt reacts by taking back the megaphone.

tropes.name: Cut Apart
tropes.html: After a particularly good film shoot showing that Colt and Jody are starting to get their spark back, Jody invites Colt to go to karaoke with her, which he accepts. Before he is able to go, he gets caught up in a giant action set piece involving a French dog and truck. Thinking that he has ditched her when he doesn't show up, Jody begins to sing a song that intercuts with Colt trying to survive. You even see the truck drive by through the window of the bar. Finally, Colt stops the bad guys and rushes back to the bar just as Jody finishes her number. Except by the time he arrives, most of the film crew, including Jody, had already left with only Dan and a few others still there.

tropes.name: Damsel out of Distress
tropes.html: Ryder's kidnapped P.A. Alma manages to beat up one of her kidnappers and knock him out of the truck, although the truck would have then crashed without Colt's intervention and he also distracts some other thugs who would have been able to help the one Alma was fighting.

tropes.name: Dented Iron
tropes.html: Colt suffered a really hard hit in the opening scene, requiring surgery and some rehabilitation. This doesn't appear to directly impact his current physical abilities, but has shaken his confidence. This is related to an underlying theme of the film in that stuntmen refuse to admit they are hurt.

tropes.name: Dies Wide Open
tropes.html: When Tom accidentally kills his stunt double while they were both high on drugs, the latter's eyes are still open as he lies motionless on the floor. This persists when Colt finds his corpse on ice in a bathtub.

tropes.name: Digital Head Swap
tropes.html: Given it's a film about a Stunt Double on a big-budget movie, this comes up several times in the plot. Most notably, Jody takes advantage of Tom Ryder's absence and Colt's presence to film bigger, more impressive action scenes and then replace Colt's face with Ryder's in post, because Colt is much better at filming action scenes. After The Reveal, we see that Gail has used a Digital Head Swap to frame Colt for an Accidental Murder.invoked

tropes.name: Disney Acid Sequence
tropes.html: While at a nightclub looking for Tom, Colt is drugged and fights off several goons while high, with the lighting effect becoming very trippy and sparks flying away from every impact. Even after it dies down, he still hallucinates a full-sized unicorn.

tropes.name: Disproportionate Retribution
tropes.html: Colt suffers a horrible injury that he feels is his fault, so he leaves the stunt business and Jody, until a year and a half later when he is effectively tricked into working on her movie. Jody's response is to force him into several takes of a dangerous stunt out of pure pettiness and spend the time between takes passive-aggressively lashing out at him in front of the entire cast and crew. His accident was itself a result of this as Ryder sabotaged the stunt because he felt Colt was stealing his spotlight.

tropes.name: Does This Remind You of Anything?
tropes.html: Though the plot of the movie is outright shown to be Jody's attempt to work through her complicated feelings about Colt and how their relationship ended, one scene that hammers this in without the two even realizing it is when they are discussing the plot of the movie over the phone with a split-screen shot (that they moments earlier just discussed the benefits of doing such a shot). While they are talking, Jody absent-mindedly puts on a prosthetic alien arm, highlighting that the alien in her movie represents her while they discuss what the arc of the movie should be (and by extension where their relationship should go).

tropes.name: Double-Meaning Title
tropes.html: Colt works as a "fall guy" – i.e. a stuntman, taking falls (and hits, and fire). We eventually learn he's being set up to take the fall for an Accidental Murder.

tropes.name: Dramatic Spine Injury
tropes.html:
Ryder challenges Henry, his stunt double, to a fight while both of them are high on drugs at a party, and things take a turn for the worst when Henry is kicked back and smacks the back of his neck on a side table, breaking his upper spine and killing him instantly.
  • Downplayed with Colt's accident at the start of the movie which later was revealed also caused by Ryder where he seemingly makes a full recovery but loses his confidence and left ashamed that he got badly hurt.

tropes.name: Drives Like Crazy
tropes.html: When he's given the keys to a car early on, Colt's asked to take it easy, since the giver "knows how you stunties drive!" The rest of the film proves him right; Colt seems to enjoy wild turns and doughnuts even when it's not part of his job.

tropes.name: Early-Bird Cameo
tropes.html: When Colt searches through Tom Ryder's luxury apartment, a freeze frame on Ryder's assortment of Post-It notes shows one reading "Is it Momoa or Mamoa" which ends up foreshadowing Jason Momoa's eventually replacing Ryder as the star of "Metalstorm".

tropes.name: Earn Your Happy Ending
tropes.html: After much deliberation over the ending of Metalstorm, Jody's rekindled romance with Colt convinces her to give the Space Cowboy and Aliana a Happily Ever After ending to their relationship after much hardship. Exposing and ridding the picture of Tom and Gail and a timely phone call to Jason Momoa's agent also save the film, which is a big success that lays the groundwork for Colt and Jody to keep doing what they love together.

tropes.name: Engineered Public Confession
tropes.html: While not exactly a live broadcast, Colt and Jody are able to trick Tom into confessing his crimes by forcing him into doing a dangerous stunt while forgetting his microphone is still on.

tropes.name: Executive Meddling
tropes.html: In-Universe, Jody's original vision for Metalstorm ended with the Space Cowboy and Aliana failing to rekindle their relationship. However, the studio executives have been pressuring her to give the couple a happy ending as it will play better with the intended audience.

tropes.name: Extremely Short Timespan
tropes.html: The bulk of the film takes place over about four days. Gail had Colt in Australia overnight and we are shown only three days of filming.

tropes.name: Evil Is Petty
tropes.html:
• Tom nearly killed Colt and ended his career by sabotaging his fall stunt at the start of the movie, simply because he thought Colt pointed his face toward the camera too much and thus needed a "lesson" even when Colt was redoing the stunt to correct this. He then inadvertently kills Henry after the latter made a mocking remark about Tom never doing his own stunts.
  • Gail just to protect her own company from scandal while also protecting Ryder from being exposed for killing someone in an egotistical, drunken temper tantrum manipulates Colt—just because he's considered expendable as the lowly stuntman—into danger so as to pin it all on him while also manipulating Jody against him while making her also think nothing is wrong at the same time too.

tropes.name: Fall Guy
tropes.html:
• Obviously, there's Colt, who is being set up to take the blame for Ryder's disappearance. It turns out to be more complex than a simple case of framing him by being the most convenient suspect: everything, from suddenly being forced into joining Jody's crew, the 3D scanning and mocap work, and being asked to investigate Ryder's disappearance were part of an elaborate plan to deepfake him into being the main suspect for an apparent manslaughter that Ryder committed.
  • Jody is set up to become blamed for an engineered Troubled Production that'll cover up Ryder's crime. The producer forces Colt into her movie, demands a recut of the third act that's heavily implied to be an awful ending, makes a big stink of Colt apparently killing a stuntman to poison the movie's rep, and tries to get her to 'take a vacation' so she, and by extension the studio, can screw up her first movie and pin everything that went wrong with the movie on her.invoked

tropes.name: Film Within a Film
tropes.html: Metalstorm, the film that Jody and Colt are making, is essentially a remake of Metalstorm: The Destruction of Jared-Syn and can best be described as a cross between Mad Max: Fury Road and Dune (with non-humanoid aliens). We see snippets of the final film through the production.

tropes.name: Five-Second Foreshadowing
tropes.html: While scrolling through Tom's videos of himself, he's shown doing a monologue from Richard III. A minute later, he's revealed to have accidentally killed Henry and kicked off the whole plot, and a scene later he's revealed to be one of the main villains.

tropes.name: Freeze-Frame Bonus
tropes.html: Ryder's Post-it covered apartment. Among them are "Shark Attack" and "Penis Enlargement."

tropes.name: Friendship Moment
tropes.html: Dan decides to forgo his turn during karaoke night to help Colt track down Tom, getting himself involved in numerous dangerous fights in order to help his friend. He later assembles the rest of the stunt crew to fight off Tom's security detail while Colt and Jody are preoccupied with getting a confession out of him.

tropes.name: The Friend Nobody Likes
tropes.html: None of the Metalstorm cast and crew, with the possible exception of Iggy, likes Tom due to his diva antics on set and overinflated ego. Even Gail, his longtime producer and staunchest ally, readily admits that he's an asshole, not that it stops her from conspiring to cover up the Accidental Murder of his previous stuntman.

tropes.name: Gaslighting
tropes.html: Gail makes extensive use of this to manipulate and bamboozle both Colt and Jody combined with sheer Motor Mouth bluster and Blatant Lies. Eventually it loses its effectiveness when Colt and Jody realize what is going on and Gail lets slip her contempt for Jody by condescendingly noting how 'moldable' she has been.

tropes.name: Girlboss Feminist
tropes.html: Gail, a Hollywood executive, is known for Breaking the Glass Ceiling and producing Hollywood blockbusters. However, she is still a typical Hollywood vulture who manipulates a handful of bankable acts to make easy money and manipulates movies for stupid audiences while cutting costs to up profits. She orchestrates a conspiracy to cover up a golden goose's killing of a stuntman to boost studio profits. She uses gaslighting to manipulate Colt into becoming the other kind of Fall Guy for Ryder, Jody into believing Colt is the killer, and the public through special effects and evidence-tampering to sell the pin. During her escape attempt, she shrieks "toxic masculinity", even though it has nothing to do with toxic masculinity and has everything to do with her being an accessory to manslaughter.invoked

tropes.name: Got Me Doing It
tropes.html: Jody ends up using a finger gun gesture herself which she previously felt embarrassed by when Colt repeatedly made the same gesture at her. Now embarrassed by her own, she tells Colt "You Didn't See That".

tropes.name: Grievous Bottley Harm
tropes.html: During the night club fight, Colt hits one goon in the chest with the bottom of a champagne bottle, which causes the cork to shoot out, which he then aims at the face of another goon.

tropes.name: Groin Attack
tropes.html: Tom’s dog Jean Claude aids Colt in a few fight scenes by biting the enemies in their groins.

tropes.name: Have I Mentioned I Am Sexually Active Today?
tropes.html: During Jody "explaining" the romantic subplot of her film totally not being based on her and Colt falling out, she claims she had so many 'mind-blowing flings' to prove she moved on. It's implied none of it is true because all of her subsequent interactions with Colt make it clear she never got over him.invoked

tropes.name: Heroes Love Dogs
tropes.html: Colt is reunited with Jean Claude, a miniature pinscher who ostensibly belongs to Tom. Jean Claude becomes a sidekick and only responds to French commands; Colt makes frequent use of the Groin Attack one.

tropes.name: Horrible Hollywood
tropes.html: The Big Bad Duumvirate are an egotistical, murderous movie star, and his corrupt and manipulative agent and producer. Downplayed as the hero himself is a stunt man, and his allies include the film's director and crew members. If anything, the film praises the cool of stunt work and the more humble behind the scenes workers vs. the true jerks of the higher-ups.

tropes.name: Hypocrite
tropes.html: Tom Ryder reveals he intentionally caused Colt's career-halting accident because he felt Colt became too obsessed with himself and needed to be taken down a notch, even though Ryder is the one who's constantly shown to be a self-absorbed narcissist. He's also offended when Gail says Colt doesn't matter and no one will miss him if Tom shoots him, claiming Colt is the best stuntman he ever had, after spending the entire movie trying to murder Colt and have him take the fall for Henry's death.

tropes.name: Ignored Expert
tropes.html: When he arrives on the shoot, Colt quickly notes that the sand isn't quite right for the stunt driving he's expected to do, and they should wait until after the tide comes in and out again. He's overruled, and the car ride is unnecessarily bumpy when he does the stunt, leading to the destruction of a camera.

tropes.name: Immediate Self-Contradiction
tropes.html: Tom explains Gail's "simple solution" for him accidentally killing his stuntman, which is full of Complexity Addiction, something Colt points out.

tropes.name: Improbable Parking Skills
tropes.html: Colt Seavers proves he's a Badass Driver at the beginning when he valets a guest's Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat by doing donuts when going down the lot, and even doing donuts upon parallel parking, much to the guest's horror!

tropes.name: Informed Ability
tropes.html: Tom Ryder's definitely a bankable star in-universe, and several characters who dislike him personally even admit they think he's a really good actor. What's shown of his performance in the film seems to be a bit too wacky and over-the-top to merit that response. His take on Richard III does have intensity and the Kubrick Stare helps, but it's a bit wooden. Justified in that Ryder's fame led to Hookers and Blow and prima donna that likely dented his acting chops.

tropes.name: In Name Only
tropes.html: It's billed as The Film of the Series of The Fall Guy with Lee Majors but has little in common besides a few names and stunt work as a theme. In the show Colt was a stuntman who did work on the side as a Private Detective / Bounty Hunter to make ends meet, and would borrow his stunt equipment to do a particular job. The movie is an action-romantic-comedy involving a stuntman trying to salvage the directorial debut of his ex by finding the lead actor, and while he does do some detective work in looking for the lead actor who has gone missing, the entire "case" was an elaborate set up to make Colt take the fall for the death of the actor Ryder accidentally killed during a party. And afterwards, there is no sign that Colt plans to do any more detective work, he's happy just continuing on as a stuntman with Jody.

tropes.name: Irony
tropes.html:
• Gail's status as a Girlboss Feminist is lampooned, but the film actually does have an unconventional feminist message. Colt's downward spiral happened in part because of his wounded male pride, and his loss of confidence after he could no longer ignore the pain inherent to his profession made him feel emasculated and cut ties with Jody, even though she loved him and wouldn't've respected him less. He spends most of the movie giving her confusing mixed messages because he can't bring himself to admit to any of it, something which Jody outright calls macho bullshit. Opening up to her about his feelings and learning to be more in tune with them is what saves their relationship, and rather than making him weak or wimpy, only helps him become a better, more confident stuntman.
  • In a meta example, the film itself relies heavily on post-production CGI, including full digital double takeovers and actual Digital Head Swaps, to accomplish the more outlandish stunts in the film.

tropes.name: It's All About Me
tropes.html: Tom's reaction to accidentally killing his stunt double is to cry about how "This is not what [he] needs right now." Later, while talking to Colt about why he went along with the plan to frame him, he also mentions he likes Jody's movie and wants it to succeed, but because he thinks it's his best performance yet.

tropes.name: It Was Here, I Swear!
tropes.html: Colt finds a dead guy in a bathtub. He tries reporting it to the police sometime later, but by then, the body is gone. It doesn't help that he was still high on drugs, and in fact spends a good part of the film believing the body was a hallucination until the news reports on it.

tropes.name: Karma Houdini
tropes.html: Ryder's girlfriend Iggy Starr was a part of the plot to frame Colt for manslaughter; and yet the final scene in the movie reveals that apparently she was not replaced as the female lead in Metalstorm, implying she got away scot-free.

tropes.name: Leaning on the Fourth Wall
tropes.html:
• At one point, Jody calls Colt to get his input on the movie. At the start of the call, she tells him that she's considering doing a split screen effect and asks him what he thinks of that. Naturally, the call transitions to a splitscreen effect.
  • After the car-rolling stunt, Gail says it's eight and a half rolls, a new world record – a record set by the real movie.

tropes.name: Leitmotif
tropes.html: Colt doing a number of the crazier stunts of the plot have KISS' "I Was Made for Loving You" as background music - and a Softer and Slower Cover by Dominic Lewis and YUNGBLUD for when Colt fakes his death.

tropes.name: A Lighter Shade of Black
tropes.html:
Of the two main villains, Tom Ryder is a noticeably lesser evil, even if he's still an awful, selfish wreck of a human being. While his producer is a manipulator who doesn't care about anyone or anything except themself, and may be actively sabotaging the film rather than get into trouble for going overbudget, her counterpart does seem to genuinely love and care about movies and his craft, claiming part of the reason he went along with the whole scheme was because he thinks the movie they're making is going to be good and he wants to set up the director for success (although part of it is that he thinks his performance in it is his best yet). He also has the good grace to be offended on Colt's behalf, calling him the best stuntman he's ever known when his opposite number insults Colt as a nobody. This comes on the heels of spending the entire film trying to kill Colt and pin a homicide on him, mind. It also helps that Tom is an all too frequently drug-addled idiot who may not fully understand or appreciate the full impact of some of his actions.
  • Debatable, given Ryder was clearly lying to Colt about his good opinion of him, coldly ordered the murder of two people simply because they were “witnesses,” had Colt tortured, admitted to having deliberately caused Colt’s accident, showed outright sociopathic disinterest in his own murder of Henry, threatened the life of several others including Dan and Jody in order to make Colt talk, and flippantly arranged for Colt’s murder once he had the information he wanted. Very little of which can be passed off as simply being too drug-addled to know better. Gail may be manipulative and cold-blooded, but she’s no murderer, much less to the extent of Ryder.

tropes.name: A Lizard Named "Liz"
tropes.html: The main female character in Metalstorm is a female alien named Aliana.

tropes.name: Macho Masochism
tropes.html: Stuntmen ritually stick out their hands and give a thumbs-up after performing a successful stunt, even though, safety precautions or no, their insanely dangerous job still hurts them a lot even when it's done properly. Colt admits his downward spiral after the botched/sabotaged stunt that broke his back and put him out of commission was partially rooted in feeling ashamed that he couldn't give the thumbs-up after being so horribly wounded.

tropes.name: Made of Iron
tropes.html: Fitting for a stuntman, Colt goes through all sorts of punishment during the movie and never slows down. Hell, he fully recovered from a broken back in the span of 18 months, with only a little metal device he wears on his lumbar to show for it.

tropes.name: Mass "Oh, Crap!"
tropes.html: After Ryder kicks Henry back and wins the sparring match the two were having, he and the entire party break out in cheering and applause as Ryder boasts to the camera. However, things die down once everyone realises that Henry is lifeless, having broken his neck on a side table. Several people can be heard screaming as Ryder hastily shuts off the video.

tropes.name: Meaningful Background Event
tropes.html: While Colt and Alma are talking on a sidewalk, a garbage disposal truck can be seen pulling up behind them and the two "garbage men" get slowly closer and closer to them as they converse. Then they suddenly whip out their tasers and strike both Colt and Alma, revealing themselves to be goons.

tropes.name: "Metaphor" Is My Middle Name
tropes.html:
This exchange between Colt and Jody in a car:
Jody: We need to keep it super profesh.
Colt: Profesh is my middle name.
Jody: You said your middle name is Danger.
Colt: That's a stage name.

tropes.name: Muse Abuse
tropes.html: The relationship between "Space Cowboy" and Aliana in Metalstorm is transparently based in the bad way in which Colt and Jody's relationship fell apart after his accident, with a Sci-Fi paint job applied, and she makes no attempt to hide it when describing the plot to him, in front of the entire film crew.

tropes.name: Mushroom Samba
tropes.html: Colt is given a spiked drink and starts hallucinating, as the drug dealer's henchmen try to apprehend him, and he has to fight them while seeing all kinds of visual sparks and random unicorns.

tropes.name: Must Have Caffeine
tropes.html: Colt dealing with a bad case of jetlag desperately wants a cup of coffee but keeps being denied one either due to his requests being ignored or interrupted in some way when trying to get one himself.

tropes.name: My Greatest Failure
tropes.html: Colt blames himself for the stunt-gone-wrong that ended his career and his relationship with Jody, and it turns out the reason he never contacted Jody was that he considered the accident proof that he was a failure who didn't deserve Jody. We learn later in the film that Colt's "accident" was engineered by Tom.

tropes.name: Named After Somebody Famous
tropes.html: Jean Claude the stunt dog is named after Jean-Claude Van Damme (the human).

tropes.name: Never My Fault
tropes.html: Tom Ryder never takes any responsibility for his many, many screw ups. Even when he causes the deaths of other people (both accidentally and deliberately) he will inevitably blame it on the actions of other people including the victim.

tropes.name: Noodle Incident
tropes.html: While Jody goes on a long-winded tangent about Metalstorm's plot, which is a very thinly-veiled version of her own relationship with Colt and her attempt to process it, a crew member takes the microphone from Colt and mentions that he went through something similar when he fell in love with his wife's sister. Colt immediately takes the microphone back.

tropes.name: No Stunt Double
tropes.html:
• invoked Tom Ryder is every arrogant Hollywood actor wrapped into one package, insisting he does his own stunts despite the fact Colt was his dedicated double for years. It's said by other characters that Tom isn't even all that good in general action scenes, and he is very skittish the instant someone suggests anything but a close-up. It is revealed he sabotaged Colt's wire stunt that broke his back, his ego made him think Colt was trying to upstage him and that same ego led to the death of his current stunt double. Notably, though, the film Hilarious Outtakes appropriately shows all of Ryan Gosling's stunt doubles.
  • Played straight with Iggy Starr, Ryder's girlfriend and co-star of Metalstorm, who can easily fight off Colt for real with just a prop katana, and is later seen doing the fight choreography herself with Colt during the big set piece in front of the Sydney Opera House.
  • Production-wise, the Harbor Bridge garbage truck scene does include shots where Gosling surfed behind the moving truck, although the more complex jumps and fight scenes were done by a double.

tropes.name: Not-So-Harmless Villain
tropes.html: Big Bad Gail is a smarmy person with Complexity Addiction and a fondness for having subordinates do all the hard work, but she does get in a few punches in the climax, steals back the evidence against Ryder, and nearly shoots Colt with an enormous gun she was apparently carrying on her person all along.

tropes.name: The Oner
tropes.html: The film's prologue is all shot in a single take, right up until Colt's career-ending injury. Later in the film, the concept of the Oner is referenced by Jody when she's pitching ideas for Metalstorm.

tropes.name: The Other Marty
tropes.html: In-Universe. After Tom's crimes are exposed (and he accidentally blows himself up), the movie is reshot with Jason Momoa in the role.

tropes.name: Overly Long Gag
tropes.html:
• Colt's attempts to get into Ryder's hotel room. It takes him quite a while due to the key card for the room not working. He tries it several times, goes down to the front desk to get it fixed, tries the new card only for it not to work again, so he decides to simply break in and finds someone dead in the bathtub.
  • After going through a glass pane Colt is having a conversation with the lead actress and is trying to empty out all the glass shards in his jacket.

tropes.name: Pet the Dog
tropes.html: Downplayed with Horrible Hollywood movie star Ryder's four actual pet dogs (he also has a cockatoo, but he's planning to sell it); he does give his assistant instructions to take care of them during his disappearance, but also only keeps at least one of them, Jean-Claude, around to do violent party tricks. He also often compliments Colt as the best stuntman he ever had even he tries to kill him, actually hesitating to shoot him at point-blank range at the climax while Gail tells him to and giving this as the reason.

tropes.name: Pink Elephants
tropes.html: Colt gets a spiked drink from Tom's drug dealer. He asks how long it should last and is told it's on its way out when he stops seeing unicorns. About 20 minutes of the movie has a unicorn following him around.

tropes.name: The Prima Donna
tropes.html: Tom Ryder. Even his longtime producer, Gail, acknowledges that he's an asshole to work with. His diva antics go so far as trying to kill two of his stunt doubles – and succeeding once.

tropes.name: Police Are Useless
tropes.html: The Sydney police seem to be rather absent even for an action movie, whether it's a very visible long car chase-slash-fistfight downtown and across the city bridge, or a long and loud shootout in the harbour. They only appear to give Colt a parking ticket and follow him to what he swears was a dead body in a tub full of ice. Two police show up after Tom and Gail's helicopter has crashed to arrest them, played by the original leads from the original show, but they're quickly identified as part of the film staff posing as cops.

tropes.name: Precision F-Strike
tropes.html: When Ryder calls Gail in a panic after killing Henry, he lets out a hysterical “Fuckin’ Henry!”

tropes.name: Recording Your Crime
tropes.html: Played with. Ryder happens to record Henry's murder/manslaughter on his phone. However, he uses it to try and frame Colt for the murder via a deepfake.

tropes.name: Recruit the Muggles
tropes.html: In the climax, most of the film crew help trick Ryder into confessing and a small army of stunt workers provide Dan backup during his fight with the mooks and mop the floor with them.

tropes.name: Remake Cameo
tropes.html: Original series stars Lee Majors and Heather Thomas appear as police officers in the stinger, arriving to arrest Gail and Tom.

tropes.name: Rental Car Abuse
tropes.html: Inverted. Colt gives the Jerkass who mocked him for his accident and his current work as a valet (which Colt is about to quit in about five seconds) some payback by driving his Challenger like a bat out of hell, while the horriifed man yells out "be careful with it, man, it's a rental!"

tropes.name: Rhymes on a Dime
tropes.html: When trying to explain what happened at the night club over the phone to Gail, he says "it was Doone's Goons who dirtied my Shirley"

tropes.name: Romance on the Set
tropes.html:
Two instances In-Universe:
  • Colt and Jody were hot and heavy during productions they were both working on.
  • Tom Ryder is dating Iggy Starr, the female lead of Metalstorm, although it is never established if their relationship developed during filming or predated it.

tropes.name: Scary Teeth
tropes.html: Ryder's drug dealer has a fancy grill that he shows as he tries to intimidate Colt. Emphasis on "tries" to, as he's a dumbass who relies on his goons and squeals on the disappearance behind Ryder as soon as Colt gets his hands on him.

tropes.name: Secret Word
tropes.html: Colt is told to ask for a "fruit platter" at the Hotel reception to get the key to Tom Ryder's room, but the first receptionist isn't in on the secret and asks is he's trying to order room service.

tropes.name: Self-Disposing Villain
tropes.html: Ryder attempts to escape police custody by running onto the open set and trying to call for help. The use of his cell phone detonates the pyrotechnics on set, causing Ryder to blow himself up.

tropes.name: Shipper on Deck
tropes.html: Several of Colt's friends seem to be supportive of him and Jody getting back together, with Dan noticing that Jody is still into him, while Alma also notes that they seem to be rekindling their relationship and hopes that they do, though it is beneficial to her as she might get a producer credit for Metalstorm out of it.

tropes.name: Shout-Out
tropes.html:
• The movie uses a lot of behind-the-scenes footage of stunt people from real movies, including director David Leitch's previous films Atomic Blonde and Nobody.
  • A Running Gag has Dan quoting other movies for inspirational moments or just one-liners including Rocky Balboa and The Fast and the Furious (2001).
  • The score for Metalstorm contains a One-Woman Wail very similar to that from the score for Dune. The film itself is a mashup of Dune and Mad Max: Fury Road, which was also stunt heavy.
  • When Colt's experience as a performer for the Miami Vice stunt show comes in handy as he escapes from the mercenaries in the harbor, the camera not only lingers on the jacket's logo for a good long time, but the Miami Vice main theme begins to play.
  • The ending is a big one to Tropic Thunder: showing off the Show Within a Show to an excited crowd and all the protagonists happily in the audience, and with the star being the winner of the "MTV Film Award for Best Kiss", which Tropic Thunder's Tobey Maguire also had a credit for in Satan's Alley.
  • When Colt pushes Dan to safety as the villain shoots at them through the stairs we hear the sound effect from 'The Six Million Dollar Man', a series starring original The Fall Guy actor Lee Majors.

tropes.name: Shut Up, Hannibal!
tropes.html: Jody is finally able to put an end to Gail's gaslighting when she strikes her in the face when she's attempting to manipulate her again during the climax.

tropes.name: Slipping a Mickey
tropes.html: While trying to track down Tom Ryder, Colt meets Tom's drug dealer Doone at a fancy night club, and as Doone insists Colt have a drink, he asks for a Shirley Temple. After having a sip, Colt soon starts experiencing hallucinations as Doone was tasked with drugging and subduing Colt so he could be framed for the death of Henry, Tom's new stunt double.

tropes.name: Small Name, Big Ego
tropes.html: Tom is an egotistical action star who boasts about doing all of his stunts, but is shown to be a major coward who can barely get through a simple driving stunt on his own without complaining.

tropes.name: Smug Snake
tropes.html: This is Gail all over. She spends almost the whole film with either a smile or a little grin showing only her upper teeth, an "I am the boss and I am better than you" smile that she tries (with various degrees of success) to present as "friendly". At the climax, the smile remains but switches to "violently manic".

tropes.name: Soundtrack Dissonance
tropes.html: Two major fight scenes are backed by “All I Do Is Win” and “Against All Odds” respectively.

tropes.name: Space Western
tropes.html: Metalstorm, the Film Within a Film, is mostly desert and focuses on a protagonist literally named "the Space Cowboy" who speaks in an exaggerated Southern twang and does fancy revolver tricks. It's based on a 1983 film in the same genre, even using the film's tag line.

tropes.name: Speaks in Shout-Outs
tropes.html: Every other line out of Dan's mouth is a referencing a movie or actor by name.

tropes.name: The Stinger
tropes.html: Treated as a Previously on… segment, there is a midcredits sequence of the previous actors of the original series posing as cops arriving to arrest Gail and Tom, with Tom fleeing into an area filled with pyrotechnics as getting blown to bits, prompting Alma to make a call requesting Jason Momoa’s agent.

tropes.name: Star-Crossed Lovers
tropes.html: Jody's original plan for the Space Cowboy and Aliana's relationship was to have their love fail to overcome the differences between them.

tropes.name: Strange Minds Think Alike
tropes.html: During the "splitscreen" phone call, you can see that Colt and Jody are going through the exact same physical motions while talking to each other, highlighting their compatibility despite their current relationship struggles.

tropes.name: Surprisingly Realistic Outcome
tropes.html: Colt and Dan abandon their plan to unlock a cellphone by having Venti engage in Hollywood Hacking when she tells them that it would take three or four days and that Ryder's likely wrote the passcode down on a Post-It as Ryder already writes almost everything else down to not forget, which turns out to be the better option that actually works.

tropes.name: Symbolic Glass House
tropes.html: Ryder lives in an all-glass apartment that overlooks the city, where Colt gets in a fight with Iggy Starr after sneaking in.

tropes.name: Take That!
tropes.html:
• Tom Ryder is a mockery of numerous egotistical Hollywood stars:
    • Aaron Taylor-Johnson's performance clearly imitates the persona of Matthew McConaughey, and he further plays it up as the Space Cowboy with McConaughey's exaggerated twang, and suggests an improvised line for an action scene that is a direct reference to McConaughey's Lincoln ad campaign.
    • "Tom Ryder"'s name is just one degree removed from Tom Cruise (who exists in-universe too, presumably as Plausible Deniability). He shares Cruise's reliance on being seen as doing his own stunts, speaks the same way as Cruise does when not acting, and his behavior has much in common with rumors (and verified recordings) of Cruise being passive aggressive and sometimes outright hostile towards crew members. Colt's little chats to himself also show Ryder is a macho, homophobic bully, which also matches rumors from co-stars about on-set behavior.
    • The crappy sci-fi movie he's in mimics the overblown Scientology vehicle of Battlefield Earth, starring fellow action starlet-cum-serious actor and Scientologist John Travolta.
    • His angry public antics and constant breakdowns references Mel Gibson's own (complete with "Action Part One", one of Ryder's ego vehicles, also being a reference to Lethal Weapon and its many sequels).
    • Him really being behind the 'accident' that severely injured Colt out of pettiness digs at various sets that cut corners on stunts and risk everyone's lives, but it's especially pointed after the then-recent high-profile killing of a cinematographer due to the armorer's cavalier attitude towards gun safety, as well as the killing of a stuntwoman on the set of Deadpool 2, which is likely a bit of ultra-dark self-criticism for Leitch (who directed Deadpool 2).
    • His constant chewing out of set personnel also references Christian Bale's infamous rant on the set of Terminator Salvation.
