tropes.html: The doctors manage to botch Kenny's surgery so badly (at one point, they seem to be going in there with hedge trimmers) that they replace his heart with a baked potato. Somehow, he survived long enough for them to tell him he had three seconds to live.

tropes.name: Comically Missing the Point
tropes.html:
• When the President declares war on Canada, everyone in the school gym is shocked...except for Mr. Garrison:
    Garrison: All the Baldwins are dead?!
  • When the Canadian ambassadors are talking the unjustness of Terrance and Phillip's arrest and declaring war upon the United States, the United Nation's ambassadors can't get over the way they pronounce "about".
  • The doctor who implants Cartman's V-Chip to curb his foul mouth proclaims it as a success after Cartman doesn't want to swear—not because he's learned his lesson, but because every time he swears, it electrocutes him, which he takes exception to (and often leads to more swearing).
  • At school, after Cartman tells Kyle, "don't call me fat, you fucking Jew!", Mr. Garrison asks about him using the F-word. Cartman apparently thinks "Jew" is the F-word.

tropes.name: Compressed Vice
tropes.html: The boys are portrayed as innocents who don't take up swearing until seeing the Terrance & Phillip movie. They cursed just as much before and after then.

tropes.name: Condescending Compassion
tropes.html:
A potential example with Cartman and Kyle.
Cartman: All those times I said you were a big dumb Jew, I didn't mean it... you're not a Jew.
Kyle: [irritably] Yes I am! I am a Jew, Cartman!
Cartman: No, no, Kyle, don't be so hard on yourself.
  • The reason this is a questionable example is that the film takes place within the early seasons of South Park where Cartman was more of an Expy of Archie Bunker (whose racism was due to being oblivious and from an older time) rather than The Sociopath Manipulative Bastard he is more well known for being nowadays. In this case, Cartman may legitimately think and believe that calling someone Jewish is an insult without actually understanding it what it means.

tropes.name: Conditioned to Be Weak
tropes.html:
Satan and Saddam Hussein are a dysfunctional couple where Saddam is the abusive boyfriend who alternates between abusing/degrading Satan and emotionally manipulating him. Despite Satan being much more physically powerful, he's been so browbeaten and worn down that he lets Saddam walk all over him... until at the end of the movie he finally snaps and kills Saddam. Afterwards, Satan muses about this trope.
Satan: He spent so much time convincing me I was weak and stupid that I? believed it myself.

tropes.name: Continuity Nod
tropes.html:
• The subplot of "Death" also involved parents protesting Terrance & Phillip. This was a major inspiration for the movie's plotline, and is basically that subplot expanded from 22 minutes to 81 minutes and with musical numbers.
  • If you look closely at the newspaper Gerald is reading in the opening number, you can see it says "Bookmobile Driver Released", which is a reference to "Chickenlover", where the driver was found to be the titular culprit.
  • In the theater where the kids watch Asses of Fire for the second time after "It's Easy, M'kay", you can see Damien sitting next to them.
  • The four-assed ostrich from "An Elephant Makes Love to a Pig" can be seen in the crowd.
  • The midget wearing a bikini reporter from "Pinkeye" returns.
  • A poster on a movie theater entrance reads Mecha-Streisand Takes New York, a nod to "Mecha-Streisand".
  • The title card of "Terrance and Phillip in Not Without My Anus" can be seen on a TV in a store Stan walks into.
  • The map of the Canadian internment camp that Gregory uses when sharing his plans to the others is the same one used in "Cartman's Mom is Still a Dirty Slut".
  • Satan and Saddam Hussein are officially confirmed to be a couple, this was first foreshadowed in the ending of "The Mexican Staring Frog of Southern Sri Lanka".
  • Kelly, Kenny's girlfriend from "Rainforest Shmainforest", also makes a cameo in the same scene, despite living on the other side of the country.
  • Scuzzlebutt from "Volcano" can be seen in the crowd, singing the reprise of "Mountain Town".
  • Cartman sang "Kyle's Mom is a Bitch" before in "Mr. Hankey, the Christmas Poo", and here, it's modulated from the original D minor to C major and includes a tutorial on how to sing the song in different languages.

tropes.name: Cooldown Hug Interruption
tropes.html: Sheila shooting Terrance and Phillip after Kyle stops the warring sides.

tropes.name: Creator Cameo
tropes.html: Composer Marc Shaiman (himself an out and proud gay man) makes a brief background appearance as the pianist in "I'm Super".

tropes.name: Credits Gag
tropes.html: Satan and Saddam are listed as playing themselves. Also, the songs are said to have been performed by the characters themselves.

tropes.name: Creepy Changing Painting
tropes.html: Played for Laughs during "Blame Canada", when Liane holds up a picture of Cartman that changes to show him grinning evilly and Flipping the Bird.

tropes.name: Cultural Translation
tropes.html:
• In the Japanese dub, the Clitoris' voice sounds like that of a woman orgasming, like you would hear in an undubbed hentai.
  • The German version changes the German porn video to British porn.

tropes.name: Culture Police
tropes.html: Sheila ends up starting a war with Canada (and eventually The End of the World as We Know It) over the Terrance and Phillip film Asses of Fire.

tropes.name: Dark Reprise
tropes.html: The dying words of Ze Mole are one of "La Resistance".

tropes.name: Deathly Unmasking
tropes.html: Right before he performs a Heroic Sacrifice to save his friends that gets him sent back to the afterlife, Kenny drops his hoodie to tell them goodbye before fading away, giving the audience a clear view of his head for the first time. Kenny's deaths in the series are never permanent, but the unmasking made this particular death feel more significant for The Movie.

tropes.name: Demoted to Dragon
tropes.html: Satan may be the chief entity of evil in the universe, but Saddam is clearly the one who wears the pants in their relationship.

tropes.name: Demoted to Extra
tropes.html: Despite being a major recurring character at the time of this movie's release, Pip is simply a background character here and does not get any lines.

tropes.name: Descent into Darkness Song
tropes.html: The "Hell Isn't Good" song that plays when poor Kenny, well, goes to Hell.

tropes.name: Description Cut
tropes.html: After "It's Easy, M'kay", Mr. Mackey tells the children they can take the rest of the day off for personal reflection or to do something constructive. Cut to the movie theater where the entire class (except for Wendy and Gregory) is watching Asses of Fire.

tropes.name: Destination Defenestration
tropes.html: Outside-to-inside example. Ike is kicked through a window twice, courtesy of Kyle.

tropes.name: Didn't Think This Through
tropes.html: The boys gather all the other kids who've been grounded to form a resistance group devoted to stopping the war and rescuing Terrence and Phillip. However, when the meeting begins, it's clear they don't have a real plan in mind aside from pointlessly pranking the police.

tropes.name: Died in Your Arms Tonight
tropes.html: How Ze Mole dies.

tropes.name: Disney Villain Death
tropes.html: Saddam dies when Satan throws him down into hell, getting impaled by the rocks below.

tropes.name: Disproportionate Retribution
tropes.html:
• The kids watch Terrance and Philip's movie and start cussing worse than they usually do (except for Kenny, who's typically more risqué in his dialogue than his friends), which eventually leads to an all-out war with Canada because the parents refuse to accept responsibility and Kenny died because of a movie he shouldn't have watched in the first place.
  • Sheila's retribution against Canada wasn't just disproportionate; it was misplaced. She was seeking to punish the entire nation of Canada based on the actions of only two of its citizens.

tropes.name: The Dog Bites Back
tropes.html:
• Canada keeps retaliating defensively against American aggression. The Mothers Against Canada arrest Terrance and Philip in order to execute them. Only after diplomatic negotiations fail do the Canadians do the same to a group of American celebrities. Then the U.S. declares a full-out war on Canada, bombs Toronto, and forces all Canadian-Americans into happy camps. The Canadians respond by attacking South Park to rescue Terrance and Philip.
  • The black soldiers, led by Chef, defy the general's orders to act as a human shield in revenge for his blatant racism, leaving the white soldiers behind them to explode.
    Soldier: Great plan, Chef!
    Chef: Operation Human Shield my ass!
  • Satan finally has enough of Saddam's emotional abuse and impales him on a stalagmite. Not that it makes any difference—after all, where else was he going to go? Detroit?

tropes.name: Double Standard
tropes.html: Sheila says that it's okay for a film to have all the carnage and mayhem it wants, as long as there are "no naughty words". Stan and Kyle do a double take in response.

tropes.name: Double-Meaning Title
tropes.html: The title is not only a description of how the film is a longer, uncensored version of the series but also a crude dick joke.

tropes.name: Dramatic Irony
tropes.html: Minor example when the boys are first hauled before Mr. Mackey. He demands to know where they heard such profanity and they try to scapegoat Garrison. For all of Garrison's faults, Mackey has a hard time believing he would ever say "Eat penguin shit, you ass spelunker" to his own students. The irony, of course, is that this is exactly the kind of thing Garrison would say (and had) at this point in the show's run.

tropes.name: Dramatic Unmask
tropes.html: At the end, Kenny's face is shown for the first time, when he sacrifices himself to save the rest of the Earth at the cost of going back to the afterlife.

tropes.name: Driven to Suicide
tropes.html: Conan O'Brien, following his My God, What Have I Done? moment, jumps out of the studio window and to his death onto a parked car.

tropes.name: Dude, Not Funny!
tropes.html:
• Terrance and Phillip appear on Late Night with Conan O'Brien and do their fart joke routine but after guest Brooke Shields admits that she once farted on the set of Blue Lagoon, (Beat), Terrance slaps her in response.
  • Mr. Garrison thinks that the mothers of the kids are overreacting about the swearing incidents when he finds he has to teach their syllabus, and makes an offhand remark about them being on their periods. Wendy and Gregory call him out on it (deeming it a sexist statement), but he makes an even cruder comment in response.

tropes.name: Dude, Where's My Respect?
tropes.html: Gregory pretty much assumed leadership of La Resistance and came up with the entire plan to save Terrence and Phillip. But when everything is said and done, he gets no credit for anything and Wendy ditches him to get back with Stan, saying "Fuck Gregory. Fuck him right in the ear!" His look of indignation says it all.

tropes.name: Early Adaptation Weirdness
tropes.html: There are many notable differences from the show due to being created around the same time as its third season. If someone who was introduced to the later episodes of the show watched this film, they would notice the much cruder animation, art style and jokes that were standard during those times, and how much smaller the town of South Park used to be. Cartman himself is the bratty jerk he was known for early on instead of the cunning and manipulative sociopath of the later seasons. Also, certain characters who would rise to prominence much later on, such as Craig and Tolkien, are just background characters; in particular, it's odd to see such a big event where Butters is nothing more than a Spear Carrier or for that matter, where Kenny actually does get focus. Even Randy, who has since gone on become the most prominent adult character of the show, only had one single speaking line in the whole movie (questioning the V-chip).

tropes.name: Earn Your Happy Ending
tropes.html: For all four leads, but the boys don't have it so good before Kenny's wish. Cartman suffers for most of the film because of the V-Chip, but it backfires in spectacular fashion and he's able to use swearing as a superpower. Kyle finally finds the courage to stand up to his mother, Stan's bravery wins Wendy's favor, and Kenny's willingness to go back to Hell for everyone's sake earns him a spot Heaven.

tropes.name: Easy Road to Hell
tropes.html: In the South Park universe, the only people who go to Heaven are Mormons. Everyone else, including poor Kenny, goes straight to Hell.

tropes.name: 11th-Hour Superpower
tropes.html: Cartman's V-chip gets its wiring fried and accidentally reversed, allowing him to use it as a cuss-powered Kamehamehadoken.

tropes.name: Entertainment Above Their Age
tropes.html: Stan, Kenny, Cartman, Kyle, and Ike pay a homeless man to pretend to be their guardian so they can watch Terrance & Phillip: Asses of Fire, an in-universe R-rated movie. By the end of the it, they're the only people still in the theater, and they become much more foul-mouthed after viewing it, leading Sheila and the parents to start a war against Canada for making the movie.

tropes.name: Epic Fail
tropes.html:
Doctor: (to Kenny) Son, we have some bad news. We accidentally replaced your heart with a baked potato. You have about 3 seconds to live.
Kenny: What?! (Kenny's heart then blows up)
  • Before Gregory takes command, Stan's plan to save Terrance and Phillip involves prank-calling the South Park police and sending them pizza that they didn't order.

tropes.name: Establishing Character Moment
tropes.html:
• During the opening number, Sheila's verse is noticeably darker in tone, and all about how evil the world is. She also blames Ike (her adopted, Canadian child) for something Kyle was clearly responsible for. The same scene also establishes that Kyle is useless at standing up to her.
  • Butters has his status as a Cloudcuckoolander who takes orders from Cartman established when he gives in to Cartman's demands for somebody to touch him, and says "Oooh" while doing so.

tropes.name: Et Tu, Brute?
tropes.html: When all the kids joined in when Cartman began singing "Kyle's Mom Is a Bitch", even Stan couldn't help but sing along.

tropes.name: Evil Overlooker
tropes.html: Satan is seen looming above the characters in the poster above.

tropes.name: Evil Parents Want Good Kids
tropes.html: Sheila doesn't take Kyle's Armor-Piercing Question to her very well.

tropes.name: Even Evil Has Standards
tropes.html: The Mothers Against Canada (except Sheila) support war with Canada, but not if it means their children are in the middle of it. Sheila learned her lesson the hard way.

tropes.name: Evil Is Petty
tropes.html: Sheila and the Mothers Against Canada declared war on Canada and wanting to kill Terrence and Phillip all because the boys got in trouble in school after watching an R-rated movie.

tropes.name: Evil Matriarch
tropes.html: Sheila (Kyle's mother) is the main antagonist of the film, blaming the film for Kyle cursing more.

tropes.name: Exact Words
tropes.html: Saddam saying he can change, and not he will change.

tropes.name: Failed a Spot Check
tropes.html: In the opening number Mountain Town, Stan sings about how the snow is pure and white, missing that the snow he picked up has a yellow stain on it from a deer.

tropes.name: Family-Values Villain
tropes.html: Mothers Against Canada. Especially Sheila.

tropes.name: Fan Disservice
tropes.html:
• At the end of "I'm Super", Big Gay Al bares his naked genitals to the audience. Of course, most of the audience were non-homosexual males.
  • During the apex of "Mountain Town", Sheila sings so powerfully that her fat, foldy granny knickers are exposed.

tropes.name: Fanservice
tropes.html: Kenny sees Heaven as being full of naked women, since he's a pervert.

tropes.name: Farts on Fire
tropes.html: Turns out that this really works, much to Kenny's regret. He burns himself to death by lighting his fart like what Terrence did in the movie, though in Kenny's case it kills him and effectively puts the plot into motion.

tropes.name: Final Solution
tropes.html: Sheila's Evil Plan is to wipe out all Canadians, not just Terrance and Phillip.

tropes.name: First Kiss
tropes.html: At the end of the film, Wendy finally gives Stan a kiss. Unlike every instance in the show when she tries to go for a slow buildup that's ruined by Stan's delicate tummy, here she surprises Stan with a quick one before he can barf on her.

tropes.name: Flanderization
tropes.html:
Several characters are exaggerated from their show versions. Of course, it's all part of the plot.
  • Sheila's Jerkass and Moral Guardian qualities are taken even further here.
  • Terrance and Phillip swear much more harshly here than in the show — might be justified as Asses of Fire and their Late Night appearance were intended in-universe for adults, and of course, their being arrested unfairly and nearly executed.
  • The boys had a reputation for having filthy mouths before, but it's also taken to higher levels in the movie.

tropes.name: Fooled by the Sound
tropes.html: The Mole's distress call is to imitate a dying giraffe. When the kids make the sound, some nearby soldiers comment "Hey, did you hear that? Sounds like a giraffe is dying over there."

tropes.name: Foreshadowing
tropes.html:
Several during the "Mountain Town" opening number:
  • Stan picking up yellow snow that a deer left behind serves as a hint of the crass humor of the series, something the opening downplays to build up the shock value of Terrance and Phillip.
  • Kyle hops over the same hobo that would later pay the boys' admission to see the Terrance and Phillip movie for them.
  • A news report says that Saddam Hussein (who appears in Hell as Satan's lover) was killed six weeks ago by wild boars.
  • There's also a line by Kenny's mom that predicts Kenny will end up in Hell (which happens after he dies).
  • Sheila yells at Ike for breaking a window that was really Kyle's doing. His Canadian blood aside, Kyle later asks his mother why she always blames everyone else when he gets into trouble.
  • Later on, Stan sings about how the sight of Wendy gives him butterflies in his stomach. As soon as Wendy greets him, Stan barfs.

tropes.name: Freeze-Frame Bonus
tropes.html:
• A chart on the hospital wall where Kenny dies lists several doctors assigned to different things; the doctor assigned to "Kill Bond" is No.
    • Also on the agenda is "Disembowel Kenny".
  • When Kyle's mom tells Mr. Garrison to pull the switch on the electric chairs while Kyle yells "Mom, no!", if you look carefully, you can see that Kyle has peed himself.
  • When the troops are marching through South Park on their way to the USO Show, you can see Jesus in the marching line.
  • A movie poster at the South Park Bijou Cinema features Mecha-Streisand fighting Leonard Maltin in a film titled, Mecha-Streisand Takes New York.
  • Before they break into the USO camp, Ze Mole looks at his watch to check how much time they have before the rendezvous with La Resistance. If you look closely, the label on his watch reads "Third Act: The Ticking Clock".
  • The Establishing Shot of the UN has a Jolly Roger flag and a gay pride flag flying outside.
  • In the first song, a log covered in snow has a suggestive yellow patch on it.
  • As Kenny first lands in Hell and is too terrified at the horror before him, a tiny fart is heard. At first, you think this is Kenny's nature, but you see a skeletal dragon breathing fire in the background. Watch carefully as the fart is heard and the dragon makes its pass off-screen. Just before it flies off and you hear the fart, you can see a very tiny flaming rock falling from the general direction of what we're supposed to assume is the thing's anatomy.
  • Right before the boys' mothers come into the hospital room, you can see the astronaut-themed episode of Terrance & Phillip playing on the TV.
  • During the Triumphant Reprise at the end, the recently impaled Saddam is briefly seen singing along.

tropes.name: Gag Penis
tropes.html: Saddam teases Satan with two of these, which are fake, but extremely realistic-looking.

tropes.name: The Gods Must Be Lazy
tropes.html: Satan and Saddam Hussein rise up from hell and take over earth. Only the fact that Saddam is such a Jerkass and Satan is a Jerk with a Heart of Gold saved Earth from being plunged into two million years of darkness, and yet God doesn’t even appear or do anything. It's especially jarring considering that Jesus and God are both recurring characters, and you can actually briefly see Jesus in the background of one of the shots in the movie (when the soldiers are marching in front of Kyle's house).

tropes.name: Go Through Me
tropes.html: Attempted, but... subverted. While it's no doubt cool that La Résistance forms a human shield to protect Terrance and Philip, the fact that they're kids and thus much shorter than the duo doesn't prevent them from getting shot at all.

tropes.name: Good Is Not Nice
tropes.html: Ze Mole is a heroic character (working with Gregory to free Terrance and Phillip), but has an abrasive personality.

tropes.name: Go, Ye Heroes, Go and Die
tropes.html: "La Resistance" is a very inspiring song for everyone who hears and sings it... except Stan, Kyle and Cartman, who are the three people that the song is supposed to inspire.

tropes.name: Gosh Dang It to Heck!
tropes.html:
• Sheila's dialogue is obviously devoid of swearing (since she along with the rest of the boys' mothers are trying ban foul-mouthed content and most of all exterminate Canada for producing it). In fact, she advocates Dr. Vosknocker's idea of placing V-chips inside children's heads to prevent them from swearing, after hearing Cartman's foul-mouthed song about her ("Kyle's Mom is a Bitch"). She also uses "heck" as a substitute for the F word:
Sheila: What the heck is a rimjob?
  • Later Inverted when she calls Terrence and Phillip "bastards" upon their execution.
  • What Mr. Mackey tries to teach the kids by singing "It's Easy, M'kay".
  • Cartman is reduced to this, since the V-Chip installed in his head shocks him whenever he tries to swear.
  • Inverted with Liane Cartman, whom, in a sense of Hypocritical Humor, swears in the musical number "Blame Canada" (with the lines "Now when I see him [Eric Cartman], he tells me to fuck myself" and "And that bitch Anne Murray too!"), despite being part of the Mothers Against Canada organization trying to prevent children from swearing.

tropes.name: Grounded Forever
tropes.html:
• Inverted. The kids are grounded by their moms for a few weeks for seeing the Terrance & Phillip movie again (and maybe for causing Kenny's death).
  • Also inverted by Ze Mole before he and the boys sneak into the USO show.
Ze Mole: You guys know that if we do this, we could get grounded for two, maybe three weeks.

tropes.name: Guilt by Association Gag
tropes.html: For some reason, Wendy and Gregory are in Mr. Mackey's support group with the other kids despite neither having seen Asses of Fire.

tropes.name: Hammerspace
tropes.html: Where Cartman got his megaphone from.

tropes.name: Hand Wave
tropes.html: We never see how the other kids snuck into Asses of Fire, nor how the entire class was able to sneak into the movie a second time. Presumably the ticket guy wouldn't have fallen for the "homeless guardian" trick a second time (unless the cinema has rotating staff).

tropes.name: Have I Mentioned I Am Heterosexual Today?
tropes.html: Mr. Garrison: Oh boy, I can't wait for our first shore leave so I can get me some fucking poontang.

tropes.name: Heel–Face Turn
tropes.html: Mrs. Broflovski, at the end. Demonstrated during the closing number, wherein she pats Terrance and Phillip on the shoulder, calling them, "super sweet".

tropes.name: Heel Realization
tropes.html: Most of the Mothers Against Canada have one when they realize that they have endangered their own boys with their actions. Sheila's doesn't come around until it's almost too late (in other words, it doesn't come until she executes Terrance and Phillip and unleashes Hell on Earth).

tropes.name: Hell on Earth
tropes.html: Happens near the end as a result of Terrance and Phillip's execution.

tropes.name: Hello, Sailor!
tropes.html: Satan's "I Want" Song song "Up There" includes imagining himself aboard the SS Manhandler cavorting with many muscular men wearing very tight Speedos.

tropes.name: Heroic Sacrifice
tropes.html: Kenny is willing to sacrifice a second chance at life in order to hit the Reset Button on the Canadian-American war. For his selfless wish, he is admitted into Heaven. This becomes absolute Fridge Horror when it is revealed during the Mysterion timeline that Kenny doesn't stay dead. That means the poor kid received the reward of going to Heaven...and was then reincarnated into his abusive, drug-addicted, white-trash family—with his memories of Heaven intact.

tropes.name: Homage
tropes.html: Gregory to Enjolras from Les Misérables: Long blond hair? Check. Charismatic leader of La Résistance? Check. Waves a red and black flag? Check.

tropes.name: Hope Spot
tropes.html:
• After Kenny's surgery, it briefly seems like everything is fine and he'll live through it, as the doctors calmly wake him up. They then inform him that they accidentally replaced his heart with a baked potato and he's gonna die in roughly three seconds.
  • It looked like Sheila finally came to her senses before gunning down Terrance and Phillip.

tropes.name: Hope Sprouts Eternal
tropes.html: After Satan and the rest of Hell goes back, the battlefield is covered in grass and flowers.

tropes.name: Human Shield
tropes.html:
• The General of the American forces reveals that he's planning to use all African-American soldiers as human shields to protect them from the Canadian forces. Chef obviously takes offense at that and commands his men to duck.
Chef: "Operation Human Shield", my ass!
  • Taken to ridiculous levels when it's shown the black soldiers were also strapped to the exterior of a tank. Whatever's strong enough to damage a tank isn't going to be dulled by human flesh.

tropes.name: Hypocrite
tropes.html:
• Kyle calls out his mom for trying to exterminate Canada, when her adopted son Ike is also Canadian.
  • She also calls Terrance and Phillip "bastards" as a Pre-Mortem One-Liner, despite spending the whole movie crusading against foul language.
  • Not to mention she's fine with horrific deplorable violence over obscenities.

tropes.name: Hypocritical Humor
tropes.html:
• Liane is a part of the Mothers Against Canada organization trying to prevent their children from swearing, but swears herself in the musical number "Blame Canada" with the lines "Now when I see him [Cartman], he tells me to fuck myself" and "And that bitch Anne Murray too!".
  • Kyle says, "God damn, your mom sucks, Cartman" after the boys find an Internet video of her doing German scat porn (there's also a chance Kyle may have been speaking literally). Considering what his own mother is in this film, it's definitely throwing stones in a glass house on Kyle's part. To be fair, it's not as though Kyle approves of his mother's actions either, and calls her out on her Moral Knight Templar Parent nonsense. He just gets tired of Cartman making musical numbers dedicated to his mom.
  • Terrance, co-star with Phillip on their titular show that, in-universe, is notorious for an obscene amount of fart jokes on their program, slaps Brooke Shields on The Conan O'Brien Show for happily mentioning that she once farted on the set of The Blue Lagoon.
  • After Mr. Garrison tells Cartman off for calling Kyle a "fucking Jew", Kyle responds with “No, he’s talking about fuck. You can’t say 'fuck' in school, you fucking fatass!”
Cartman: Why the fuck not?!

tropes.name: I Resemble That Remark!
tropes.html: Gregory and Wendy accuse Garrison of making a sexist remark when he accuses the kids' moms of being on their period as the motive behind their rage against Canada. Garrison responds by saying "I don't trust anything that bleeds for seven days and doesn't die".

tropes.name: I'm Cold... So Cold...
tropes.html: Ze Mole says this after his cover is blown during the USO show.

tropes.name: I'm Dying, Please Take My MacGuffin
tropes.html: Mr. Garrison is shot in battle against the Canadian forces and so he passes down Mr. Hat to the Boys. Later on, Satan picks it up as his new Companion Cube.

tropes.name: In-Theater Poster
tropes.html: The cover of the 4K Ultra HD release for the movie's 25th anniversary shows many of the characters in a movie theater, referencing how a major plot point in the film is the kids sneaking into the R-rated Film Within a Film Terrance and Philip: Asses of Fire.

tropes.name: Ignorant About Fire
tropes.html: Kenny farts on a match, resulting in his whole body catching on fire. Cartman tries to help him by whacking him with a stick, which does nothing but also set the stick on fire.

tropes.name: Ignored Epiphany
tropes.html:
• A variation of the trope in that someone tries to invoke self-reflection on others, only for the people in question to take it for granted:
Mr. Mackey: Now you're cured! You can take the rest of the afternoon off for personal reflection, m'kay? Find your own constructive way to better yourself, m'kay?
(cut to the kids watching Terrance and Philip at the theater yet again)
  • See Hope Spot above, even after her son reasoned with her, she ignores it, and kills Terrance and Phillip.

tropes.name: Immune to Bullets
tropes.html: When Saddam Hussein rises from Hell along with Satan, the American soldiers immediately shoot him. He laughs off their gunfire.

tropes.name: Impaled with Extreme Prejudice
tropes.html: When Satan throws Saddam Hussein back into Hell, he lands with a sharp rock going through his torso.

tropes.name: Incredibly Long Note
tropes.html: Pretty much almost every musical number in the movie ends with these. Wouldn't be a Broadway musical inspired movie without 'em!

tropes.name: Internal Homage
tropes.html: Kenny's heart being replaced by a baked potato is one to the duo's first project, Cannibal! The Musical, in which the opening song features the lyric "My heart's as full as a baked pa-tay-da."

tropes.name: Interruptus Musicus Continuous
tropes.html:
When Kyle's mom sparks a war between America and Canada, Cartman starts to sing, "Kyle's Mom Is a Bitch in D-Minor", much to Kyle's outrage, as he angrily shuts him up, but he sings it anyway.
Cartman: Weeeeell~!
Kyle: Don't do it, Cartman!
[Beat]
Cartman: Weeeeell~!
Kyle: I'm warning you!
Cartman: Okay, okay! [walks off-screen]
Kyle: I'm getting pretty sick of him calling my mom a—
Cartman: [slides back into frame] Weeeeell, Kyle's mom's a bitch, she's a big fat bitch, she's the biggest bitch in the whole wide world!

tropes.name: Invaded States of America
tropes.html: In the climax, the Canadian Armed Forces invade Colorado to rescue Terrance and Phillip from execution. This is after the Americans themselves already attacked Toronto and interned Canadians in "Happy Camps".

tropes.name: Irony
tropes.html:
• Cartman describes Terrance & Phillip as having "crappy animation" in order to convince himself that the movie isn't all that good after the movie theater clerk prevents the boys from seeing Asses of Fire, even though Terrance and Phillip is a live-action movie. Right after that scene, we see four crudely animated boys no other than the four main characters themselves walking down the sidewalk:
    Stan: This can't be happening.
    Kyle: We have to see this movie dude.
    Cartman: Ah, screw it. It probably isn't all that good anyway.
    Kyle: Cartman, what are you talking about?! You love Terrance & Phillip!
    Cartman: Yeah, but the animation's all crappy.
    • This also qualifies as Leaning on the Fourth Wall.
  • Cartman gets a V-chip that zaps him to prevent him from swearing. After it malfunctions, it allows him to electrocute people whenever he does swear, and uses it to overpower Saddam. Cartman saved everyone by swearing.
  • The film is about mothers uniting to push for censorship and banning works with swearing in them, but unlike the broadcasted TV episodes of South Park, all of the swearing in the movie is uncensored.

tropes.name: I Take Offense to That Last One
tropes.html: The News reporter claims that the Terrance and Phillip Movie was worse than Bryan Adams. The Canadian minister of movies was insulted for saying "The Canadian government has apologized for Bryan Adams on several occasions."

tropes.name: It's All About Me
tropes.html: Cartman is stoked that he doesn't have to pay Kenny after he dies on the operating table. Right before Kenny was sent to the hospital, Cartman bet Kenny $100 that he couldn't light his own fart on fire.

tropes.name: "I Want" Song
tropes.html:
• "Up There" for Satan, as he describes how he hates being in Hell and just wants to live on Earth. Just like most classic Disney-styled "I want" songs, it has an open interpretation.
  • The bridge in "What Would Brian Boitano Do?" serves as this for Cartman, Kyle, and Stan.
Cartman: I want this V-chip out of me. It has stunted my vocabulary.
Kyle: And I just want my mom to stop fighting everyone.
Stan: For Wendy I'll be an activist too, 'cause that's what Brian Boitano'd do!

tropes.name: I Was Told There Would Be Cake
tropes.html: The kids' lure to get people to join La Résistance. Only two kids walk out when they find out there is no punch and pie.

tropes.name: Jerkass Has a Point
tropes.html: Considering everything Sheila does throughout the movie which includes executing Terrance and Phillip, Cartman singing "Kyle's Mom is a Big, Fat Bitch" was warranted no matter what protests Kyle may have.

tropes.name: Joke and Receive
tropes.html: When the boys stumble upon a German Scheisse video, Stan jokingly asks if the woman in the video is Cartman's mom. Kyle looks closer on the screen and realizes it actually is Cartman's mom!

tropes.name: Killed Off for Real
tropes.html: Subverted in that everyone who is killed in the war, including Ze Mole, Mr. Garrison, Terrance, and Phillip, comes back to life thanks to the Reset Button. This also includes Bill Gates, who was shot in the head by the General, and appears in a later episode still with a hole in his forehead!

tropes.name: Kneel Before Zod
tropes.html: After Armaggeddon begins, Saddam Hussein demands that everyone, Americans and Canadians, all bow down before him.

tropes.name: Knight Templar Parent
tropes.html: Mothers Against Canada, and Sheila Broflovski in particular, who eventually starts a war over a dirty movie.

tropes.name: Lampshade Hanging
tropes.html: "Why did our mothers start this war, what the fuck are they fighting for? When did this song become a marathon?"

tropes.name: Land of Tulips and Windmills
tropes.html: During Cartman's performance of "Kyle's Mom is a Bitch", there's a segment where he and the other South Park elementary boys are depicted as people from around the world. The Dutch (singing gibberish like the other nationalities depicted) are shown in traditional clothing with windmills in the background.

tropes.name: La Résistance
tropes.html: The Trope Namer. The kids start a riot against the adults, trying to execute Terrance and Phillip and prevent Saddam and Satan from taking over the earth.

tropes.name: Laughably Evil
tropes.html: Saddam. He's not really evil because he never gets violent, and is too funny to hate because of his sexual relationship with Satan being the only thing that matters to him.<!-- * LawfulStupid: Mothers Against Canada, and again, Sheila Broflovski.-->

tropes.name: Letting the Air out of the Band
tropes.html: Happens at the end of "Mountain Town". The flourish stops after the clerk at the Bijou says "No!"

tropes.name: Literal Soapbox Speech
tropes.html: While forming La Résistance, Gregory of Yardale stands on a wooden crate with the word "SOAP" on it.

tropes.name: Location Song
tropes.html: "Blame Canada", a song the citizens of "South Park" sing when caught up in a media frenzy about the country, because they made a film that upset the parents with its vulgar language. It was even nominated for an Oscar for Best Original Song.

tropes.name: Logo Joke
tropes.html: The Paramount logonote  which gained an updated appearance starting with this movie: the stars gained a thick golden border (and were now visible in the lake below the mountain), while the Paramount text slowly shined; this would precede the 2002 CGI mountainfades into an equivalent as part of the mountain backdrop of South Park. The joke was ruined for the international version though, where the 1998 Warner Bros. shield takes the place of the Paramountainnote In case you're wondering why Warner Bros. had anything to do with this, it's because at the time Viacom and Time Warner each owned half of Comedy Central - it was formed in 1991 by a merger of MTV Networks' HA! TV Comedy Network, and HBO's Comedy Channel; Time Warner sold their stake in 2003. This split was also reflected by earlier South Park VHS tapes and DVDs- the first video tapes went under Time Warner's Rhino Home Video label (a part of Rhino Records and spunoff with the rest of the Warner Music Group in 2004), while the DVDs were initially released by Warner Home Video- some re-issues still credit WHV and Paramount both. In a sense of irony, Warner Home Video struck a deal with Paramount to distribute Paramount movies on Blu-ray and DVD, giving them the domestic home video rights in the mid-2010s. However, WB continues to distribute this movie internationally.

tropes.name: Mama Bear
tropes.html: Sheila takes this trope way too far. She goes as far as to launch a full-scale attack against the Canadians and kill Terrance and Phillip just to prevent Kyle from swearing.

tropes.name: Massive Multiplayer Ensemble Number
tropes.html: Tying with this, Reprise Medley and The Song Before the Storm, "La Resistance" proves to be a Crowning Music triple-threat.

tropes.name: Megaphone Gag
tropes.html:
Mr. Garrison: How would you like to go see the school counselor?
Cartman: How would you like to suck my balls?
(everyone gasps)
Mr. Garrison: WHAT DID YOU JUST SAY?!
Cartman: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm sorry. Actually, what I said was... [produces a megaphone] HOW WOULD YOU LIKE TO SUCK MY BALLS, MR. GARRISON?

tropes.name: The Mel Brooks Number
tropes.html: "Up There" and "La Resistance".

tropes.name: Memetic Badass
tropes.html: invoked In-universe: The boys mention that Brian Boitano did three salchows and a triple lutz blindfolded, can breathe fire, fought the Evil Robot King, built the Pyramids, and killed Kublai Khan.

tropes.name: Meta Fiction
tropes.html: Terrance and Phillip in the movie function as a satire of South Park itself and its controversial nature. Asses of Fire acts as a satire of the movie it takes place in.

tropes.name: Moose and Maple Syrup
tropes.html: The entire film is about parents trying to exterminate Canada because of Terrance and Phillip influencing their children to use vulgar language. Many of the Canadian stereotypes are portrayed throughout.

tropes.name: Most Definitely Not a Musical
tropes.html: The trailers focus on the comedic elements of the movie while heavily downplaying the fact that it’s a musical.

tropes.name: The Musical
tropes.html: This movie parodies Disney Animated Canon musicals (which were pretty big at the time), right down to the (tongue-in-cheek) Award-Bait Song during the credits. It even recycles "Kyle's Mom's a Bitch" from a Musical Episode of the series proper. In fact, it was a minor cliché at the time for (mostly) non-musical cartoons such as Animaniacs to get musical movies, although South Park is probably the only one that's an adult cartoon.

tropes.name: Musicalis Interruptus
tropes.html: The "Kyle's Mom is a Big, Fat Bitch" song comes to an awkward, grinding halt when the kids, followed by Cartman, realize in horror that Sheila is glaring right down at Cartman in silent, slowly building rage.

tropes.name: My God, What Have I Done?
tropes.html:
• Conan O'Brien, after tricking Terrance and Phillip onto his show so that they could get arrested, instantly regrets what he did to his two friends when they call him out on his betrayal, and ends up jumping out his studio window to his death.
  • Sharon Marsh and the other members of Mothers Against Canada (save Sheila) have this reaction when they see the scale of the carnage between America and Canada.
    Sharon: My God, this is terrible!
    Sheila: This is what we wanted! We wanted our children to be brought up in a smut-free environment!
    Sharon: But we didn't want this! (Sharon and the other M.A.C. members leave)
    Sheila: Where are you going?!
    Sharon: We're going to find our boys! For God's sake, Sheila, we're gonna get them killed!
  • Sheila when she finally does a Heel–Face Turn... after triggering Armageddon by shooting Terrance and Phillip. As Satan calls her out for her immoral action on killing them and dooms everyone by having to spend two million years of darkness, Sheila hangs her head in shame very briefly as she realizes she is the one to blame for causing the end of the world.
    Satan: You have spilled the blood of the innocent. Now begins two million years of darkness!
    Chef: Oh, good job, Mrs. Broflowski. Thanks a lot!
    Sheila: I was just trying to make the world a better place for children!
    Saddam: Yeah, and you brought enough intolerance into the world to allow my coming!
  • The General says this when Saddam forces the American and Canadian soldiers to bow down before him.

tropes.name: Mythology Gag
tropes.html: "What Would Brian Boitano Do?" is a callback to the "Jesus vs. Santa" (see Call-Back above) short done as a video Christmas card prior to the start of the series that featured Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny. This includes Brian Dennehy saying "Bye-ee!" in the same way Boitano did in the original short.

tropes.name: A Nazi by Any Other Name
tropes.html: The Mothers Against Canada. An early draft of the script even has it made explicitly clear that the "Happy Camps" are purely Sheila Broflovski's idea. Ironically, Sheila is Jewish.

tropes.name: Never Going Back to Prison
tropes.html: Ze Mole isn't getting grounded again. Not for you, not for anyone! He's mauled by guard dogs and dies from blood loss.

tropes.name: Never My Fault
tropes.html: Mothers Against Canada immediately blame Canada partly because they want someone to blame before anyone thinks about blaming them for not being proper parents.

tropes.name: NOT!
tropes.html:
Happens during Cartman and Saddam's showdown.
Saddam: Hey, buddy! I know I was mean before, but don't worry, I can change.
Cartman: Okay... NOT!

tropes.name: Not Blood, Not Family
tropes.html: When Sheila tells her son Kyle to bring his brother Ike with him, Kyle replies, "But he's not really my brother; he's adopted!".

tropes.name: Offscreen Teleportation
tropes.html: After announcing herself as President Clinton's new "Secretary of Offense", Sheila makes it from D.C. back to Colorado (a three-hour flight) in time to catch Cartman singing about her during recess.

tropes.name: Oh, Crap!
tropes.html:
• Cartman has an R-rated version of this reaction when he sees Sheila right behind him after singing "Kyle's Mom is a Bitch".
Cartman: ...oh, fuck.
  • Cartman has a pretty effective silent one when he's instructed to say "horsefucker" with the V-chip on him.
  • Sheila has one herself when Satan reveals that Terrance and Philip were innocent all along, and her hatred against them and murdering them allow him to cause The End of the World as We Know It. Chef rubbing salt in the wound with his Sarcasm Mode doesn't help and makes her feel worse.

tropes.name: Once More, with Volume!
tropes.html:
Where the show would normally use a Lame Rhyme Dodge, the movie has Cartman repeat his "How would you like to suck my balls?" retort with the aid of a megaphone after Mr. Garrison threatens him with going to the principal's office.
Mr. Garrison: How would you like to go to the principal's office?!
Cartman: How would you like to suck my balls?
Mr. Garrison: WHAT DID YOU JUST SAY?!
Cartman: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm sorry. Actually, what I said was... [produces a megaphone] HOW WOULD YOU LIKE TO SUCK MY BALLS, MR. GARRISON?

tropes.name: One-Shot Character
tropes.html: Gregory, Dr. Vosknocker and Ze Mole are only used for the movie. The latter does make a very brief cameo in "Two Guys Naked in a Hot Tub" while Stan is flipping through channels, but that was it.

tropes.name: Operation: [Blank]
tropes.html: Parodied with Operation: Human Shield and Operation: Get Behind The Darkies.

tropes.name: Paper-Thin Disguise
tropes.html:
The Executioner pulling the switch is labeled as "Anonymous", and has the traditional hood over his head, but he also somehow has a hood over his puppet's head, making it obvious that he's Mr. Garrison. Later, Sheila slips and calls him by his true name.
Sheila: Mr. Garrison, pull the switch!
Anonymous: Hey, I'm supposed to be anonymous!

tropes.name: Parental Hypocrisy
tropes.html: The mothers of South Park never think twice to consider the fact that it's all on them for letting their kids watch the movie in the first place. Sharon seems to recognize what movie it is when Stan shows her the tickets, in fact. They seem to have forgotten what they learned in the episode "Death" when they found out their kids were watching Terrance and Phillip in the first place, and the movie is canon to the series.note Proven in the episode "Do the Handicapped Go to Hell?" in which Saddam returns and Satan acknowledges his attempt to kill him.

tropes.name: Patter Song
tropes.html: "Kyle's Mom is a Bitch" is fast-paced and uses "bitch" constantly to mesh with the instrumental.

tropes.name: The Pearly Gates
tropes.html: When he dies early in the film, Kenny finds himself ascending to Heaven, where he's greeted by the Pearly Gates as well as a pair of beautiful naked women... right before he's sent plummeting to Hell for having skipped church that day.

tropes.name: Period Shaming
tropes.html: Played for Laughs. When the students ask Mr. Garrison why their mothers have arrested comedians Terrance and Philip, Garrison dismissively states their mothers are "just upset" because they're "probably all on their periods or something". When Gregory and Wendy point out the sexism of this statement, Garrison replies "Well, I'm sorry Wendy, but I just don't trust anything that bleeds for five days and doesn't die."

tropes.name: Politically Incorrect Hero
tropes.html:
• Ze Mole, who despises God with a passion and isn't afraid to let Him know it.
  • And of course there's Cartman, who rags on Kyle for being a Jew, advocates standing up to Kyle's mom in a way that comes across as misogynistic, and he wears blackface during a musical number.

tropes.name: Politically Incorrect Villain
tropes.html: Kyle's mom is this when it comes to Canadians — despite the fact that her own adopted son is Canadian.

tropes.name: Precision F-Strike
tropes.html: Wendy never says any profanity at allnote She is shown singing along with the rest of the kids in "It's Easy, M'Kay", but her lips are never shown mouthing the words, as she (and Gregory, for that matter) has her head cut off by another student in front of her. until the ending, where she says, "Fuck Gregory. Fuck him right in the ear!" This is truer in the eighth draft in which she has much more dialogue, none of which feature any curse words at all.

tropes.name: Rage Against the Heavens
tropes.html: Ze Mole does this constantly, as he has a propensity to badmouth God.

tropes.name: "The Reason You Suck" Speech
tropes.html: Kyle gives one to his mom, calling her a good-for-nothing bitch who's never around for him and instead goes off fighting against things she shouldn't be fighting against.

tropes.name: Reduced to Ratburgers
tropes.html: Kyle hid Ike in the attic to protect him, but forgot to leave him any food. Ike after not having eaten for a while finds a mouse and eats it up.

tropes.name: Reestablishing Character Moment
tropes.html:
The film reintroduces everyone for newcomers.
  • "Mountain Town" shows Stan as a carefree all-American lad, Kenny as dirt-poor and unintelligible, Kyle as a Big Brother Bully that's cowed by his mother and Cartman as a spoiled brat.
  • Sheila is reestablished as overbearing and looking for something to be outraged over.
  • Terrence and Phillip are incredibly low-brow entertainers whose brand of comedy is just farts and swearwords, only now they also sing.
  • Wendy is an idealized love interest that's just outside of Stan's reach.
  • Saddam Hussein is a Card-Carrying Villain whose motives are purely For the Evulz.

tropes.name: Refuge in Audacity
tropes.html: This film could easily be called The Movie. One key instance being in the medley when Gregory starts singing about genital mutilation, which is drowned out by the dads' singing.

tropes.name: Rerouted from Heaven
tropes.html: Kenny floats towards the gates of Heaven while a voice sings about his troubles being behind him...only for a large "ACCESS DENIED" sign to appear and send him tumbling down to Hell.

tropes.name: Reset Button
tropes.html: After Kenny inspires Satan to kill Saddam Hussein (who he was getting sick of), Satan grants him a wish, which he uses to get everything back the way it was before the war. See "Deus ex Machina".

tropes.name: The Reveal
tropes.html: At the end, Kenny's face and unmuffled voice are revealed for the first time.

tropes.name: Right Behind Me
tropes.html: Kyle's mom is standing right behind Cartman while he's singing "The Villain Sucks" Song, which leads to him having the V-chip implanted in his head.

tropes.name: Romantic False Lead
tropes.html: Gregory - there are constant hints that Wendy Testaburger is falling for him and his activist ways until the denouement.

tropes.name: Ruder and Cruder
tropes.html: More so than the series it's based on; It was originally going to be rated NC-17 because of its language — although through sheer attrition was it able to be dialed down to an R rating.

tropes.name: Running Gag
tropes.html: As in the series itself, Stan vomits every time Wendy speaks to him or whenever he sees her.

tropes.name: Say My Name
tropes.html: Phillip when Sheila shoots Terrance.

tropes.name: Screaming at Squick
tropes.html:
The first result of searching the word "clitoris" is a Scheisse porn video featuring Cartman's mom, with the most obvious disgusted reactions from the boys.
Stan: Dude, what the fuck is wrong with German people?!

tropes.name: Screen-to-Stage Adaptation
tropes.html: Well, with all the Broadway-style singing and dancing, do you think people wouldn't try this? There have been two unofficial stage musical adaptations of Bigger, Longer & Uncut: one by the Berklee College of Music with only the musical numbers, and a "24-Hour Musical" version by University College Dublin.

tropes.name: Screw the Rules, I'm Doing What's Right!
tropes.html: Stan, Kyle, and Cartman break all of the rules they normally wouldn't along with the rest of the kids in La Resistance in order to stop their parents and fix their mistakes.

tropes.name: Screw This, I'm Outta Here
tropes.html:
When the General of the American forces reveals that their big battle plan is to place all Black people in front and use them as Human Shields, Chef has his men drop to the ground at the appropriate point—which lets Canada eviscerate a good chunk of America's armed forces right off the bat.
Chef: "Operation: Human Shield" my ass!

tropes.name: Self-Deprecation
tropes.html: Cartman criticizes Terrance & Phillip's poor animation to convince himself that the movie will suck after the theater clerk prevents the boys from sneaking in, all while he and the boys do the show's famous "bobbing walk".

tropes.name: Series Fauxnale
tropes.html: The ending plays out very much like a series finale, with every single character who'd appeared in the series up to that point making cameos in the final scenes (and also being featured on the poster). It was also originally intended to be the last hurrah, but its unexpected success made sure that didn't happen. In other words, the success of this movie is the reason South Park is still going strong decades later!

tropes.name: Setting Introduction Song
tropes.html: The opening musical number "Mountain Town" describes the whitebread Colorado town in which the boys live. Reprised at the end of the movie by the whole town.

tropes.name: Shock and Awe
tropes.html: A malfunction in Cartman's V-Chip during the final battle allows him to shoot electricity from his body when he swears—the more profane, the more powerful.

tropes.name: Shout-Out
tropes.html: See the South Park Shout Out page for the movie.

tropes.name: Silly Reason for War
tropes.html: See Disproportionate Retribution above; only in the South Park universe is war declared over a movie.

tropes.name: Sir Swears-a-Lot
tropes.html:
• All four boys (Stan less than the others) become this after seeing Asses of Fire.
  • Terrance and Phillip cuss a lot more (and a lot harsher) in The Movie than they normally do in the show.
  • This is taken further when Cartman's V-Chip malfunctions.

tropes.name: Skewed Priorities
tropes.html:
• After the boys see the movie again and Kenny dies as a result, Sheila, Sharon and Liane are more upset about the former.
  • After Kenny sets himself on fire, Cartman tries extinguishing the flames by hitting Kenny with a stick. Eventually Cartman is more focused on the stick being on fire than he is on Kenny burning to death.
  • From what we see, most of the American military's planning for the war with Canada seems to revolve around the big USO Show where Terrance and Philip will be executed. This comes back to bite them when it becomes clear that Canada, conversely, has been preparing for an actual invasion of the United States.
  • Through most of the movie, Stan is more interested in "finding the clitoris" (even though he has no idea what that actually means) than in stopping the war and preventing The End of the World as We Know It.
  • While trying to avoid being caught in American-Canadian crossfire near the end, Terrance and Phillip still find time to laugh at each other's farts.

tropes.name: Small Role, Big Impact
tropes.html:
• The Hobo who takes the boys into the theater only appears at the beginning, but he accidentally kickstarts the entire film's story off.
  • The song "Kyle's Mom's a Bitch" - at first it just seems like Cartman blowing off steam at Sheila, but it results in him getting V-chipped and later enabling him to save the world by using the V-chip as a weapon against Saddam Hussein.

tropes.name: Spoof Aesop
tropes.html:
The ending of the Movie Within a Movie:
Terrance: Well, Phillip, I hope you learned something from this whole experience.
Phillip: I did, Terrance. I learned that you are a boner biting dick fart fuck face!

tropes.name: The Starscream
tropes.html: Saddam Hussein when he declares himself ruler of the world and tries to have everyone killed, completely betraying Satan in doing so.

tropes.name: The Stinger
tropes.html: Ike eats a rat in the attic. His family forgot to tell him the war is over.

tropes.name: Stunned Silence
tropes.html: What Mr. Garrison is reduced to when Cartman breaks out the megaphone.

tropes.name: Subverted Rhyme Every Occasion
tropes.html:
During What Would Brian Boitano Do?, Cartman sings a lyric that would naturally rhyme with "anyone" but we instead get the following exchange:
Cartman: And when Brian Boitano built the pyramids
He beat up Kublai Khan
Stan and Kyle: 'Cause Brian Boitano doesn't take shit from an-y-bod-y!

tropes.name: Suddenly Shouting
tropes.html:
Sheila, when Kyle doesn't want to bring Ike along to the movies:
Sheila: DO AS I SAY, KYLE!
Kyle: Okay, okay, I'm sorry.

tropes.name: Suicide as Comedy
tropes.html: Conan O'Brien's jumper suicide is played for laughs, especially when he crashes into and destroys a car parked on the street below, and the owner walks up to turn off the car alarm.

tropes.name: Suspiciously Similar Substitute
tropes.html: Ze Mole is basically a more resourceful Kenny. He's rougher than the other kids and swears a lot even for this movie. And of course, he dies.

tropes.name: Sympathy for the Devil
tropes.html: Literally! While in Hell, Kenny notices how Satan is driven to tears by his frequent arguments with Saddam and offers to comfort him, even encouraging the Devil to just break up with the former dictator already. Even the people of South Park feel sympathy for him when they see how lonely he is and invite him to come back to the surface at anytime.

tropes.name: Take That!
tropes.html:
• The first one in the film is about the fictional death of Saddam Hussein (who died seven years after the film's release), with a news anchor on TV bluntly stating that "the world is still glad to be rid of him."
  • When Kenny demands to go see the Terrance and Phillip film rather than go to church, Carol tells him that when he dies, he's going to Hell to see Satan. Kenny doesn't care.
  • An African-American soldier asks "Is the people gonna die?" in a voice that sounds a lot like Jar Jar Binks, a jab at the character's alleged racist implications.
  • And of course, the entire film is essentially one of the most vicious Take Thats ever made against Moral Guardians, the MPAA, censorship and scapegoat parenting.
  • It's hard not to pick up on a certain amount of frustration with Windows 98 in the scene where Bill Gates is summoned by the General, yelled at for not making Windows 98 fast enough, and then summarily shot in the head.
  • Cartman's V-chip-powered, swear-fueled rant against Saddam is capped off with "Barbra Streisand". Who knew that was the foulest word in the English language?
  • Played more for laughs, but "Blame Canada" calls Anne Murray a bitch, which the real Anne Murray was amused by (she was even invited to sing the song at the Oscars, but had to decline due to previous commitments).
  • During the news debate:
Newsreader: This movie isn't the first troublesome thing to come out of Canada. Let us not forget Bryan Adams.
Canadian Minister: Now, now. The Canadian government has apologised for Bryan Adams on several occasions.

tropes.name: Talk Show Appearance
tropes.html: Terrance and Phillip appear on Conan O'Brien's show where it's a trap set up by Shelia and the Mothers Against Canada group where they arrest the duo. After the duo call out Conan for his betrayal, he has a My God, What Have I Done? moment before he jumps out of the window and lands on top of a car.

tropes.name: Tempting Fate
tropes.html:
After the Baldwin family's home gets bombed by the Canadian Air Force, all of them are dead except for a single survivor. He triumphantly boasts "Ha ha! You missed me!" right before the last plane drops a bomb on his head as well.
  • After watching the subsequent news report on the incident, and Terrance and Phillip due to be executed, Stan wonders how things could get any worse. In the next scene, Satan is introduced.

tropes.name: They Killed Kenny Again
tropes.html: Kenny's death in this movie comes from trying to light one of his farts on fire, leading to being set on fire. This and a Plethora of Mistakes by the medical staff leads to his death — and because of how South Park's afterlife works, Kenny goes to Hell.

tropes.name: Too Much Information
tropes.html:
• Sheila and Sharon's reaction after Liane says what a rimjob is.
  • When Gregory starts going into details about just what will happen if La Résistance is captured in song form, Stan, Kyle, and Cartman all silently look on with horrified faces.

tropes.name: Trailers Always Spoil
tropes.html: Most of the trailers completely spoil Kenny taking off his hood. While his face is kept hidden, his hair is still revealed in said trailers.

tropes.name: Triumphant Reprise
tropes.html:
The reprise of "Mountain Town" at the end.
Chef: Everything worked out, what a happy end…
Americans and Canadians are friends again…
So let’s all join hands and knock oppression doooown…
Soldiers: Good Lordy, I’m found!

tropes.name: Troll
tropes.html: The afterlife itself. When Kenny dies (again), he gets to see heaven... for a total of ten seconds before being plummeted into hell.

tropes.name: Truck Driver's Gear Change
tropes.html: “Kyle’s Mom’s a Bitch” does this four times, moving from C major to E major one semitone at a time in less than 90 seconds.

tropes.name: Tunnel King
tropes.html: "Ze Mole" digs his way to the USO show stage to free Terrance and Phillip, but the boys forget to turn off the alarm on time and he's mauled to death by guard dogs.

tropes.name: Turn the Other Cheek
tropes.html: Even after causing World War III over a show, set up death camps, and nearly causing the end of the world after gunning down Terrance and Phillip (even when Kyle reasoned with her), Sheila was pretty much forgiven for causing the whole mess. Justified that Kenny wished Satan to bring back everything to normal.

tropes.name: Unfortunate Search Results
tropes.html: Chef, forgetting that he's talking to an 8-year old, tells Stan that finding the clitoris is the key to making a girl like him, but Stan has no other information about what the clitoris is. At one point, he tries turning to the Internet with Kyle and Cartman. Of course, they get lots of pornographic hits; the one they click on is a German fetish video featuring Cartman's mom.

tropes.name: Unishment
tropes.html: Mr. Mackey announces a ban on Terrance and Phillip apparel in school, adding that anyone wearing such clothing will be sent home immediately. Every kid, save for Wendy and Gregory, cheers and runs out.

tropes.name: Unusual Euphemism
tropes.html: Barbra Streisand, one of the many profanities said by Cartman while his V-Chip was malfunctioning.

tropes.name: The Usurper
tropes.html:
When Armageddon is brought upon by Sheila when she kills Terrance and Phillip, Saddam takes the opportunity to command all the soldiers in the American and Canadian armies to bow down to him, and even takes orders to make a huge statue of him. Satan does not tolerate with this very well.
Satan: Saddam, I'm the dark ruler, not you.

tropes.name: Villainous Breakdown
tropes.html: Sheila shooting and killing Terrance and Phillip. She soon realizes her actions once Satan and Saddam emerge and wreak havoc.

tropes.name: Villainous Lament
tropes.html: In the musical number "Up There", quite possibly the only serious number in the movie, Satan expresses his sorrow due to never being able to live back on Earth and be a normal member of society.

tropes.name: Villain Song
tropes.html: Three of the villains get their own songs: Saddam sings "I Can Change", Satan performs "Up There", and Mothers Against Canada perform "Blame Canada".

tropes.name: "The Villain Sucks" Song
tropes.html: "Kyle's Mom is a Bitch," originally from the series' first Christmas special. Thanks, Cartman.

tropes.name: Villain with Good Publicity
tropes.html: Sheila is sided with by the rest of the South Park adults in their striving to stop their kids from swearing and obviously isn't Hated by All, since she was a normal character before the movie.

tropes.name: Walking Out on the Show
tropes.html: The entire Asses of Fire audience—except our heroes, of course—leave the theater in disgust during the "Uncle Fucker" song.

tropes.name: War Is Hell
tropes.html:
Most of the Mothers Against Canada are horrified when seeing the actual Canadian-American battlefield, especially since their sons are wandering around in it. But of course, being South Park, it also manages to play this trope for laughs. In song.
"They may cut your dick in half, and feed it to a pig,
And though it hurts you'll laugh, and dance a dickless jig!
For that's the way it goes, in war you're shat upon..."
  • Keep in mind, considering Team America: World Police and a few other South Park episodes on the subject, the creators aren’t anti-war, per se, but they are anti-this war.

tropes.name: We Hardly Knew Ye
tropes.html: Ze Mole. He only has 15 minutes of screentime, and ultimately gets killed by the guard dogs.

tropes.name: We Have Reserves
tropes.html: In the invasion plans of Canada, Black people are put into units best described as "Operation: Human Shield".

tropes.name: Well-Intentioned Extremist
tropes.html: Sheila may go to unreasonably far lengths to enforce the morality and safety of the town's children by launching a war against Canadians, but it was really for a good cause.

tropes.name: What Do You Mean, It's Not for Kids?
tropes.html: The Terrance and Phillip movie is an In-Universe example. The boys sneak into a screening of the film not once, but twice - the second time around, there's nothing but kids in the audience. The content, of course, is anything but kid-friendly.

tropes.name: When You Coming Home, Dad?
tropes.html: Kyle just wants his mom to stop fighting and actually be a mom to him.

tropes.name: Would Be Rude to Say "Genocide"
tropes.html: "All Canadian-Americans are to report to one of these death camps right away. Did I say death camps? I meant happy camps!"

tropes.name: Yank the Dog's Chain
tropes.html: After getting killed yet again, Kenny thinks he's going to heaven. He's wrong.

tropes.name: You Are Grounded!
tropes.html: Happens to Stan, Kyle and Cartman after Kenny's death.

tropes.name: You Have Failed Me
tropes.html: When the Army's holo-projector fails, which runs on Windows 98, the General orders his men to bring in Bill Gates and shoots him in front of everyone.

tropes.name: Your Approval Fills Me with Shame
tropes.html: Although it's never said outright, Satan and Saddam Hussein all but tell Sheila to her face that she's responsible for the end of the world. She did not take their compliment well, as she hangs her head in shame upon realizing she has doomed the whole world.

tropes.name: Acoustic License
tropes.html: Bodhi and Johnny Utah have a conversation in freefall.

tropes.name: Actor Allusion
tropes.html:
• Johnny reports to Angelo on Bodhi's movements that day. He comments on how he ate lunch at Patrick's Roadhouse, which is an actual restaurant in LA. It might also be construed as a reference to Patrick Swayze's movie Road House (1989).
  • Gary Busey previously played a LA-based federal agent in Predator 2 the year prior.
  • Tom Sizemore would go on to play a Los Angeles police officer in True Romance two years later.

tropes.name: Affably Evil
tropes.html: Bodhi in spades.

tropes.name: Agony of the Feet
tropes.html: One of the drug-dealing surfers literally shoots himself in the foot when an FBI agent slams a door on him.

tropes.name: Alas, Poor Villain
tropes.html: Make no mistake, Bohdi, charming and likable though he may be, is a villain. His selfishness and recklessness get innocent people and his crew killed, and his remorse only goes so far. Nevertheless, Bohdi's being reduced to begging Johnny to let him go out on a lethal wave rather than being taken into custody is quite sad. The 50-Year Storm is all Bohdi has left to live for, and he's not wrong that he would suffer locked away. His subsequent death is both magnificent and pitiful.

tropes.name: Always Save the Girl
tropes.html: Invoked. Bodhi secures Johnny's help in making his getaway by showing him footage of his girlfriend in the custody of a Psycho for Hire.

tropes.name: Anti-Villain
tropes.html: Bodhi. He's charming, likable, and can be a genuinely good friend. He's genuinely taken aback by violence and has no time for the local Nazi assholes. He's also selfish and self-centered in the extreme. He doesn't let his genuine fondness for Johnny and Tyler stop him from blackmailing Johnny with Tyler's safety. Above all else, Bodhi refuses to accept a loss. He'll double down on a plan that's gone back and then double down again rather than admit he's failed. This leads directly to the violent demise of his crew. While Bodhi expresses remorse, it isn't enough to stop him.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Geography
tropes.html:
A wave headed towards Bells Beach, Victoria from Antarctica would have to swamp Tasmania in order to maintain its trajectory.
  • Arguably justified in that while Bodie is aware of the 50 year storm, he's not any kind of meteorologist and may simply not really understand its mechanics. His description may simply be wrong.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Law Enforcement
tropes.html:
• Johnny and Pappas' boss ignores their very logical conclusions based on what little evidence they have (considering they have nowhere else to look, why not look there?). Not only that, most directors in his position would be overjoyed to have agents who not only keep up their normal caseload, but work another case on their own time. The biggest offender, however, is Johnny using his real name while going "undercover" on the beach. This would be dumb enough under normal circumstances, but Johnny is a former college football star who blew out his knee in a big game, and he was well-known enough that years later people still remember him. Even in the pre-internet era, all it would take is one big college football fan in the group following his life after the injury to know that the famous Johnny Utah became an FBI agent after he couldn't play any more, and the whole operation is blown.
  • At the bank robbery that Utah and Pappas stake out, Johnny starts firing his gun at the fleeing vehicle, and hasn't even been fired on by them first. Using deadly force against a fleeing felon had been illegal since 1985.
  • Near the end of the movie, Pappas knocks his boss out cold with a punch after hearing one too many insults from him, and is just allowed to walk away afterwards. Needless to say, this would result in an immediate suspension from duty in real life.
  • The finale sees Johnny confronting and attempting to arrest Bodhi at Bells Beach, Victoria, Australia, with local law enforcement arriving to provide backup. However, FBI agents generally lack the authorization to make arrests abroad. It's also heavily implied that his investigation is not an officially sanctioned one, so he wouldn't be allowed to participate in (let alone lead) such an operation as a civilian.

tropes.name: Artistic License – Physics
tropes.html: The first skydiving scene features an extended free fall that could never occur from any altitude where the divers wouldn't need an oxygen tank.

tropes.name: Badass Bystander
tropes.html: The off-duty cop who opens fire on the Ex-Presidents during the final heist is an interesting deconstructed example of this trope. While his intentions are noble, he vastly overestimates his own capabilities when he decides to take on four heavily armed professional bank robbers (plus Johnny) with only a handgun. Not only that, but he drags a reluctant security guard into his plan, despite the guard wisely warning him against doing anything reckless. The result is a messy shootout that endangers the lives of the other hostages and leaves three people (the cop, the guard and Grommet, one of the Ex-Presidents) dead.

tropes.name: Bait-and-Switch
tropes.html: The scene where Bodhi tells his gang he knows what to do about Johnny since finding out he's an FBI agent. The very scene is Johnny asleep with a gun aimed at him, implying Bodhi was going to kill him. It turned out to be Tyler also finding out he's FBI.

tropes.name: Battle in the Rain
tropes.html: The final fight between Johnny and Bodhi.

tropes.name: Becoming the Mask
tropes.html: Johnny Utah pretends to be an extreme sports enthusiast to try and find out who the Ex-Presidents are, but after learning how to surf and skydive he really does come to love extreme sports. During the epilogue, Johnny admits to Bodhi that he still surfs every day.

tropes.name: BFG
tropes.html: Bodhi's Freedom Arms Model 83 revolver, chambered in .454 Casull (a cartridge with almost TWICE the muzzle energy of a .44 Magnum).

tropes.name: Big "NO!"
tropes.html:
Shouted by Johnny Utah when he sees Pappas being shot in the back with a shotgun.
  • Also Bodhi when Johnny has him handcuffed on the beach at the end and realizes he can't make an easy escape.

tropes.name: Bolivian Army Ending
tropes.html: Bodhi goes off to surf the "50 Year Storm", with his death all but guaranteed, and even if he does somehow manage to survive, the cops are waiting for him at the beach. The film shows Bodhi falling off his board and being swallowed by a monster wave, but never explicitly confirms his ultimate fate.

tropes.name: Boom, Headshot!
tropes.html: Pappas shoots one of the meth dealers in the head during the raid.

tropes.name: Bulletproof Vest
tropes.html: The Ex-Presidents wear them while robbing the banks. One saves Johnny's life when he takes two bullets to the chest, though he is still knocked off his feet and is shown in pain and gasping for air on the floor afterwards.

tropes.name: Byronic Hero
tropes.html: Both Johnny and Bodhi.

tropes.name: Chekhov's Gun
tropes.html: Johnny's knee injury. In an action movie, a character who was a former athlete until an injury derailed his career is nothing unusual. Nor here, as there's nothing seen that shows his leg ever affecting him... until he jumps down a concrete flood break and pops it badly, causing him to to lose Bodhi during their chase.

tropes.name: Commonality Connection
tropes.html: Exploited by Johnny who invents a tragic backstory about his parents dying in a car accident to bond with Tyler.

tropes.name: Da Chief
tropes.html: Supervising Agent Ben Harp, played by a delightfully hammy John C McGinley. Every single scene he has with Utah and Pappas has him screaming at them for their supposed inefficiency even when Utah points out in a scene right after one chewing out that they are handing in their case quota and the surfing he's been doing with Bodhi's gang to infiltrate them has been done (up to that point) on his own free time, and Pappas pointing out at the moment of that specific chewing out that undercover operations are a thing that takes time. It becomes clear that he hates them just because he hates them even before shit really starts going bad for the two agents.

tropes.name: Chute Sabotage
tropes.html: Lampshaded as Johnny becomes suspicious, and the surfers swap their rigs with each other while in the jump plane.

tropes.name: Cluster F-Bomb
tropes.html: We get some from Da Chief Harp, and the DEA agent whose investigation the FBI raid on the Surf Nazis ruins.

tropes.name: The Comically Serious
tropes.html: Meta-example. Part of the film's charm is that it plays such a ridiculous premise straight without a sense of irony or self-awareness.

tropes.name: Control Freak
tropes.html: Keanu Reeves described Johnny as a "total control freak, and the ocean beats him up and challenges him. After a while, everything becomes a game. He becomes as amoral as any criminal. He loses the difference between right and wrong."

tropes.name: Cross-Operational Interference
tropes.html: Johnny suspects a crew of territorial surf punks to be the bank heist crew known as the Ex-Presidents, and the FBI execute a raid on their house which results in a gunfight leaving most of the gang dead. They are then yelled at by a DEA agent who's been deep cover with them investigating their drug dealing operation, with the deadly raid cutting off the ability to trace their suppliers.

tropes.name: Dark Action Girl
tropes.html: The girl in the shower at the drug dealer house who first kicks the shit out of Johnny and then repeatedly stabs a FBI agent before finally taken down, all while being naked.

tropes.name: Deadpan Snarker
tropes.html:
Johnny proves himself quite adept at this.
Harp: "I guess we must just have ourselves an asshole shortage, huh?" [winks sarcastically and walks away]
Johnny: "Not so far."

tropes.name: Defiant to the End
tropes.html: Roach.

tropes.name: Description Cut
tropes.html: When Johnny expresses skepticism about being able to go undercover as a surfer, Angelo points out how he's an athlete and asks, "How hard could it be?" Cue the next scene where Johnny wipes out, and has to be rescued by Tyler.

tropes.name: Determinator
tropes.html: Johnny, who manages to successfully track Bodhi's whereabouts after his escape, chasing him through Mexico, South America, Sumatra, Fiji and finally Australia. Hell, the fact that he follows Bodhi out the door of a skydive plane, and without a parachute of his own, marks him as this.

tropes.name: Disc-One Final Boss
tropes.html: The drug-dealing surfer thugs whom Utah initially suspects of being the Ex-Presidents.

tropes.name: Donut Mess with a Cop
tropes.html: In the scene where Utah arrives at his new posting, he pinches a donut in passing out of a box on one of his new colleague's desks.

tropes.name: Down L.A. Drain
tropes.html: Utah chases one of the "Ex-President" bank robbers on foot, ending with him injuring his knee after jumping into the viaduct and his quarry getting away.

tropes.name: Even Evil Has Standards
tropes.html:
• Bodhi only had Rosie threatening Tyler because he deep down couldn’t possibly do it himself. He’s just as uncomfortable about the whole thing as Johnny and once is poised to escape, keeps his word and demands her freedom.
  • Bodhi also has no use for Bunker and his friends, calling them "Nazi assholes" who are wired wrong and have no understanding about what it's all about.

tropes.name: Evil Cannot Comprehend Good
tropes.html: Bodhi never manages to understand why Johnny is so determined to arrest him. During the epilogue, even after Bodhi admits that "it went bad" and Johnny explicitly explains that Bodhi needs to answer for his murder and the deaths of Pappas and his gang, Bodhi doesn't understand why Johnny refuses to let him go.

tropes.name: Fake-Out Fade-Out
tropes.html: While there are no literal fade outs, the movie has several scenes that feel like they could be the ending. Angelo being shot, Utah saving Tyler, then the real ending at Bells Beach.

tropes.name: Fake Shemp
tropes.html: Patrick Swayze is not the one wearing the Reagan mask during the foot chase sequence. Instead, his stunt double, Scott Wilder, performed the scene because Swayze was in Europe doing press for Ghost (1990).

tropes.name: Famed in Story
tropes.html: Johnny Utah used to play College Football until a Game-Breaking Injury and then deciding to become an FBI agent. This proves an issue when trying to go undercover, but he's able to just go undercover as himself, just lying about his new career.

tropes.name: Fanservice
tropes.html: Uh, yeah. The film opens with Keanu Reeves soaked to the skin and wearing a tight fitting shirt while demonstrating his weapon prowess, and he has multiple shirtless scenes (one which includes a quick shot of his naked butt) throughout the rest of the film. There's also a number of scantily clad women, a woman taking a shower then kicking Johnny 's ass (without getting dressed) during a raid, plus the surfing scenes in general.

tropes.name: Firing in the Air a Lot
tropes.html: The scene where Utah empties his gun into the air instead of shooting Bodhi.

tropes.name: Flipping the Bird
tropes.html: Happens several times during the film.

tropes.name: Full-Frontal Assault
tropes.html: During the raid on the Surf Thugs' house, Johnny is attacked by a naked woman who had been taking a shower when the raid began.
